```ts
  if (last !== x) {
    const la = countAt(last);
    la.write((la.read() & NOT_EDGES) | (toU64(i) << CAND_SHIFT));
  }
  ca.write(n & NOT_SCAN_BITS);
}

/** A decrement left a count above zero (D41): a candidate, if it isn't one, forgetting another if the table is full. */
/** @tsl.inline */
// SAFETY: x is a live counted slot whose class can be in a cycle, in no scan.
function tablePush(x: u64): void {
  if (ccTable === 0n || x >= SCANNABLE) {
    ccLost = true;
    return;
  }
  if (ccTop >= TABLE) {
    const v = ptrAt(u64, ccTable).add(toUsize(ccVictim)).read();
    ccVictim = ccVictim + 1 >= TABLE ? 0 : ccVictim + 1;
    tableOff(v);
    ccLost = true;
  }
  ptrAt(u64, ccTable).add(toUsize(ccTop)).write(x);
  const ca = countAt(x);
  ca.write((ca.read() & NOT_SCAN_BITS) | ST_CAND | (toU64(ccTop) << CAND_SHIFT));
  ccTop++;
}

/** A decrement on an object whose class can be in a cycle: D39's, with the barrier and candidates (D41). */
// SAFETY: x is a live counted slot whose class can be in a cycle, and n its count word as read.
function ccDrop(x: u64, n: u64): void {
  const ca = countAt(x);
  if ((n & COUNT) > 1n) {
    ca.write(n - 1n);
    if (n >= ST_WHITE) {
      touch(x);
      ca.write(ca.read() | AGAIN);
    } else if ((n & ST_MASK) === 0n) tablePush(x);
    return;
  }
  if (n >= ST_WHITE) {
    if (ccPhase !== 3 && ccPhase !== 4 && waiting <= QLINK) {
      // in a scan that hasn't decided: given up, and on the queue like any other (R1e, 3.5)
      ca.write(WAITING | ST_GONE | (n & LINK_A) | waiting);
      waiting = x;
      ccPending++;
      ccGaveUp++;
      return;
    }
    // in a scan that has decided: it stays there, held, and goes on the queue when the scan lets it go
    ca.write(n - 1n);
    touch(x);
    return;
  }
  if ((n & ST_MASK) === ST_CAND) tableOff(x);
  ca.write(waiting | WAITING);
  waiting = x;
}

/** x joins the scan, white, with no edges found yet, at the end of its list. */
// SAFETY: x is a live counted slot below SCANNABLE, in no scan and not in the table.
function join(x: u64): void {
  const ca = countAt(x);
  ca.write((ca.read() & COUNT) | ST_WHITE);
  setNext(x, 0n);
  if (ccTail === 0n) ccHead = x;
  else setNext(ccTail, x);
  ccTail = x;
  ccSize++;
}

// SAFETY: x is a counted slot that was in the table, now off it.
function joinRoot(x: u64): void {
  join(x);
  const ca = countAt(x);
  ca.write(ca.read() | ROOT);
}

/** Visit.Scan reached y: an edge found, and y joins the scan if it isn't in it. */
// SAFETY: y is a live counted slot whose class is in the group being scanned.
function ccEdge(y: u64): void {
  const ca = countAt(y);
  let n = ca.read();
  if (n < ST_WHITE || n >= WAITING) {
    if (y >= SCANNABLE) return;
    if (ccSize >= ccLimit && !ccExh) {
      ccCut = true;
      return;
    }
    if ((n & ST_MASK) === ST_CAND) {
      tableOff(y);
      joinRoot(y);
    } else join(y);
    n = ca.read();
  }
  if ((n & EDGES) >> 32n >= EDGES_MAX) {
    if ((n & ST_MASK) === ST_WHITE) ca.write((n & NOT_ST_MASK) | ST_HELD);
    return;
  }
  ca.write(n + EDGE);
}

/** Visit.Trace reached y: if it's in the scan and white, it's held, and marking needs another pass. */
// SAFETY: y is a live counted slot whose class is in the group being scanned.
function ccTrace(y: u64): void {
  const ca = countAt(y);
  const n = ca.read();
  if ((n & ST_MASK) !== ST_WHITE) return;
  ca.write((n & NOT_ST_MASK) | ST_HELD);
  ccDirty = true;
}

/** Whether y is in the scan and white: garbage, once the scan has decided. */
// SAFETY: y is a live counted slot.
function ccWhite(y: u64): bool {
  return (countAt(y).read() & ST_MASK) === ST_WHITE;
}

/**
 * One the scan gave up, out of its list (R1e): its block given back if freeing is done with it, or left to freeing to give
 * back, with nothing of the scan's left in its prefix.
 */
// SAFETY: x was in the scan's list, given up, and the caller has read its next; n is its count word as read.
function ccLetGo(x: u64, n: u64): void {
  if ((n & ST_MASK) === ST_DONE) {
    clearScan(x);
    const owner = ownerAt(x).read();
    giveBack(x, owner, entryOf(owner >>> 8));
    return;
  }
  const g = genAt(x);
  g.write(g.read() % 0x1_0000);
  const o = ownerAt(x);
  o.write(o.read() % 0x100_0000);
  countAt(x).write((n & (WAITING | QLINK)) | ST_OUT);
}

/** Collector steps, at most b, unless it's waiting out its gap: gives how many it took. */
function ccWork(b: usize): usize {
  stepping = true;
  let used: usize = 0;
  while (used < b) {
    if (ccPhase === 0 && (ccTop === 0 || (pacing && ccGap > 0 && !ccExh))) break;
    ccStep();
    if (ccWait) {
      ccWait = false; // marking waits for freeing, which gets the rest of the budget
      break;
    }
    used++;
  }
  stepsTaken = BigInt.asUintN(64, stepsTaken + toU64(used));
  ccSteps += used;
  stepping = false;
  return used;
}

/** Steps until the scan under way is done: exhaustion's and rcCollect's, with no limit. */
function ccFinish(): void {
  let used: usize = 0;
  while (ccPhase !== 0) {
    ccStep();
    if (ccWait) {
      ccWait = false;
      stepping = false;
      runSteps(RC_BUDGET);
      stepping = true;
      continue;
    }
    used++;
  }
  stepsTaken = BigInt.asUintN(64, stepsTaken + toU64(used));
  ccSteps += used;
}

/**
 * One step: one root taken, one slot visited, one object passed in marking, or one block given back. The phases are tested
 * most frequent first, marking's, then finding's, deciding's and giving back's, as `tmk profile` counted them, and the
 * dispatch is inlined into its two callers (R1f).
 */
/** @tsl.inline */
function ccStep(): void {
  if (ccPhase === 2) ccMark();
  else if (ccPhase === 1) ccFind();
  else if (ccPhase === 3) ccDecide();
  else if (ccPhase === 4) ccGiveBack();
  else if (ccPhase === 5) ccRoots();
  else ccStart();
}

function ccStart(): void {
  ccScans++;
  ccPhase = 5;
  ccGather = ccTop;
  ccHead = 0n;
  ccTail = 0n;
  ccSize = 0;
  ccCut = false;
  ccDirty = false;
  ccFound = 0;
}

/** Phase 5: the table's candidates become the scan's roots, one a step, last first. */
// SAFETY: every slot in the table is live, with a count above zero, and its index right.
function ccRoots(): void {
  if (ccGather > 0 && ccTop > 0) {
    ccGather--;
    const x = ptrAt(u64, ccTable).add(toUsize(ccTop) - 1).read();
    tableOff(x);
    joinRoot(x);
    return;
  }
  if (ccHead === 0n) {
    ccPhase = 0;
    return;
  }
  ccLimit = toUsize(toU64(FIRST_LIMIT) << toU64(ccLevel * 2)) + ccSize;
  ccCur = ccHead;
  ccIdx = 0;
  ccPhase = 1;
}

/** Phase 1: what the roots reach, each slot one step, counting an edge for each reference found. */
// SAFETY: ccCur is in the scan, so live.
function ccFind(): void {
  // one given up is passed over: freeing drops what it holds (R1e)
  if ((countAt(ccCur).read() & ST_MASK) < ST_GONE) {
    const k = releaseCall(ccCur, ccIdx, Visit.Scan);
    if (ccIdx < k) {
      ccIdx++;
      return;
    }
  }
  ccCur = nextOf(ccCur);
  ccIdx = 0;
  if (ccCur !== 0n) return;
  ccPhase = 2;
  ccPrev = 0n;
  ccCur = ccHead;
  ccDirty = false;
}

/**
 * Phase 2: marking, in passes over the scan's list, reversing it each time. An object is held if its count isn't the
 * edges found, or a count operation touched it, or something held refers to it. A pass in which nothing new is held is
 * the decision: from that instant, what's white is garbage.
 */
// SAFETY: ccCur is in the scan, so live.
function ccMark(): void {
  const x = ccCur;
  if (x === 0n) {
    if (!ccDirty && ccPending !== 0) {
      // nothing new held, but something given up still holds references the scan counted: no decision until freeing
      // has dropped them, each a count operation on what it held (R1e, 3.5)
      ccWait = true;
      return;
    }
    ccHead = ccPrev;
    ccCur = ccPrev;
    ccPrev = 0n;
    ccIdx = 0;
    if (ccDirty) {
      ccDirty = false;
      return;
    }
    ccGarbage = 0n;
    ccPhase = 3;
    return;
  }
  const ca = countAt(x);
  let n = ca.read();
  if ((n & ST_MASK) >= ST_GONE) {
    ccCur = nextOf(x);
    ccIdx = 0;
    ccLetGo(x, n);
    return;
  }
  if (ccIdx === 0 && (n & ST_MASK) === ST_WHITE && (n & COUNT) !== (n & EDGES) >> 32n) {
    n = (n & NOT_ST_MASK) | ST_HELD;
    ca.write(n);
  }
  if ((n & ST_MASK) === ST_HELD) {
    const k = releaseCall(x, ccIdx, Visit.Trace);
    if (ccIdx < k) {
      ccIdx++;
      return;
    }
    ca.write((ca.read() & NOT_ST_MASK) | ST_TRACED);
  }
  const nx = nextOf(x);
  setNext(x, ccPrev);
  ccPrev = x;
  ccCur = nx;
  ccIdx = 0;
}

/**
 * Phase 3: what's held goes back as it was, a step each (a candidate again if a decrement left it a count, back in the
 * table if it was a root of a scan that was cut off, on the queue if its count reached zero meanwhile). What's white is
 * garbage: its count is set to zero, and its slots released a step each, dropping what isn't garbage too.
 */
// SAFETY: ccCur is in the scan; a white object's slots are visited through its own release function.
function ccDecide(): void {
  const x = ccCur;
  if (x === 0n) {
    if (ccFound > 0) {
      ccCur = ccGarbage;
      ccPhase = 4;
      return;
    }
    ccPhase = 0;
    ccNextLevel();
    ccGap = toUsize(toU64(ccSize) << toU64(ccCut ? GAP_SHIFT_CUT : GAP_SHIFT));
    return;
  }
  const ca = countAt(x);
  const n = ca.read();
  if ((n & ST_MASK) >= ST_GONE) {
    ccCur = nextOf(x);
    ccIdx = 0;
    ccLetGo(x, n);
    return;
  }
  if ((n & ST_MASK) !== ST_WHITE) {
    const nx = nextOf(x);
    clearScan(x);
    if ((n & COUNT) === 0n) {
      ca.write(waiting | WAITING);
      waiting = x;
    } else if ((n & AGAIN) !== 0n || ((n & ROOT) !== 0n && ccCut)) tablePush(x);
    ccCur = nx;
    ccIdx = 0;
    return;
  }
  // releasing empties a vector as it goes, so how many slots there are is its first answer, as freeing's is
  const k0 = releaseCall(x, ccIdx, Visit.Collect);
  if (ccIdx === 0) {
    ca.write(ca.read() & NOT_COUNT);
    ccFound++;
    ccSlots = k0;
  }
  if (ccIdx < ccSlots) {
    ccIdx++;
    return;
  }
  const nx = nextOf(x);
  setNext(x, ccGarbage);
  ccGarbage = x;
  ccCur = nx;
  ccIdx = 0;
}

/** Phase 4: each garbage object's block given back, a step each. */
// SAFETY: ccCur is garbage, released in phase 3, linked only on this list; nothing holds a count on it.
function ccGiveBack(): void {
  const x = ccCur;
  if (x === 0n) {
    ccPhase = 0;
    ccNextLevel();
    ccGap = 0;
    return;
  }
  ccCur = nextOf(x);
  clearScan(x);
  const owner = ownerAt(x).read();
  giveBack(x, owner, entryOf(owner >>> 8));
  ccFreed++;
}

function ccNextLevel(): void {
  ccLevel = ccCut ? (ccLevel + 1 > MAX_LEVEL ? MAX_LEVEL : ccLevel + 1) : 0;
}

/**
 * Exhaustion's walk (D41): a scan whose roots are every live object whose class can be in a cycle, found by walking each
 * size class's chunks: the one pass over the whole counted heap there is, and only at exhaustion or in rcCollect.
 */
// SAFETY: every chunk was recorded when it was made, and every slot below its end was handed out, so each is a counted
// slot, live (an odd generation and no queue link) or not.
function ccWalk(): void {
  ccWalks++;
  ccStart();
  ccGather = 0;
  for (let k: usize = FIRST_CLASS; k < CLASSES; k++) {
    const size = toU64(1) << toU64(k);
    let c = ptrAt(u64, ccChunks).add(k * 3).read();
    while (c !== 0n) {
      const end = ptrAt(u64, c).add(1).read();
      for (let x = c + toU64(CHUNK_HEAD); x + size <= end; x += size) {
        if (genAt(x).read() % 2 === 0) continue;
        const n = countAt(x).read();
        if (n >= ST_WHITE || (n & COUNT) === 0n) continue;
        if (groupOf(x) === 0 || x >= SCANNABLE) continue;
        if ((n & ST_MASK) === ST_CAND) tableOff(x);
        joinRoot(x);
      }
      c = ptrAt(u64, c).read();
    }
  }
}

/**
 * The counted objects of one class (3.5, D39, D63): what freeing one takes, its release function, and how many there are.
 * Its objects are in the one counted heap every store shares. `make` places an object with a count of one, `share` adds
 * one, `drop` takes one away, and at zero the object waits to be freed, so a drop never frees anything itself. Every
 * `make` first does up to `RC_BUDGET` steps of freeing, of whatever is waiting, one reference slot or one block a step,
 * with a cursor through the object being freed. When the heap has nothing more, everything waiting is freed before `make`
 * gives up. If T can be in a cycle (`cycleGroup<T>()`, from the type graph), the cycle collector's barrier is in its count
 * operations and garbage cycles are collected (D41); if it can't, none of that is in them.
 *
 * Where tslc's `rc` expansion places every count of T (`countedExactly`, D74), a counted reference can't be stale (3.5), so
 * a count operation checks nothing; anywhere else it checks that the slot is this store's and the reference's generation.
 * @tsl.sharedSlots
 */
export class Rc<T extends object> {
  private id: u32 = 0; //   this store's number, in its slots' prefixes and the table of stores; 0 until its first make
  private k: usize = 0; //  the size class of one of its objects with no tail; 0 until its first make
  private owner: u32 = 0; // what that object's owner word is
  private elem: Elem<T> = inlineOf<T>();
  private tn: usize = 0; // R3: the tail length of its last object made with one, and that object's size class
  private tk: usize = 0;
  private tw: u32 = 0; // R21: and that object's owner word, worked out (checked) when tk is

  /** `release` is a top-level function, given each object as it's freed, one slot at a time (`Release`). */
  constructor(private release: Release<T>) {}

  /** T's group in the type graph: a constant natively, 0 if T can't be in a cycle. */
  /** @tsl.inline */
  // SAFETY: on the host the group is in this store's entry, registered at its first make.
  private grp(): u32 {
    const g = cycleGroup<T>();
    if (g === GROUP_UNKNOWN) return this.id === 0 ? 0 : toU32(ptrAt(u64, entryOf(this.id)).add(1).read() >> 48n);
    return g;
  }

  /** Objects made and not yet given back: waiting ones count, as they still hold what they hold. */
  // SAFETY: the entry is this store's, in the table.
  get size(): usize {
    if (this.id === 0) return 0;
    const e = ptrAt(u64, entryOf(this.id));
    if (cyclesLinked()) return toUsize(e.add(2).read() - (e.add(1).read() & FREED));
    return toUsize(e.add(2).read() - e.add(1).read());
  }

  /** The store's number and its entry, at its first make: its release function, typed for any class, and no objects. */
  // SAFETY: the table is grown to hold the entry before it's written; the old one is copied whole and then given back.
  private register(): bool {
    if (this.id !== 0) return true;
    if (heads === 0n && !setUp()) return false; // a registered store's make reads its size's list straight away
    if (stores + 1 >= tableCap) {
      if (cyclesLinked() && stores + 1 >= MAX_STORES) return false;
      const cap: u32 = tableCap === 0 ? 16 : tableCap * 2;
      const t = heap.allocBytes(toUsize(cap) * ENTRY);
      if (t === 0n) return false;
      if (table !== 0n) {
        copyBytes(t, table, toUsize(tableCap) * ENTRY);
        heap.freeBytes(table, toUsize(tableCap) * ENTRY);
      }
      table = t;
      tableCap = cap;
    }
    // its release function's number: freeing and the collector call it by a comparison and a direct call (D70, R1d)
    const r = releaseIndex(this.release);
    if (r === 0) trap(Trap.Dispatch);
    stores++;
    this.id = stores;
    ptrAt(u64, entryOf(this.id)).write(releaseIsEmpty(this.release) ? toU64(r) | EMPTY : toU64(r));
    ptrAt(u64, entryOf(this.id)).add(1).write(0n);
    ptrAt(u64, entryOf(this.id)).add(2).write(0n);
    if (cyclesLinked()) ptrAt(u64, entryOf(this.id)).add(1).write(toU64(this.grp()) << 48n);
    this.k = sizeClass(SLOT_PREFIX + elemSize(this.elem));
    this.owner = this.id * 256 + toU32(this.k);
    return true;
  }

  /** On the host, which can't see T: its group, from its first object, into the store and its entry. */
  // SAFETY: the entry is this store's, registered before its first object was placed.
  private learn(made: T): void {
    if (cycleGroup<T>() !== GROUP_UNKNOWN || ptrAt(u64, entryOf(this.id)).add(2).read() !== 1n) return;
    ptrAt(u64, entryOf(this.id)).add(1).write(toU64(cycleGroupOf<T>(made)) << 48n);
  }

  /** A fresh object's prefix: a count of one, the next generation, and its owner word. */
  /** @tsl.inline */
  // SAFETY: slot is a free counted slot of the size class in owner.
  private claim(slot: u64, owner: u32): u32 {
    countAt(slot).write(1n);
    const g = genAt(slot);
    // R17: unchecked, as a free slot's generation is even and below MAX_GEN - 1 (giveBack keeps one that reaches it off
    // every list), and so is a fresh one's, 0
    const gen = (g.read() + 1) >>> 0;
    g.write(gen);
    ownerAt(slot).write(owner);
    const made = ptrAt(u64, entryOf(this.id)).add(2);
    made.write(BigInt.asUintN(64, made.read() + 1n));
    return gen;
  }

  /** @tsl.inline */
  // SAFETY: only an odd generation that matches, in a slot of this store's, is one of ours and not yet given back. A scan's
  // bits are in the top of the owner and generation words of an object whose class can be in a cycle, so those are masked.
  private slotIn(item: T): u64 {
    // tslc placed every count: it can't be stale, so nothing is checked, its generation bits included (3.5, D74, R1f)
    if (countedExactly<T>()) return slotOfLive(item);
    const slot = slotOf(item);
    if (cycleGroup<T>() !== 0) {
      if ((ownerAt(slot).read() % 0x100_0000) >>> 8 !== this.id) trap(Trap.Stale);
      if ((genAt(slot).read() % 0x1_0000) !== genOf(item)) trap(Trap.Stale);
      return slot;
    }
    if (ownerAt(slot).read() >>> 8 !== this.id) trap(Trap.Stale);
    if (genAt(slot).read() !== genOf(item)) trap(Trap.Stale);
    return slot;
  }

  /** Whether a count word says nothing holds a count: zero, or waiting to be freed. */
  /** @tsl.inline */
  private gone(n: u64): bool {
    if (cycleGroup<T>() !== 0) return (n & COUNT) === 0n || n >= WAITING;
    return n === 0n || n >= WAITING;
  }

  /**
   * `make` for a class with a tail of n elements (D69): the moved object's fields go in a slot of its real size, from the
   * same size classes as every other counted object, and its tail is zeroed.
   */
  /** @tsl.moves item */
  /** @tsl.tailed item */
  /** @tsl.inline */
  tryMakeTail(n: usize, item: T): Counted<T> | null {
    return this.tailMake(n, 0, item);
  }

  /**
   * tryMakeTail, with the tail's first `keep` elements left unzeroed (R4): the caller writes them before anything reads
   * them, as a room a lowered array grows into is written with the elements it had.
   */
  /** @tsl.moves item */
  /** @tsl.tailed item */
  private tailMake(n: usize, keep: usize, item: T): Counted<T> | null {
    const slot = this.tailSlot(n);
    if (slot === 0n) return null;
    return this.tailPlace(slot, n, keep, item);
  }

  /**
   * R30: tailMake's steps and its slot, without the object: freeing's steps, the store registered, the size class for a tail
   * of n (kept as the last, with its owner word), and a free slot of it, off its list or slotFor's; 0 if there's none, or the
   * store can't be registered. Out of line, and given no object, so a caller's new object is never in memory of its own: it's
   * placed where it's made (tailPlace, inlined), its fields written straight into the slot.
   */
  /** @tsl.noinline */
  // SAFETY: a slot on a list is free and 2^k bytes; slotFor's is too.
  private tailSlot(n: usize): u64 {
    if (cyclesLinked()) {
      if (ccPhase !== 0 || (ccTop !== 0 && (ccGap === 0 || !pacing))) stepAll(budget);
      else idleStep();
    } else if (waiting !== 0n || cur !== 0n) freeAlloc(budget);
    if (!this.register()) return 0n;
    // the size class as for the last object made, if its tail was as long: a lowered array's holders mostly are (R3)
    let k = this.tk;
    if (n !== this.tn || k === 0) {
      k = sizeClass(SLOT_PREFIX + tailBytes(this.elem, n));
      this.tn = n;
      if (k !== this.tk) {
        this.tk = k;
        this.tw = tailOwner(this.owner, k);
      }
    }
    // a free slot of its size on its list first, as `tryMake` takes one (R3: a lowered `rc` array is made so)
    const head = ptrAt(u64, heads).add(k);
    const slot = head.read();
    if (slot !== 0n) {
      head.write(countAt(slot).read());
      return slot;
    }
    return slotFor(k);
  }

  /**
   * R30: a slot of size class tk, free, for an object with a tail of n elements (tn is n): claimed, the object placed in it
   * with its tail zeroed but for what's kept, as every make of a tailed object ends. Inlined, so the moved object is placed
   * where it's made.
   */
  /** @tsl.moves item */
  /** @tsl.tailed item */
  /** @tsl.inline */
  // SAFETY: the slot is a free one of size class tk, which holds the prefix and tailBytes(n) as tn is n, claimed before it's
  // placed in; keep is the caller's promise, and more than n traps.
  private tailPlace(slot: u64, n: usize, keep: usize, item: T): Counted<T> {
    const gen = this.claim(slot, this.tw);
    // a whole tail zeroed is one fill: only a room growth writes into (keep) takes the two around what it keeps
    const made = keep === 0 ? placeTail(slot, gen, n, item) : placeTail(slot, gen, n, item, keep);
    // learn has nothing to do but on the host, for a store's first object
    if (cycleGroup<T>() === GROUP_UNKNOWN) this.learn(made);
    if (cyclesLinked() && rest !== 0) restIfWork();
    return made;
  }

  /** @tsl.moves item */
  /** @tsl.tailed item */
  /** @tsl.inline */
  makeTail(n: usize, item: T): Counted<T> {
    return this.tailFast(n, 0, item);
  }

  /** makeTail with the tail's first `keep` elements left for the caller to write before anything reads them (R4). */
  /** @tsl.moves item */
  /** @tsl.tailed item */
  /** @tsl.inline */
  makeTailKeep(n: usize, keep: usize, item: T): Counted<T> {
    return this.tailFast(n, keep, item);
  }

  /**
   * R17: `makeTail` and `makeTailKeep`, inlined where the inliner inlines, as `make` is: for a tail as long as the last one
   * made (its size class known, R3), freeing's steps as `tailSlot` takes them, then a free slot of that size off its list.
   * Anything else is `tailSlot`'s, or with the steps taken, `tailSlotAfter`'s, out of line: the same steps and the same
   * slot. R19: a tail of another length than the last is made in line too, its size class worked out here (sizeClass,
   * inlined) and kept as the last, as `tailSlot` keeps it: a lowered array's rooms are each a length of their own, and its
   * holders' lengths alternate where two arrays of a class are made in turn. R30: whichever way the slot comes, the object
   * is placed here (tailPlace): only the slot is found out of line, so the moved object is never given to a call, and the
   * optimiser writes its fields straight into the slot, where it was built in a frame slot and copied.
   */
  /** @tsl.moves item */
  /** @tsl.tailed item */
  /** @tsl.inline */
  // SAFETY: the slot is a free one of size class tk, as tailPlace needs.
  private tailFast(n: usize, keep: usize, item: T): Counted<T> {
    let slot: u64 = 0n;
    if (
      this.id !== 0 &&
      !(cyclesLinked() && (ccPhase !== 0 || (ccTop !== 0 && (ccGap === 0 || !pacing))))
    ) {
      if (cyclesLinked()) idleStep();
      else if (waiting !== 0n || cur !== 0n) freeAlloc(budget);
      if (n !== this.tn || this.tk === 0) {
        // R22: a new length's size class, and its owner word only where the class is new too (short strings' lengths
        // change from one make to the next, and most share a class)
        const nk = sizeClass(SLOT_PREFIX + tailBytes(this.elem, n));
        this.tn = n;
        if (nk !== this.tk) {
          this.tk = nk;
          this.tw = tailOwner(this.owner, nk);
        }
      }
      const k = this.tk;
      const head = ptrAt(u64, heads).add(k);
      slot = head.read();
      if (slot !== 0n) head.write(countAt(slot).read());
      else {
        // R28: without the collector, a fresh slot cut in line where its page has room, as tailSlotAfter cuts it
        if (!cyclesLinked()) {
          slot = pageCut(k);
          if (slot !== 0n) genAt(slot).write(0);
        } else if (rest === 0 || (waiting === 0n && cur === 0n)) {
          // R30: with the collector, from its chunk in line, where slotFor's dryStep would do nothing
          slot = chunkCut(k);
          if (slot !== 0n) genAt(slot).write(0);
        }
        if (slot === 0n) slot = this.tailSlotAfter();
      }
    } else slot = this.tailSlot(n);
    if (slot === 0n) trap(Trap.OutOfMemory);
    return this.tailPlace(slot, n, keep, item);
  }

  /**
   * `tailFast`'s rest, its steps taken, its size class tk's list empty: slotFor's slot, as `tailSlot` takes it (R19: by way
   * of freshSlot, as the list was just found empty). R30: the slot alone; tailFast places the object.
   */
  /** @tsl.noinline */
  private tailSlotAfter(): u64 {
    return freshSlot(this.tk);
  }

  /** @tsl.moves item */
  tryMake(item: T): Counted<T> | null {
    const slot = this.slotSlow();
    if (slot === 0n) return null;
    return this.place(slot, item);
  }

  /**
   * R30: tryMake's steps and its slot, without the object: freeing's steps, then, for a store that has made something before,
   * a free slot of its size off its list, or else the store registered at its first make, and slotFor's; 0 if there's none.
   * Out of line and given no object, as tailSlot is, so `make` places its object where it's made.
   */
  /** @tsl.noinline */
  // SAFETY: a slot on a list is free and of the class's size class; slotFor's is too.
  private slotSlow(): u64 {
    if (cyclesLinked()) {
      if (ccPhase !== 0 || (ccTop !== 0 && (ccGap === 0 || !pacing))) stepAll(budget);
      else idleStep();
    } else if (waiting !== 0n || cur !== 0n) freeAlloc(budget);
    // the common case first: a store that has made something before, and a free slot of its size on its list
    if (this.id !== 0) {
      const head = ptrAt(u64, heads).add(this.k);
      const slot = head.read();
      if (slot !== 0n) {
        head.write(countAt(slot).read());
        return slot;
      }
    } else if (!this.register()) return 0n;
    return slotFor(this.k);
  }

  /**
   * R30: a free slot of the class's size class: claimed, and the object placed in it, as every make ends. Inlined, so the
   * moved object is placed where it's made.
   */
  /** @tsl.moves item */
  /** @tsl.inline */
  // SAFETY: the slot is a free one of the class's size class, claimed before the object is placed in it.
  private place(slot: u64, item: T): Counted<T> {
    const made = placeObject(slot, this.claim(slot, this.owner), item);
    // learn has nothing to do but on the host, for a store's first object
    if (cycleGroup<T>() === GROUP_UNKNOWN) this.learn(made);
    if (cyclesLinked() && rest !== 0) restIfWork();
    return made;
  }

  /**
   * R17: inlined where the inliner inlines, as the direct route's `__rc_new` is at -O2: freeing's steps first, as `tryMake`
   * takes them (a call, only with something waiting; with the collector, only while it's idle or waits out its gap), then
   * a free slot of its size off its list. Anything else is `slotSlow`'s, or with the steps taken, `slotAfter`'s, out of
   * line: the same steps and the same slot as `tryMake` takes. R30: whichever way the slot comes, the object is placed here
   * (`place`), so the moved object is never given to a call, and its fields are written straight into the slot.
   */
  /** @tsl.moves item */
  /** @tsl.inline */
  // SAFETY: the slot is a free one of the class's size class, as `place` needs.
  make(item: T): Counted<T> {
    let slot: u64 = 0n;
    if (this.id !== 0 && !(cyclesLinked() && (ccPhase !== 0 || (ccTop !== 0 && (ccGap === 0 || !pacing))))) {
      if (cyclesLinked()) idleStep();
      else if (waiting !== 0n || cur !== 0n) freeAlloc(budget);
      const head = ptrAt(u64, heads).add(this.k);
      slot = head.read();
      if (slot !== 0n) head.write(countAt(slot).read());
      else {
        // R28: without the collector, a fresh slot cut in line where its page has room: slotAfter's slot and steps
        if (!cyclesLinked()) {
          slot = pageCut(this.k);
          if (slot !== 0n) genAt(slot).write(0);
        } else if (rest === 0 || (waiting === 0n && cur === 0n)) {
          // R30: with the collector, from its chunk in line, where slotFor's dryStep would do nothing
          slot = chunkCut(this.k);
          if (slot !== 0n) genAt(slot).write(0);
        }
        if (slot === 0n) slot = this.slotAfter();
      }
    } else slot = this.slotSlow();
    if (slot === 0n) trap(Trap.OutOfMemory);
    return this.place(slot, item);
  }

  /**
   * `make`'s rest, for a registered store whose steps are taken and whose size's list is empty: slotFor's slot (R19: by way
   * of freshSlot, as the list was just found empty). R30: the slot alone; `make` places the object.
   */
  /** @tsl.noinline */
  private slotAfter(): u64 {
    return freshSlot(this.k);
  }

  /** One more count: the result is a second handle to the same object. */
  /** @tsl.inline */
  // SAFETY: slotIn checked it's ours and live, or tslc placed every count of T.
  share(h: Counted<T>): Counted<T> {
    const slot = this.slotIn(h);
    const c = countAt(slot);
    const n = c.read();
    // waiting to be freed: nothing holds a count to share
    if (!countedExactly<T>() && this.gone(n)) trap(Trap.Stale);
    c.write(n + 1n);
    if (cycleGroup<T>() !== 0 && n >= ST_WHITE) touch(slot); // the barrier (D41): a load and a branch
    return h;
  }

  /** The handle moved out, its count unchanged: for putting a local's count into a field. */
  /** @tsl.moves h */
  /** @tsl.inline */
  take(h: Counted<T>): Counted<T> {
    return h;
  }

  /** One count less. At zero it waits to be freed by later allocations, or `collect`. */
  /** @tsl.moves h */
  /** @tsl.inline */
  // SAFETY: slotIn checked it's ours and live, or tslc placed every count of T; a waiting object is never dropped, so the
  // queue's link can't overwrite a count.
  drop(h: Counted<T>): void {
    const slot = this.slotIn(h);
    const c = countAt(slot);
    const n = c.read();
    if (!countedExactly<T>() && this.gone(n)) trap(Trap.Stale);
    if (cycleGroup<T>() !== 0 && this.grp() !== 0) {
      // the barrier, and a candidate if a count is left (D41): the common case, a count left on an object in no scan that's
      // already a candidate, is a store and two tests
      if ((n & COUNT) > 1n && (n & ST_MASK) === ST_CAND) {
        c.write(n - 1n);
        return;
      }
      ccDrop(slot, n);
      return;
    }
    if (n > 1n) {
      c.write(n - 1n);
      return;
    }
    c.write(waiting | WAITING);
    waiting = slot;
  }

  /** A count-preserving move of `h` out of a slot, such as a vector's element moved: the barrier only (D41). */
  /** @tsl.inline */
  // SAFETY: slotIn checked it's ours and live, or tslc placed every count of T.
  touch(h: Counted<T>): void {
    if (cycleGroup<T>() === 0) return;
    const slot = this.slotIn(h);
    if (countAt(slot).read() >= ST_WHITE) touch(slot);
  }

  /**
   * What a release function does with the reference in a slot: `op` on `h` (3.5). Freeing drops it; the cycle collector,
   * for a class in the group it's scanning, counts an edge to it, marks it held, or, for an object decided to be garbage,
   * drops it unless it's garbage too (D41).
   */
  /** @tsl.moves h */
  /** @tsl.inline */
  // SAFETY: slotIn checked it's ours and live, or tslc placed every count of T.
  visit(h: Counted<T>, op: Visit): void {
    if (op === Visit.Drop) this.drop(h);
    else if (cyclesLinked()) this.visitCc(h, op);
  }

  /**
   * `visit`, for a class whose objects have no slots of their own, so freeing one is only giving its block back (R4).
   * Freeing with steps to spare (`spare`, set while a slot is visited) drops the last count of one by giving its block back
   * at once, as one of those steps, where `drop` would queue it to take that step later: the same steps, the bound the
   * same (D39), and no trip through the queue and its release function. Anything else is `visit`.
   */
  /** @tsl.moves h */
  /** @tsl.inline */
  // SAFETY: slotIn checked it's ours and live, or tslc placed every count of T. T's objects have no slots (the caller's
  // promise: tslc's expansion calls this only for such a class), so a count of one, the one this drops, is the last, and
  // what freeing would do with the object is give its block back, which this does.
  visitLeaf(h: Counted<T>, op: Visit): void {
    if (op === Visit.Drop && spare !== 0n) {
      const slot = this.slotIn(h);
      const c = countAt(slot);
      const n = c.read();
      if (n === 1n) {
        leafBack(slot);
        return;
      }
      // R24: a count left, which `drop` would take one off, as here, with the count read once: the same test of it (a
      // count tslc placed is never stale or waiting, and one below WAITING isn't), and no barrier, as T is in no cycle;
      // above 1, so less one can't wrap
      if (cycleGroup<T>() === 0 && n > 1n && (countedExactly<T>() || n < WAITING)) {
        c.write(BigInt.asUintN(64, n - 1n));
        return;
      }
    }
    this.visit(h, op);
  }


  /** visit's collector part: Collect, Scan and Trace. */
  /** @tsl.moves h */
  // SAFETY: slotIn checked it's ours and live, or tslc placed every count of T.
  private visitCc(h: Counted<T>, op: Visit): void {
    const g = this.grp();
    if (op === Visit.Collect) {
      if (g === 0 || !ccWhite(this.slotIn(h))) this.drop(h);
      return;
    }
    if (g === 0 || g !== ccGroup) return;
    if (op === Visit.Scan) ccEdge(this.slotIn(h));
    else ccTrace(this.slotIn(h));
  }

  /** Drops the old value and gives back the new one, for `o.f = rc.replace(o.f, h)`. Null is dropped as nothing. */
  /** @tsl.moves h */
  /** @tsl.inline */
  replace(old: Counted<T> | null, h: Counted<T>): Counted<T> {
    if (old !== null) this.drop(old);
    return h;
  }

  /** The count, for tests and assertions: always checked. */
  // SAFETY: checked here that it's ours and live.
  count(h: Counted<T>): u32 {
    // a reference tslc's expansion counts is a plain address, with no generation to check (R8)
    if (countedExactly<T>()) return toU32(countAt(slotOfLive(h)).read() & COUNT);
    const slot = slotOf(h);
    if (cycleGroup<T>() !== 0) {
      if ((ownerAt(slot).read() % 0x100_0000) >>> 8 !== this.id) trap(Trap.Stale);
      if (genAt(slot).read() % 0x1_0000 !== genOf(h)) trap(Trap.Stale);
      return toU32(countAt(slot).read() & COUNT);
    }
    if (ownerAt(slot).read() >>> 8 !== this.id) trap(Trap.Stale);
    if (genAt(slot).read() !== genOf(h)) trap(Trap.Stale);
    return toU32(countAt(slot).read());
  }

  /** Frees everything waiting now, and garbage cycles: the one unbounded call, only when asked. */
  collect(): void {
    if (cyclesLinked()) collectAll();
    else drainAll();
  }

  /** Where a weak reference finds `h`: its slot. */
  // SAFETY: slotIn checked it's ours and live.
  weakSlot(h: Counted<T>): u64 {
    return this.slotIn(h);
  }

  /** And the generation it has to still have there. */
  // SAFETY: slotIn checked it's ours and live, so its generation is the one in the slot's prefix. A reference tslc's
  // expansion counts is a plain address, carrying no generation (R8), so that's read from the prefix, a scan's bits off.
  weakGen(h: Counted<T>): u32 {
    const slot = this.slotIn(h);
    if (countedExactly<T>()) return genAt(slot).read() % 0x1_0000;
    return genOf(h);
  }

  /**
   * A weak reference's target, with a count of its own, if it's still alive: the slot is this store's, still has the
   * generation, and its count is above zero, and the cycle collector hasn't decided it's garbage (D41). From the moment the
   * count reaches zero, or the decision, this gives `undefined`, while the object waits, after it's freed, and after the
   * slot holds another object of any class, so nothing is ever brought back (D39). These checks stay wherever T is
   * counted: a weak reference holds no count, so it's the one that can go stale. The count it adds is a count operation, so
   * an object in a scan is held by it.
   */
  // SAFETY: a counted slot is never given back to the heap, so reading its prefix is reading our own memory.
  upgrade(slot: u64, gen: u32): Counted<T> | undefined {
    if (cycleGroup<T>() !== 0) {
      if ((ownerAt(slot).read() % 0x100_0000) >>> 8 !== this.id) return undefined;
      if (genAt(slot).read() % 0x1_0000 !== gen) return undefined;
      const m = countAt(slot).read();
      if ((m & COUNT) === 0n || m >= WAITING) return undefined;
      if ((ccPhase === 3 || ccPhase === 4) && (m & ST_MASK) === ST_WHITE) return undefined; // decided: garbage (D41)
      countAt(slot).write(m + 1n);
      if (m >= ST_WHITE) touch(slot);
      return objectAt<T>(slot);
    }
    if (ownerAt(slot).read() >>> 8 !== this.id) return undefined;
    if (genAt(slot).read() !== gen) return undefined;
    const n = countAt(slot).read();
    if (n === 0n || n >= WAITING) return undefined;
    countAt(slot).write(n + 1n);
    return objectAt<T>(slot);
  }
}

/**
 * A weak reference to a counted object (3.5, D39, D74): `new WeakRef(x)` in an `rc` package. It holds the object's slot
 * and generation and no count, so it never keeps the object alive; `deref` gives the object with a count of its own while
 * the object's count is above zero, and `undefined` from the moment it reaches zero or the cycle collector decides it's
 * garbage.
 */
export class Weak<T extends object> {
  private slot: u64 = 0n;
  private gen: u32 = 0;

  constructor(
    private store: Rc<T>,
    target: Counted<T>,
  ) {
    this.slot = store.weakSlot(target);
    this.gen = store.weakGen(target);
  }

  deref(): Counted<T> | undefined {
    return this.store.upgrade(this.slot, this.gen);
  }
}

/**
 * A room of the counted heap (R3): raw words for what a library keeps in the counted heap, such as a lowered `rc` array's
 * elements once they outgrow its holder's tail. It's a counted object with no reference slot, so freeing it is one step,
 * and the collector's walk sees an object like any other.
 */
export class Room {
  words = tail(u64);
}

function roomRelease(_o: Room, _at: usize, _op: Visit): usize {
  return 0;
}

const rooms = new Rc<Room>(roomRelease);

/**
 * A room of n words: an allocation of the counted heap, which takes its freeing steps as any `make` does. Its first `keep`
 * words aren't zeroed (R4): the caller writes them before anything reads them, as growth copies the elements it had; the
 * rest are zero. R19: inlined, as `make` is, into a lowered array's growth.
 */
/** @tsl.inline */
export function roomMake(n: usize, keep: usize): Counted<Room> {
  return rooms.makeTailKeep(n, keep, new Room());
}

/** Where a room's first word is. R19: inlined, a field's address. */
/** @tsl.inline */
// SAFETY: a room's words are its tail, there while the room is, which its holder's count keeps.
export function roomAddr(r: Counted<Room>): u64 {
  return tailAddr(r);
}

/**
 * A room let go of: its count dropped, so it's freed, in one step, by a later allocation (D39); or, by freeing with a step
 * to spare, given back at once as that step (R4, `visitLeaf`: a room has no slots).
 */
/** @tsl.moves r */
export function roomDrop(r: Counted<Room>): void {
  rooms.visitLeaf(r, Visit.Drop);
}
```

*Arrays in the counted heap (R3, D66, D69).* A lowered `rc` package's array is `JsRoomArray<T>`, `JsArray`'s rules with its elements in the counted heap: its holder (`JsArr_C`) is made with a tail of its first room (`withTail`, `makeTail`), so a holder and the elements that fit are one counted allocation, and past that each room is a `Room` from `roomMake`, doubling, the one outgrown let go of at once. Freeing is the holder's: its elements a step each, then its own room if it has one (`rooms`, `trim`).

```ts
// file: ex-gc-roomarray.ts
import { idiv, toU64, Trap, trap, u16, u32, u64, u8, type bool, type usize } from "@tsl/core";
import { copyBytes, elemSize, ptrAt, tailAddr, type ElemOf, type Ptr } from "@tsl/unsafe";
import { roomAddr, roomDrop, roomMake, type Counted, type Room } from "./ex-gc-rc.ts";

/**
 * A JS array of T as a lowered `rc` package holds it (R3, D66, D69): `JsArray`'s rules, with its elements in the counted
 * heap. Its first room is its holder's tail, so a holder and the elements that fit are one counted allocation; past that,
 * each room is a `Room`, doubling as it fills, and the one outgrown is let go of. Its holder is made by
 * `withTail(n, new Holder(length))` and then gives it its tail (`attach`), which a constructor can't read. Freeing is
 * its holder's: the elements, a step each, then its room if it has one of its own (`rooms`, `trim`).
 */
export class JsRoomArray<T> {
  private data: u64 = 0n;
  private len: usize = 0;
  private cap: usize = 0;
  private room: Counted<Room> | null = null;

  /**
   * `length` elements, each zero once its holder's tail is attached: JS's `new Array(length)`, or `[]`. `holes` says a
   * slot past the length can be read again as a hole, so a shorter length zeroes what it drops: an array of references.
   * A lowered array of numbers can't have a hole (it traps 15 first), so its dropped slots are left as they are.
   */
  constructor(
    private elem: ElemOf<T>,
    length: usize,
    private holes: bool,
  ) {
    this.len = length;
  }

  /** The first room: `holder`'s tail of n elements, zeroed, which this array is in place in. At least its length. */
  /** @tsl.inline */
  // SAFETY: the holder was just made with a tail of n of this array's elements (its element's size), which lives as long
  // as the holder, and this array, in place in it, never outlives it.
  attach<H extends object>(holder: H, n: usize): void {
    if (n < this.len) trap(Trap.Bounds);
    this.data = tailAddr(holder);
    this.cap = n;
  }

  /** @tsl.inline */
  get length(): usize {
    return this.len;
  }

  /** The room the array has, in elements. */
  /** @tsl.inline */
  get capacity(): usize {
    return this.cap;
  }

  /** How many rooms of its own the array holds, 0 or 1: what its holder's freeing gives back after the elements. */
  /** @tsl.inline */
  get rooms(): usize {
    return this.room !== null ? 1 : 0;
  }

  /** @tsl.inline */
  // SAFETY: i is at most cap, so the address is in the room or just past it: an element step, with nothing to check.
  private slot(i: usize): Ptr<T> {
    return ptrAt(this.elem, this.data).add(i);
  }

  /** @tsl.inline */
  private at(i: usize): u64 {
    return this.slot(i).addr;
  }

  /** `a[i]`; past the end traps 2: a hole reads as zero, `null` for a reference. */
  /** @tsl.inline */
  // SAFETY: i is below len, so its slot is in the room.
  get(i: usize): T {
    if (i >= this.len) trap(Trap.Bounds);
    return this.slot(i).read();
  }

  /** `a[i] = v` below the length. */
  /** @tsl.inline */
  // SAFETY: i is below len, so its slot is in the room.
  set(i: usize, v: T): T {
    if (i >= this.len) trap(Trap.Bounds);
    this.slot(i).write(v);
    return v;
  }

  /**
   * Appends v and gives the new length, as JS's `push` does. R17: inlined at every level that inlines, as JsArray's is
   * (R16): with room left, a store and the length raised; full, `pushGrow`, out of line.
   */
  /** @tsl.inline */
  // SAFETY: n is below cap, so the slot at n is in the room.
  push(v: T): usize {
    const n = this.len;
    if (n >= this.cap) return this.pushGrow(v);
    this.slot(n).write(v);
    const m = n + 1;
    this.len = m;
    return m;
  }

  /** `push` on a full array: a room twice as big (`grow`), then the store. Out of line, so `push` stays small. */
  /** @tsl.noinline */
  // SAFETY: grow left room for one more, so the slot at len is in the room.
  private pushGrow(v: T): usize {
    const n = this.len;
    this.grow(n + 1);
    this.slot(n).write(v);
    const m = n + 1;
    this.len = m;
    return m;
  }

  /** The last element, removed; on an empty array, `none`. */
  // SAFETY: n is above zero, so the slot at n - 1 is in the room.
  pop(none: T): T {
    const n = this.len;
    if (n === 0) return none;
    const v = this.slot(n - 1).read();
    this.setLength(n - 1);
    return v;
  }

  /** The first element, removed, with every other moved down one; on an empty array, `none`. */
  // SAFETY: n is above zero, so slots 0 to n - 1 are in the room, and the copy moves n - 1 of them down one.
  shift(none: T): T {
    const n = this.len;
    if (n === 0) return none;
    const v = this.slot(0).read();
    copyBytes(this.at(0), this.at(1), (n - 1) * elemSize(this.elem));
    this.setLength(n - 1);
    return v;
  }

  /** Room for `n` elements without moving them again. */
  reserve(n: usize): void {
    if (n > this.cap) this.grow(n);
  }

  /**
   * JS's `a.length = n` within what's reserved: shorter zeroes what it drops (`holes`), longer adds holes. Gives n. R17:
   * inlined, as JsArray's is, and shorter tested first, which needs no test of the room, as the length is never above it:
   * so the lowering's pop (the length one less, once it's above zero) is that test, and with holes, one slot zeroed. And
   * with no holes, a longer length zeroes what it adds, as nothing kept those slots zero (a shorter length left them, and
   * growth zeroes nothing past what it copies): each slot below the length reads what was written there, or zero.
   */
  /** @tsl.inline */
  setLength(n: usize): usize {
    const len = this.len;
    if (n < len) {
      if (this.holes) this.clear(n, len);
    } else {
      if (n > this.cap) trap(Trap.Bounds);
      // with no holes, what's past the length wasn't kept zero, so a longer length zeroes what it adds (R17)
      if (!this.holes) this.clear(len, n);
    }
    this.len = n;
    return n;
  }

  /**
   * The room of its own let go of, and the array left empty: true if it had one. The last step of freeing its holder,
   * after its counted elements have been visited; the holder's tail goes with the holder.
   */
  trim(): bool {
    const r = this.room;
    this.len = 0;
    this.data = 0n;
    this.cap = 0;
    if (r === null) return false;
    this.room = null;
    roomDrop(r);
    return true;
  }

  /** Slot i, below the length, made a hole. */
  zero(i: usize): void {
    if (i >= this.len) trap(Trap.Bounds);
    this.clear(i, i + 1);
  }

  /** Calls f on each element and its index, in order, up to the length when it started; f mustn't change the length. */
  forEach(f: (x: T, i: usize) => void): void {
    const n = this.len;
    for (let i: usize = 0; i < n; i++) f(this.get(i), i);
  }

  /** @tsl.inline */
  // SAFETY: the slots from `from` to `to` are below cap, so these are the room's, a whole element at a time; an element's
  // size is a constant, so one arm is left.
  private clear(from: usize, to: usize): void {
    const size = elemSize(this.elem);
    const end = this.at(to);
    for (let a = this.at(from); a < end; a = a + toU64(size)) {
      if (size === 8) ptrAt(u64, a).write(0n);
      else if (size === 4) ptrAt(u32, a).write(0);
      else if (size === 2) ptrAt(u16, a).write(0);
      else ptrAt(u8, a).write(0);
    }
  }

  // SAFETY: the new room holds ncap elements, at least len; the first len are copied from the old one, which is let go of
  // if it's a room of its own (the holder's tail goes with the holder). Only what can be read as a hole is zeroed (R4):
  // in an array of references, the words past the ones the copy writes whole, so a slot a longer length reaches reads
  // `null`; an array of numbers has no holes (the lowering traps 15 first, and a shorter length leaves its slots as they
  // are already), so nothing in it is. Rare, so out of line: push stays small.
  /** @tsl.noinline */
  private grow(need: usize): void {
    const dbl = this.cap * 2;
    const ncap = dbl < need ? need : dbl;
    const size = elemSize(this.elem);
    // R28: an element of a word is a word: the same counts with no rounding (size is a constant, so one arm is left; cap
    // and so ncap are below 2^33, as a tail's length is below 2^32, so neither form traps where the other wouldn't)
    const words = size === 8 ? ncap : idiv(ncap * size + 7, 8);
    const keep = size === 8 ? this.len : idiv(this.len * size, 8);
    const next = roomMake(words, this.holes ? keep : words);
    const at = roomAddr(next);
    copyBytes(at, this.data, this.len * size);
    const old = this.room;
    this.room = next;
    this.data = at;
    this.cap = ncap;
    if (old !== null) roomDrop(old);
  }
}
```

**Memory modes (D38).** A package says in its `tsl.json` what an escaping `new` means: `"memory": "strict" | "leak" | "manual" | "rc"`,
default `strict`. In `rc` every class instance is counted, which tslc writes out as `@tsl/gc` calls (D74, below); `tmk lower` still
lowers `rc` by the direct route (D39). In a *lowered* `leak` or `manual` package (4.5) one more place is tslc's to choose (R6): a
`new` its escape analysis proves no export call outlives goes in the per-call region, the module's call arena, which each
export gives back as it returns (4.5's "The per-call region"); a package written by hand has no call arena, and so no region.

| Mode | Escaping `new` | Freeing | Stale reference | Safe? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `strict` | Compile error | `Slab`, `Vec` | Traps | Yes |
| `leak` | Allocated from the registered page source | Never | Can't happen | Yes |
| `manual` | Allocated from the registered heap | `unsafeFree(x)` | Undefined, with no generation check | No |
| `rc` | Every class instance: `make` on its class's `Rc` store, which tslc declares beside the class (D74). In lowered code, D39's counted heap in `auto`, and `make` through the TSL route (R2) | When its count reaches zero: queued at once, and freed by later allocations, a slot or a block a step | Can't happen: a holder has a count, and a copy without one has the slot's generation | Yes. Garbage cycles are collected (D41; in `@tsl/gc` since R1c) |

The rest of this list is about TSL proper, in its modes. `rc` has its own paragraph below.

Everything else in this section still holds in every mode, and these are the only differences:

- *Which `new` escapes* is what TSL3001 and TSL3002 already compute. In a `leak` or `manual` package those two errors are off
  for a `new`: being stored, returned, passed to a parameter that's stored or to a function value, stored by its own constructor, or
  flowing out of the loop that made it (TSL3007 otherwise) makes that `new` a heap allocation instead. One that does none of these is
  still a stack object, with all a stack object's rules (TSL2020). The errors stay on for what can't be made to last: an arena's loan
  and a view are still TSL3001 and TSL3002, which includes a read of a field holding its object in place (D37). So does TSL3003: TSL
  proper's capturing closures have no environment struct. A heap `new` allocates, so it's TSL1017 on a `@tsl.noalloc` path.
- *`leak` is memory-safe, because nothing is ever freed*, and needs no `unsafe`. Running out of memory traps with code 14.
- *A `leak` object is a static object made at run time*: an 8-byte prefix holding the generation `0xffff`, and references tagged
  with it, as for a top-level object. Plain pointers would be correct if everything in the package were leak-allocated, but a package can
  hold `Slab` objects too, and a class-typed field can't say which it has. With the prefix there's one representation, so `gen.chk` works
  unchanged on both: removing a `Slab` object still makes a stored reference to it trap with code 5, in a `leak` object's field as anywhere.
  `Slab.remove` of a leak object traps with code 5, as of a static one. A leak reference can also go in a `strict` package's stored
  field, where its generation always passes. The check is omitted, as a whole-program fact, in `leak` and `manual` packages on
  references to a class no `placeObject` or `objectAt` ever produces, since nothing of that class can go stale. The prefix's price is
  8 bytes per object.
- *A class nothing of which can go stale has no prefix (D64).* Extending the rule above from the check to the prefix, as a whole-program
  fact in every mode: a class is *plain* when no `placeObject` or `objectAt` makes one of it (so no `Slab` holds it), none is static (a
  top-level `new`), none comes from an arena, no generation check is made on one anywhere in the program, and it isn't a layout class or
  aligned above 8. A plain class's `leak` object is its fields with no prefix, as `manual`'s are, and every reference to it is a plain
  pointer with no tag, so a field access masks nothing. **The prefix stays** on every class that fails any of those: whatever a `Slab`
  can hold, whatever has a static instance or comes from an arena, anything a stored reference to which is read and checked somewhere
  (a `leak` reference held in a `strict` package's field and read there is one), layout classes, and classes aligned above 8. `slotOf`
  and `genOf` of a plain reference trap with code 5, as of a stack object. A plain class's initialisers of zero aren't stored by a
  `new`, which zeroes the object anyway, and an initialiser the constructor overwrites first, from something that can't read the
  object, isn't stored either.
- *Zeroed construction: a constructor stores no zero initialiser (pipe-c).* In every mode, a field initialiser that is a zero
  literal (`0` but not `-0`, `0n`, `false`, `null`) isn't stored by the class's constructor, so long as nothing before it in the
  initialisers can have written the field (each earlier one stores a literal, or arithmetic on other variables, into a field of
  this object) and no object of the class is ever built in place inside another (an embedded field's `new`). A constructor
  left with nothing to do isn't called, and isn't emitted. **Why it's sound:** a constructor runs only at a `new`, and every
  `new` other than one in place starts on memory that is all zero at that moment. A stack object is zero-filled at the `new`
  itself, each time it runs, so the one slot a `new` in a loop reuses is zeroed again. A `manual` object is zero-filled after
  `__heap_alloc` gives the block, so a block the heap's free lists hand back dirty, which they do, is zeroed before the
  constructor sees it (`corpus/memory/manual/manual_zero_reuse.ts`, which fails with that fill taken out). A `leak` object
  is from the bump allocator, which never hands out a byte twice, over the page source, which hands out zeroed pages by its
  contract (`setPageSource`, 3.8; the bare-metal source and every test pool zero what they give). A `Slab` slot, an `Rc`
  store's slot, in `@tsl/alloc`, `@tsl/std` and `@tsl/gc`, are reused dirty, but nothing is ever constructed in one: their
  `add` and `make` take a direct `new` by `@tsl.moves`, which is built as a stack object, zero-filled, and `placeObject`
  copies all of it into the slot, so the slot's old bytes are overwritten whole. An arena's `make` zero-fills and runs no
  constructor; a static object is built at compile time, from its constructor's source, into zeroed bytes. `rc`'s counted
  heap zeroes each block as it hands it out (D39), and no TSL constructor runs on it: lowered `rc` builds take the direct
  route, and TSL proper's `rc` is `@tsl/gc`'s `make` (D74), above. An object built in place is built inside its holder's bytes, which its
  holder's constructor may already have reached, so a class with one keeps every store. `TMK_TSL_OPT_OFF=ctorzero` turns
  this off, for measuring and for finding what moved a pin. An object with a tail (D69) is zero to its last element too:
  `leak`'s from the page source, `manual`'s filled at its real size, and `placeTail` fills all but the fields it copies.
  `corpus/std/zero_ctor.ts` dirties a reused `Slab` slot, a
  reused `Rc` slot and a stack object in a loop, and reads the zero fields back, natively and on V8 and JSC.
- *`manual` is true unsafe.* Fields hold plain 64-bit pointers with no prefix and no check for a class no `Slab`
  holds, so an object and a field access are what C's are. Without an optimiser the code around them isn't: see Phase C in M5. For a class one does, a reference out of memory is checked if it has a tag and not if it has none, so generation checks stay on for
  anything from a `Slab`, at the price of a test on the tag. `unsafeFree(x)`, in `@tsl/unsafe`, takes an object back: its reference must have no
  tag (a `Slab`'s or a static's traps with code 5), and one known to be something else at compile time is TSL5008. Outside a `manual` package
  it's TSL5007. Every module in a `manual` package must be listed in `unsafeModules` (TSL5006) and counts toward `tmk audit`.
- *A raw reference stays in `manual` packages.* It can't be stored in a field or global of a `strict` or `leak` package, directly or by a call that
  stores it (TSL3008), because nothing could check a generation there, and `leak`'s promise would no longer hold. A safe API has to wrap it,
  handing out values. A reference a `manual` package returns can be held in a local elsewhere; it can't be stored.
- *`kernel-core` stays `strict`, by policy* (5.6): nothing there allocates implicitly, and nothing there is unsafe without saying so.

**Direction for `leak` (owner, 2026-11-03, D38).** `leak` should eventually be a debug mode, not a production one. It stays selectable and
safe, and nothing about it changes now. `rc` now exists, and it's the production mode for escaping allocations in lowered code, and
`leak` remains as a debugging baseline. That's what it's for: a program that behaves differently under `leak` than under `rc` or `manual` has
a freeing bug or a refcounting bug.

**`rc` in TSL proper (D74).** In a package with `"memory": "rc"` a person writes plain classes and `new`, and tslc expands each of the
package's modules into the TSL they could have written with `@tsl/gc`, then compiles that as it compiles any `strict` module: nothing after
the expansion knows `rc` exists, and `tmk compile <file> --emit tsl` prints it. What's written is checked first, as TSL proper, where it's
written (`compiler/host/expand-rc.ts`). The rules:

- *What's counted.* Every class declared in the package, but a generic one (TSL9001 for now). A class with a tail is made by
  `withTail(n, new T(…))`, which becomes `makeTail`.
- *Stores, named and placed.* Each class `C` gets, right after its declaration in its own module, `C$release` (its release function)
  and `const C$rc = new Rc<C>(C$release)`, exported if `C` is. A module that imports `C` and needs its store imports `C$rc` beside it.
  `$` keeps the names out of the way of a program's own. A class some module makes a `WeakRef` to also gets `C$weak`, the store of its
  weak references. (R1 also gave each class a stepping function, `C$step`, for freeing to reach its store's own queue; with one queue
  and the release functions in the table of stores, R1b dropped it.)
- *Release functions, generated.* `C$release(o, at, op)`'s slots are, in order, each field of a counted class (a nullable one tested
  for `null`), then each vector of counted references in a field, a `Vec` held in place (D37): while it has elements, a step pops its last
  and visits it, and once it's empty, a step gives its buffer back (`trim`), so a freed vector is never read again. For a class the
  type graph puts in a cycle (R1c), `Visit.Scan` and `Visit.Trace` visit a vector's elements where they are, so the collector looking
  changes nothing.
- *`new C(…)`* is `C$rc.make(new C(…))`: owned. Its arguments are borrowed by the constructor. A counted parameter property becomes a
  field and an assignment taking its own count, `this.p = p === null ? null : C$rc.share(p)`.
- *Values are owned or borrowed*, by D39's convention. A call's counted result is owned; a read of a local, a parameter, `this`, a
  field, a global or a vector's element is borrowed. A borrowed value going where a count is kept, a field, a global, a vector, a result,
  an owned local, is `share`d; an owned one is moved there.
- *Stores count the new value first, then drop the old (D39's order).* `o.f = e` is `o.f = C$rc.replace(o.f, e')` when `e` can't be
  null, and otherwise `const $o = o.f; o.f = e'; if ($o !== null) C$rc.drop($o);`. A vector's `set` is `replace` on `get`; `push` and
  `insert` take an owned value; `pop`, `removeAt` and `swapRemove` give one; `clear` drops each element first. On a vector of a class
  in a cycle, while a scan is on, each element `pop`, `removeAt`, `swapRemove` or `insert` moves is touched first (D41's barrier on a
  move, R1c). A constructor's first
  assignment to a field that has nothing in it yet is a plain one.
- *Last use is a move.* An owned local named once in a statement of its own block, and never after it, is moved there with `take` (a
  nullable one, as it is), and isn't dropped. A `return` is the last use of any local it names once. So is a statement naming an owned
  local once, of any enclosing block, when the next statement assigns that local without reading it (R1b): the value is dead between
  them, so `c.next = h; h = c;` moves `h`'s count into `c.next`, and the assignment has nothing to drop. Building a list was a share and
  a drop a node before.
- *Scope exit drops* what a local owns, at the end of its block and on every `return`, `break` and `continue` that leaves it, in
  reverse order of declaration. An owned value used only for reading, an argument or a receiver, is a temporary the statement drops after
  it. A counted result thrown away is dropped.
- *Borrows, where the move and escape facts prove them sound.* An argument is borrowed, and a caller holds a count across a call only
  for an argument it read from memory (a field, a global or a vector), and only if the callee can give up a count held along a path
  (isn't *quiet*), whole-program, as D39's overwriters are. A local holds no count of its own when every value it's given is read along a
  path rooted in a parameter, `this`, a global, a borrowed local or an owned `const` local that outlives it, and nothing in its region,
  from its declaration to its block's end, can give up such a count: no counted store, no vector element moved or replaced, no call
  through a function value, and no call to a function that isn't quiet. A closure's counted parameters are held for its whole body.
  Freeing is deferred, and freeing a dead object can't reach a count held along a live path, so `make` doesn't break a borrow.
- *`WeakRef`.* `WeakRef<C>` is `@tsl/gc`'s `Weak<C>`, and `new WeakRef(x)` is `C$weak.make(new Weak<C>(C$rc, x))`; `deref()` gives an
  owned value or `undefined`.
- *What isn't expanded yet*, each TSL9001 at its place: a vector of counted references as a local or global (it would drop every
  element at once at scope exit), a top-level counted object, a generic counted class, an allocation after a call in the same expression
  or under `&&`, `||`, `??` or `?:`, an assignment of a counted value inside an expression, a loop condition that allocates, and a nested
  function declaration.
- *Counted objects stay in their package (R1b).* A module outside the program's `rc` packages can't name a counted class or have a
  value whose type holds one (a reference, a vector of them, a function taking or giving one, its store), and can't import a name the
  expansion adds; an `rc` package's module, as written, doesn't name `@tsl/gc`'s `Rc`, `Weak` or `Counted`. Each is TSL9001 at its
  place (corpus/neg/rc_counted_outside.ts, corpus/neg/rc/rc_names_rc.ts). `@tsl/std`'s `Vec` and `@tsl/gc` itself hold them as type
  parameters, which the expansion's rules for them account for.

*No generation checks on what the expansion counts (R1b; D64, D74).* Every count operation of `@tsl/gc` checks that the slot is the
store's and the reference's generation is the slot's, and a counted reference is checked at a use, because a hand-written program can
copy a handle without `share` (above). Where every count of a class is the expansion's, those checks can't fail, so tslc leaves them
out: for a class an `rc` package declares (`@tsl/unsafe`'s `countedExactly<T>()`, a constant natively and `false` on the host, so the
host checks everything), `share`, `drop`, `replace` and `visit` check nothing (since R1f not even the reference's own generation bits,
through `slotOfLive`, where `slotOf` traps on an even one), and no use of a reference to one is checked anywhere
(escape.ts), as D64 dropped prefixes where nothing can go stale. *Proof.* Call a reference *held* if it's in a field, global or vector
element of an object or module that is itself held or alive, or in an owned local or temporary. (1) The expansion keeps every counted
object's count equal to the number of held references to it: `make` gives one to an owned local or temporary; a copy into a holder is a
`share` of a borrowed value or a `take` of an owned one, whose holder stops holding it; every overwrite drops the old value after
counting the new; scope exit and every jump out drop what owned locals hold; a freed object's release function drops each reference it
held; a vector's operations move counts as above. Nothing else changes a count: by the boundary rule no code outside the `rc` packages
holds or counts a counted object, an `rc` package's module can't import `@tsl/unsafe` (tslc checks it as written with unsafe code refused, whatever `unsafeModules` says) and doesn't name `Rc`,
so the only stores of a counted class are the expansion's. (2) A borrowed reference, a local or argument holding no count of its own,
is only read where the expansion proved that what it was read from keeps its count: a caller holds a count across any call that isn't
quiet, and a borrowed local's region has no counted store, vector move, call through a function value or call that isn't quiet. (3) So
at every use and every count operation in an `rc` package, the object referred to has a count of at least one, by (1) if the reference
is held and by (2) if it's borrowed. An object is freed, and its slot's generation changed, only when its count is zero and an
allocation's freeing step or `collect` reaches it, and a slot is reused only after that. So the slot still holds the object, of the
store's class, with the reference's generation and a count above zero: the owner check, the generation check and the count check each
pass, every time. (4) A release function reads the fields of an object whose count is zero, waiting to be freed, which is still in its
slot until its last step. **Where the proof doesn't reach, the checks stay:** a hand-written `Rc` (corpus/std/rc_gc.ts, which any
package may use; a stale copy traps 5); `Weak`, whose `deref` checks the slot's owner, generation and count, as a weak reference holds
no count and is exactly what can go stale (and a store of weak references is itself a hand-written-style `Rc` of `@tsl/gc`'s class,
checked); unsafe code, which 3.8 makes responsible for what it writes, and which can't be in an `rc` package; and a `Slab`, whose `add`
takes a direct `new` (TSL3006), which a counted object never is, so no counted class is ever in one. A native caller can't give a hand-written
`rc` package's export a counted object, as exported functions taking or giving objects aren't built for TSL proper yet (pile item 6).
A lowered `rc` package's can, since R8 (4.5's ABI in `rc`), and the proof holds with the native caller as one more holder, as 3.8
holds unsafe code to what it writes: the caller gets each counted object it holds from the package (the placing export, or a result),
each with one count, adds one only through the package's retain export, which the expansion counts as a `share`, and gives one back
only through its release export, whose `@tsl.moves` parameter the expansion drops; and it holds the count of each argument across the
call, as (2)'s caller does. So (1)'s count is still the number of held references, the caller's among them, and nothing reads a
reference's generation. MEASURED (R1b, below): leaving the checks in makes the list 1.62x and churn 1.47x the instructions.

*A counted reference is an address (R8).* Since no check reads the generation a reference to a class the expansion counts carries
(the paragraph above), such a reference carries none: `placeObject`, `placeTail` and `objectAt` give a plain address for such a class
(lower-native.ts, `untaggedCounted`), where every other class's reference keeps its generation in its top 16 bits. `Weak` reads the
generation it keeps from the slot's prefix (the object is live as the weak reference is made, so it's the slot's), and `count` reads the
count with nothing checked, as `share` and `drop` do. So a native caller holds, reads and writes a counted object at its address, as
through the direct route, and a reference the caller hands in is the one the package made. A release function, given its object by the
freeing loop as `objectAt<Counted0>` (no class the expansion counts), sees a tagged reference, which it only reads fields through. What
moved: tools/r8-moved.ts lists each pinned build, every one an `rc` build through the TSL route (M5's R8 record).

*Strings counted by the expansion (R10).* Through the TSL route a lowered `rc` program's strings aren't `@tsl/jsrt`'s
`JsString`, which a `leak` package makes and never frees: they're two classes the printing puts in the program itself, as it
puts an array's holder (compiler/host/emit-rcstr.ts), so the expansion counts them as it counts every other class and there's
still one counting implementation, with nothing added to TSL. `JsStr` is a string, `n` UTF-16 units: its own tail (D69) where
its `buf` is null, a flat string, or `n` units of a `JsStrBuf` from `start`, a view, which concatenation and a long substring
make. `JsStrBuf` is a concatenation's buffer, `head` to `end` used, which an append or prepend writes outside every view's
units, D42's rule, so nothing a string reads ever changes. A buffer holds nothing, so the type graph has no cycle through
strings: a string is never a collector's candidate (D41), and a cycle of objects holding strings is freed with its strings by
the collector as any cycle is. Freeing a `JsStr` is one slot and a block, and a `JsStrBuf` a block, within D39's step bound.
Literals are module state made in `__init` (`strlit_3 = jsStrOf(lit("…"))`), held there; units are read and copied through the
tails' own slices (`.set`, `.subarray`), and hashed (D42's HalfSipHash under the hash key, `jsStrHash`) from them, so nothing
in it is unsafe; the one address it takes is a native caller's, to write a string argument's units at (4.5). *Why it's sound:*
the proof above holds unchanged, as `JsStr` and `JsStrBuf` are an `rc` package's classes like any other, and a view's
reference to its buffer is a field the expansion counts. *What differs from `JsString`, by design:* a substring of a flat
string copies where `JsString` shares it (a view's owner is always a buffer here, as a string holding a string would put
strings in a cycle of the type graph), which doesn't show in a result. *R21: one-unit strings from a table,* as `JsString`'s and the
direct route's static one: a one-unit string below 256 (`charAt`, an index, `String.fromCharCode`, a one-unit `substring`,
`slice` or code point) is `jsStrUnits`' slot for it, a holder of the runtime's own (`JsStrUnits`, its 256 slots a
`JsRoomArray`'s tail, counted as any array holder is), made the first time it's asked for and held by module state from
then on, so never freed, as the direct route never frees its static ones; a hit is `JsRoomArray.get`'s checked read and the
string's count, inlined, and a miss, or a unit from 256 up, is `jsStrUnitMade`'s, out of line. So such a string is live from
its first use on: what's live after a case counts the table's holder and the strings made so far (tools/r10-tests.ts'
`UNIT_TABLE_LIVE`, r11-tests.ts' `EXC_UNIT_TABLE`). An append or prepend of one unit to a buffer is a checked store, not a
copy's call. Nothing unchecked is added: the table is a module-state array of the program's own class. *R22: a short join made
once.* `a + b + c`, the lowering's `strConcat` of `strConcat`'s result and `c`, prints as one call of the program's own
`strConcat3`, which, where all three are non-empty and 64 units or fewer in all, makes the result once (`jsStrJoined3`: one
`jsStrZeroed` and three checked `.set`s), and otherwise makes the two joins as before. Before, the first join copied `a` and `b`
into a string of their own, freed straight after, and the second copied them again, at a length of its own, so each make worked
out a size class. Only where `c` is pure (a literal, a local, module state, or a test, choice or wrapping sum of those), as it's now
evaluated before `a` and `b` are joined, and where the program doesn't desugar its own exceptions (there `strConcat`'s RangeError
returns through `__exc_on`, and each call is its own statement anyway); the result is the same string, flat, with the same hash
word. Concatenation's new buffer is made out of line (`jsStrGrown`), so `concat`'s own frame is an append's or a prepend's. The
tail is still zeroed when it's made, and every copy is `.set`'s checked one: nothing unchecked is added. *R23:* the runtime's
`strCharCodeAt` (compiler/rt's, printed over the program's own `JsStr`) is tagged `@tsl.inline` in `rc`, so -O1 inlines it into
a scan's loop as -O2 already did; its checks are unchanged. *R24:* so are `strConcat` and `strIndex` (`a + b` and `s[i]`),
which an append loop calls once a turn. A view's start, buffer and hash word are its constructor's parameters (`new JsStr(n,
start, buf, hw)`; a flat string's are 0, null and 0), where `jsStrView` stored them after `new`: a constructor's stores to its
own fields give up nothing, so a function that makes views (`concat`) is quiet in the expansion's sense and the strings it
reads along a path, `this.buf` among them, are borrowed with no count, where each was shared and dropped. And `unit` takes its
length and start as their u32 bits (`wrapU32`), as neither is ever negative (every maker checks them): were one negative, the
index past it would be huge, and the units' own bounds check, which stays, would trap. *R25:* compiler/rt's `strIndexOf` prints
as far as its empty pattern's case and then `return s.indexFrom(p, start)`, JsStr's own search (inlined) over the two strings'
runs of units (`all()`), each read checked against its run's length, where the loop's own test proves the first read's check
(-O1's `loopbounds`, -O2's `checks`); the printed loop read each unit through `unit`, two checks each, and `matchAt` was a call.
A code point's length (`cpLen`, which `for...of` calls once a code point) reads through `unit`, inlined, where `all()` worked out
the run each call; `sub`'s common ways (the whole string, empty, one unit) are inlined, its copy and view out of line
(`subMade`), a view's copy read from its buffer's units straight; `copyFrom` (a join's copies) is inlined, one unit a checked
store and a whole string its run; `a === b`'s quick answers (the same string, one missing, the lengths differ) are inlined and
the units compared out of line (`jsStrSame`); and `slice`, `substring` and their index conversions (`relIndex`, `absIndex`) are
tagged `@tsl.inline`. Every read is still a checked read of a tail, and every copy `.set`'s checked one. *R26:* where the
lowering gives `strCharCodeAt` an `i32` index, it prints in integers: `if (x < 0 || x >= s.len()) return NaN;` then
`s.unit(x)`. JS's steps on an `i32` (ToIntegerOrInfinity, then NaN outside [0, length)) are the value itself, never NaN, so
`x !== x`, `Math.trunc` and `t | 0` drop out and the answers are the same; the float printing's compares were ones -O1's
passes, which read integer tests, can't take. `unit`'s own checks stay. A typed array a lowered function makes with a constant length (number text's scratch digits) prints in `rc` too,
as R9's layout class, which the expansion doesn't count (it holds no reference and has no tail, `isLayoutStorage`): tslc puts
it on the stack, or refuses the printing where its view would outlive the frame, as for a `strict` package's stack object.

*Maps' tables at the counted heap's pace (R11).* A lowered `rc` program's `Map` or `Set` is `@tsl/jsrt`'s `JsMap` or `JsSet`
held in place by a counted holder (R2), and its tables are `JsArray` buffers from `@tsl/std`'s global allocator, outside the
counted heap. Before R11 making them took no freeing steps, and `@tsl/std` running out freed nothing the counted heap had
waiting, so a program churning sets of numbers ran out through the TSL route where the direct route, whose map's vectors are
the counted heap's, doesn't (corpus/lower/strmap/rc_churn.ts, and a sets-only probe within its first 1,000 sets). The holder
now makes its map with `tablesIn(rcAllocSteps, rcCollect)`: before each table it makes, the map takes the freeing steps one
allocation of the counted heap takes (`@tsl/gc`'s `rcAllocSteps`: what `make` takes before it looks for a slot, then, as for a
size whose free list is empty, what the budget has left, never more than `RC_BUDGET` in all), and where `@tsl/std` has nothing
left (`JsArray`'s `tryReserve`), the counted heap frees everything it has waiting, the tables of the maps waiting with it
(`rcCollect`, exhaustion's one pause), before `@tsl/std` is asked again and, still empty, traps 14. And a map holding nothing
counted is freed in one step, its buffers, not one a position: a set of numbers was a hundred steps for one allocation's
budget. *Why it's sound:* D39's bound is per allocation and is unchanged, a table's steps being an allocation's; freeing keeps
the pace the counted heap's own allocations set, with tables counted as allocations; and running out frees all that's waiting
in both, so it means what's live doesn't fit. *Not done:* the tables in the counted heap itself (a room per table, as a lowered
array's elements are), built first and measured: `@tsl/gc`'s size classes are powers of two with a slot's prefix, and a slot
past a page is a chunk of whole pages never given back, so by that arithmetic a 4 KiB table takes 12 KiB, and a set-heavy
probe (r11_set_queue.ts) ran out through the TSL route where the direct route didn't. What's left outside the counted heap: a map's first buffers (eight of four
entries, made by its constructor before its holder is counted, with no drain), and `@tsl/jsrt`'s generations and cursors,
reused once closed, so bounded by what's open at once.

*Exceptions counted by the expansion (R11).* Through the TSL route in `rc`, exceptions are class printing's own desugaring
(D68), as in `leak` and `manual`: `__exc_val: Dyn | null` is module state the expansion counts like any other, so `throw v` is
a counted store, a catch takes the value into a local (a share) and clears the global (a drop), a `finally` holds what's in
flight in a local across its code, counted, and every jump out of a labelled block drops what the block's locals hold. A
native caller that took an exception gives it back with the module's own `__exc_release` (4.5). Four things the expansion
needed, all general: module state is counted by its declared type, not as tsc narrows it (tsc keeps a global narrowed to
`null` by an assignment across a call that throws, so a catch after it read the value as no reference and shared nothing); a
field declared assigned with no initialiser (an `unknown`'s storage shared between the classes it can hold, D68) is visited
