```ts
  shift(none: T): T {
    const n = this.len;
    if (n === 0) return none;
    const v = this.slot(0).read();
    copyBytes(this.at(0), this.at(1), (n - 1) * elemSize(this.elem));
    this.setLength(n - 1);
    return v;
  }

  /** Room for `n` elements without moving the buffer again. */
  reserve(n: usize): void {
    if (n > this.cap) this.grow(n);
  }

  /**
   * R11: `reserve`, where running out of memory gives false and leaves the array as it was, as `reserve` traps 14: a map
   * whose tables are held by a counted object frees what the counted heap has waiting, then asks again (`JsMap.tablesIn`).
   * The block growth would take is asked for and given straight back first, so growth then finds it (the allocator's own
   * list for its size, or @tsl/std's runs of whole pages); an array in the per-call region grows there, as it always does.
   */
  // SAFETY: the block is the allocator's, taken and given back at the size it was taken with, and nothing kept of it.
  tryReserve(n: usize): bool {
    if (n <= this.cap) return true;
    if (!inCallRegion(this)) {
      const twice = this.cap * 2;
      const want = (twice < n ? n : twice) * elemSize(this.elem);
      const probe = heap.allocBytes(want);
      if (probe === 0n) return false;
      heap.freeBytes(probe, want);
    }
    this.grow(n);
    return true;
  }

  /**
   * JS's `a.length = n` within what's reserved: shorter drops elements, longer adds holes. Gives n. R16: inlined, with
   * `clear`, as a lowered `pop` is a read and this (the direct route's is a store of the length).
   */
  // R17: shorter is tested first, and needs no test of the room, as the length is never above it; so the lowering's pop
  // (the length one less, once it's above zero) is that test alone, and, with no holes, the store. Longer, with no holes,
  // zeroes what it adds (`holes`).
  /** @tsl.inline */
  // SAFETY: the slots from n to len are below cap.
  setLength(n: usize): usize {
    const len = this.len;
    if (n < len) {
      if (this.holes) this.clear(n, len);
    } else {
      if (n > this.cap) trap(Trap.Bounds);
      // with no holes, what's past the length wasn't kept zero, so a longer length zeroes what it adds (R17)
      if (!this.holes) this.clear(len, n);
    }
    this.len = n;
    return n;
  }

  /**
   * The buffer given back, where the array gives buffers back, and the array left empty: true if it had one. It's the
   * last step of freeing a lowered `rc` package's array (R2), after its counted elements have been moved out.
   */
  // SAFETY: the buffer is cap elements from the global allocator, given back at that size, and nothing reads it after:
  // the length is 0, so no slot is in reach.
  trim(): bool {
    if (this.cap === 0) return false;
    if (this.giveBack && !addrInCallRegion(this.data))
      heap.freeBytes(this.data, this.cap * elemSize(this.elem));
    this.len = 0;
    this.data = 0n;
    this.cap = 0;
    return true;
  }

  /**
   * Takes `from`'s buffer, length and room, giving its own buffer back first as `trim` does, and leaves `from` empty with
   * none: a map moves a table into its old one so, without making an array (R2).
   */
  adopt(from: JsArray<T>): void {
    this.trim();
    this.data = from.data;
    this.len = from.len;
    this.cap = from.cap;
    from.data = 0n;
    from.len = 0;
    from.cap = 0;
  }

  /**
   * Exchanges buffer, length and room with `other` (R4): how a map that has made a new table's buffers in its old table's
   * arrays puts them in place, once nothing more can run out of memory. Both are arrays of the same element, made alike.
   */
  swap(other: JsArray<T>): void {
    const d = this.data;
    const n = this.len;
    const c = this.cap;
    this.data = other.data;
    this.len = other.len;
    this.cap = other.cap;
    other.data = d;
    other.len = n;
    other.cap = c;
  }

  /** Slot i, below the length, made a hole: zero, `null` for a reference (R2: a map's slot it no longer holds). */
  zero(i: usize): void {
    if (i >= this.len) trap(Trap.Bounds);
    this.clear(i, i + 1);
  }

  /** Calls f on each element and its index, in order, up to the length when it started; f mustn't change the length. */
  forEach(f: (x: T, i: usize) => void): void {
    const n = this.len;
    for (let i: usize = 0; i < n; i++) f(this.get(i), i);
  }

  /** @tsl.inline */
  // SAFETY: the slots from `from` to `to` are below cap, so these are the buffer's, a whole element at a time; an
  // element's size is a constant, so one arm is left.
  private clear(from: usize, to: usize): void {
    const size = elemSize(this.elem);
    const end = this.at(to);
    for (let a = this.at(from); a < end; a = a + toU64(size)) {
      if (size === 8) ptrAt(u64, a).write(0n);
      else if (size === 4) ptrAt(u32, a).write(0);
      else if (size === 2) ptrAt(u16, a).write(0);
      else ptrAt(u8, a).write(0);
    }
  }

  // SAFETY: the new block holds ncap elements, at least len; the first len are copied from the old one and the rest
  // zeroed, and the old block goes back to the allocator with the size it was taken with, unless it's the per-call
  // region's (R6), which gives back nothing a block at a time. An array in the region grows in it. R16: an array in the
  // region gives nothing back at all, so only one outside it asks where its old buffer is: what it gives back is a subset
  // of what it gave back before (a region array's buffers are the region's, but for one `adopt` or `swap` brought in, which
  // then stays where it is, as every buffer an array holds at the region's end does). Only `push`'s slow path, `reserve`
  // and `tryReserve` grow (not the constructor): inlined into those, which are out of line.
  /** @tsl.inline */
  private grow(need: usize): void {
    const cap = this.cap;
    const dbl = cap + cap;
    const ncap = dbl < need ? need : dbl;
    const size = elemSize(this.elem);
    const bytes = ncap * size;
    const region = inCallRegion(this);
    const next = region ? callRegionBytes(bytes) : heap.allocBytes(bytes);
    if (next === 0n) trap(Trap.OutOfMemory);
    const old = this.data;
    const kept = this.len * size;
    if (old !== 0n) {
      copyBytes(next, old, kept);
      if (this.giveBack && !region && !addrInCallRegion(old)) heap.freeBytes(old, cap * size);
    }
    if (this.holes) bytesAt(next + toU64(kept), bytes - kept).fill(0);
    this.data = next;
    this.cap = ncap;
  }
}
```

`JsArenaArray` (R13, D66, pile item 7), in `@tsl/jsrt` as its own module (`@tsl/jsrt/arena`), which a lowered `strict` package's class printing prints its arrays as: `JsArray`'s rules, `length`, `get`, `set`, `push`, `pop`, `shift`, `setLength`, `reserve` and `zero`, holes as zeroed slots, with its buffers only from the call arena the export call runs in (`callRegionBytes`), never `@tsl/std`'s heap, which `strict` code doesn't have. The arena is the caller's, reset whole between calls (D36), so nothing is given back: an outgrown buffer stays until the reset, as the direct route's call-bounded vectors' do, and growth past what the arena has left traps 14, as every arena allocation does. tslc places the array itself in the arena too (region.ts), and refuses a package where one could outlive the arena (4.5's "Arrays in `strict`"). Only a package whose tsl.json says `"lowered"` can import it (TSL1023), so the kernel's own `strict` TSL never depends on it, and it imports nothing of `@tsl/std`. On a JS engine the arena is simulated memory nothing gives back (`callRegionBytes` in `@tsl/unsafe`), so printed TSL runs on V8 and JSC as it is.

```ts
// file: ex-jsrt-arena.ts
import { toU64, Trap, trap, u16, u32, u64, u8, type usize } from "@tsl/core";
import {
  bytesAt,
  callRegionBytes,
  copyBytes,
  elemSize,
  ptrAt,
  type ElemOf,
  type Ptr,
} from "@tsl/unsafe";
export { ref } from "@tsl/unsafe";

/**
 * A JS array of T for a lowered `strict` package (R13), which has no heap: `JsArray`'s rules (D66), `length`, `get`, `set`,
 * `push`, `pop`, `shift`, `setLength`, `reserve`, holes as zeroed slots, with its buffers only from the call arena the
 * export call runs in (`callRegionBytes`), never `@tsl/std`'s heap. The arena belongs to the caller, who resets it between
 * calls (D36), so nothing here is ever given back: an outgrown buffer stays where it was until the reset, as the direct
 * route's call-bounded vectors' do. tslc places the array itself in the arena too (region.ts), and refuses the printing of
 * a program where one could outlive the export call. Growth past what the arena has left traps 14, as every arena
 * allocation does. Only `tmk lower` prints it, into a package whose tsl.json says "lowered" (TSL1023); on a JS engine the
 * arena is simulated memory nothing gives back (`callRegionBytes` in @tsl/unsafe).
 */
export class JsArenaArray<T> {
  private data: u64 = 0n;
  private len: usize = 0;
  private cap: usize = 0;

  /** `length` elements, each zero: JS's `new Array(length)` with its holes, or `[]`. */
  // R16: made at its final size in one step, as the direct route's `__vec_new` makes a vector: one block of max(length, 4)
  // elements from the arena, zeroed, and no growth path. Inlined at every level that inlines, so a constant length folds.
  /** @tsl.inline */
  // SAFETY: the block is ncap elements of the call arena, at least length, which traps 14 where it has no room, so it's
  // never 0; nothing else has it.
  constructor(
    private elem: ElemOf<T>,
    length: usize,
  ) {
    const ncap = length < 4 ? 4 : length;
    const bytes = ncap * elemSize(elem);
    const block = callRegionBytes(bytes);
    if (block === 0n) trap(Trap.OutOfMemory);
    bytesAt(block, bytes).fill(0);
    this.data = block;
    this.cap = ncap;
    this.len = length;
  }

  /** @tsl.inline */
  get length(): usize {
    return this.len;
  }

  /** The room the buffer has, in elements. */
  /** @tsl.inline */
  get capacity(): usize {
    return this.cap;
  }

  /** @tsl.inline */
  // SAFETY: i is at most cap, so the address is in the buffer or just past it: an element step, with nothing to check.
  private slot(i: usize): Ptr<T> {
    return ptrAt(this.elem, this.data).add(i);
  }

  /** @tsl.inline */
  private at(i: usize): u64 {
    return this.slot(i).addr;
  }

  /** `a[i]`; past the end traps 2 (`a[i]!`): a hole reads as zero, `null` for a reference. */
  /** @tsl.inline */
  // SAFETY: i is below len, so its slot is in the buffer.
  get(i: usize): T {
    if (i >= this.len) trap(Trap.Bounds);
    return this.slot(i).read();
  }

  /** `a[i] = v` below the length. Past it, `setLength` first, which is where JS's holes come from. */
  /** @tsl.inline */
  // SAFETY: i is below len, so its slot is in the buffer.
  set(i: usize, v: T): T {
    if (i >= this.len) trap(Trap.Bounds);
    this.slot(i).write(v);
    return v;
  }

  /**
   * Appends v and gives the new length, as JS's `push` does. R16: inlined at every level that inlines, as the direct
   * route's push is: with room left, a store and the length bumped; full, `pushGrow`, out of line.
   */
  /** @tsl.inline */
  // SAFETY: n is below cap, so the slot at n is in the buffer.
  push(v: T): usize {
    const n = this.len;
    if (n >= this.cap) return this.pushGrow(v);
    this.slot(n).write(v);
    const m = n + 1;
    this.len = m;
    return m;
  }

  /** `push` on a full array: the buffer doubled (`grow`), then the store. Out of line, so `push` stays small. */
  /** @tsl.noinline */
  // SAFETY: grow left room for one more, so the slot at len is in the buffer.
  private pushGrow(v: T): usize {
    const n = this.len;
    this.grow(n + 1);
    this.slot(n).write(v);
    const m = n + 1;
    this.len = m;
    return m;
  }

  /** The last element, removed; on an empty array, `none`, and the array stays empty, as JS's `pop` gives `undefined`. */
  // SAFETY: n is above zero, so the slot at n - 1 is in the buffer.
  pop(none: T): T {
    const n = this.len;
    if (n === 0) return none;
    const v = this.slot(n - 1).read();
    this.setLength(n - 1);
    return v;
  }

  /** The first element, removed, with every other moved down one; on an empty array, `none`, as JS's `shift`. */
  // SAFETY: n is above zero, so slots 0 to n - 1 are in the buffer, and the copy moves n - 1 of them down one.
  shift(none: T): T {
    const n = this.len;
    if (n === 0) return none;
    const v = this.slot(0).read();
    copyBytes(this.at(0), this.at(1), (n - 1) * elemSize(this.elem));
    this.setLength(n - 1);
    return v;
  }

  /** Room for `n` elements without moving the buffer again. */
  reserve(n: usize): void {
    if (n > this.cap) this.grow(n);
  }

  /** JS's `a.length = n` within what's reserved: shorter drops elements, longer adds holes. Gives n. R16: inlined. */
  /** @tsl.inline */
  // SAFETY: the slots from n to len are below cap.
  setLength(n: usize): usize {
    if (n > this.cap) trap(Trap.Bounds);
    if (n < this.len) this.clear(n, this.len);
    this.len = n;
    return n;
  }

  /** Slot i, below the length, made a hole: zero, `null` for a reference. */
  zero(i: usize): void {
    if (i >= this.len) trap(Trap.Bounds);
    this.clear(i, i + 1);
  }

  /** @tsl.inline */
  // SAFETY: the slots from `from` to `to` are below cap, so these are the buffer's, a whole element at a time; an
  // element's size is a constant, so one arm is left.
  private clear(from: usize, to: usize): void {
    const size = elemSize(this.elem);
    const end = this.at(to);
    for (let a = this.at(from); a < end; a = a + toU64(size)) {
      if (size === 8) ptrAt(u64, a).write(0n);
      else if (size === 4) ptrAt(u32, a).write(0);
      else if (size === 2) ptrAt(u16, a).write(0);
      else ptrAt(u8, a).write(0);
    }
  }

  // SAFETY: the new block is ncap elements of the call arena, at least len; the first len are copied from the old one and
  // the rest zeroed, as the arena's memory is reused. The old block stays in the arena, which the caller resets whole, so
  // nothing reads it after: `data` is the new one. The arena traps 14 where it has no room left, so `next` is never 0.
  // R16: only `push`'s slow path and `reserve` grow (not the constructor): inlined into those, which are out of line.
  /** @tsl.inline */
  private grow(need: usize): void {
    const cap = this.cap;
    const dbl = cap + cap;
    const ncap = dbl < need ? need : dbl;
    const size = elemSize(this.elem);
    const bytes = ncap * size;
    const next = callRegionBytes(bytes);
    if (next === 0n) trap(Trap.OutOfMemory);
    const kept = this.len * size;
    if (this.data !== 0n) copyBytes(next, this.data, kept);
    bytesAt(next + toU64(kept), bytes - kept).fill(0);
    this.data = next;
    this.cap = ncap;
  }
}
```

`JsMap` and `JsSet` (D72), in `@tsl/jsrt`: JS's `Map` and `Set`, `compiler/rt/map.ts` (D42, D47) written in TSL, which class printing prints a lowered program's maps as (4.5), and which a person can write too. A key is anything `keyHash` takes (an integer, a reference by identity, a class or dispatch interface with `hashKey` and `sameKey`, as `JsString` is); a number is held as its bits by `jsNumKey`, -0 as +0 and every NaN one NaN, so an integer compare is SameValueZero. Growth moves 4 entries an insert or delete, and a cursor finds its place across moves and clears through generations, with nothing registered. An unsafe module of `@tsl/jsrt`.

```ts
// file: ex-jsrt-map.ts
import {
  f64,
  Trap,
  toUsize,
  trap,
  u16,
  u32,
  u64,
  u8,
  wrapU32,
  type bool,
  type i32,
  type usize,
} from "@tsl/core";
import { keyHash, keySame, ptrAt, type ElemOf } from "@tsl/unsafe";
import { heap } from "@tsl/std";
import { JsArray } from "./ex-jsrt-array.ts";

// JS's `Map` and `Set` (D42, D47, D72), compiler/rt/map.ts written in TSL. Entries are in insertion order, in parallel
// arrays. `heads` and `chain` hold a hash table of positions: a link to position i is i + 2, END ends a chain, and a head
// of TOMB or END is empty. `chain[i]` is TOMB for a deleted entry. Along a chain positions only go down.
//
// A full table doesn't grow in one operation (D47). A new table is made at its final size, with room at its front for
// what's live, and the old one is emptied into it in order, STEP positions in each insert and delete after, while lookups
// look in both. Every array is sized when it's made, so nothing grows by copying. When a move starts, or a table clears,
// the generation is replaced: a cursor holding an older one finds its place from where the move put each old position,
// which the move writes into the old chain as MOVED | its new position. Nothing registers a cursor, so one that's dropped
// costs nothing, but where a map `freesTables` (a lowered `rc` package's), whose cursors tslc's expansion closes, so its
// generations and cursors are reused once none is open (R3).
const TOMB: u32 = 0;
const END: u32 = 1;
const MOVED: u32 = 0x80000000;
/** (s - 2) >>> 0 below this: s is a link, 2 to 2^31 - 1. TOMB and END wrap to the top, and so would MOVED | p (R29). */
const LINKS: u32 = 0x7ffffffe;
const MIN_BUCKETS: u32 = 4;
/** Old positions moved in each insert or delete while a move is on: the new table has room for the move to finish first. */
const STEP: u32 = 4;
/** Every NaN's key: JS's maps hold one NaN, whatever its bits. */
const NAN_KEY: u64 = 0x7ff8000000000000n;

let key0: u32 = 0x243f6a88;
let key1: u32 = 0x85a308d3;
let scratch: u64 = 0n; // 8 bytes where a number's bits are read, made the first time

/** The hash key (D42): two words, which a caller with entropy sets before it makes a map. */
export function jsMapKey(a: i32, b: i32): void {
  key0 = wrapU32(a);
  key1 = wrapU32(b);
}

/**
 * D42's string hash: HalfSipHash-1-3 of n UTF-16 units at p, two to a word, under the hash key, in 30 bits, as
 * compiler/rt's strHash gives it. A `JsString` key's `hashKey` is this, kept in its hash word.
 */
// SAFETY: the n units at p are a live string's, read below n only.
export function jsUnitsHash(p: u64, n: i32): u32 {
  const at = ptrAt(u16, p);
  const len: u32 = wrapU32(n);
  let v0: u32 = key0;
  let v1: u32 = key1;
  let v2: u32 = (0x6c796765 ^ key0) >>> 0;
  let v3: u32 = (0x74656462 ^ key1) >>> 0;
  let i: u32 = 0;
  while (i + 2 <= len) {
    const m: u32 = (at.add(toUsize(i)).read() | (at.add(toUsize(i + 1)).read() << 16)) >>> 0;
    v3 = (v3 ^ m) >>> 0;
    v0 = (v0 + v1) >>> 0;
    v1 = ((v1 << 5) | (v1 >>> 27)) >>> 0;
    v1 = (v1 ^ v0) >>> 0;
    v0 = ((v0 << 16) | (v0 >>> 16)) >>> 0;
    v2 = (v2 + v3) >>> 0;
    v3 = ((v3 << 8) | (v3 >>> 24)) >>> 0;
    v3 = (v3 ^ v2) >>> 0;
    v0 = (v0 + v3) >>> 0;
    v3 = ((v3 << 7) | (v3 >>> 25)) >>> 0;
    v3 = (v3 ^ v0) >>> 0;
    v2 = (v2 + v1) >>> 0;
    v1 = ((v1 << 13) | (v1 >>> 19)) >>> 0;
    v1 = (v1 ^ v2) >>> 0;
    v2 = ((v2 << 16) | (v2 >>> 16)) >>> 0;
    v0 = (v0 ^ m) >>> 0;
    i += 2;
  }
  const last: u32 = ((len << 25) | (i < len ? at.add(toUsize(i)).read() : 0)) >>> 0;
  v3 = (v3 ^ last) >>> 0;
  for (let r: u32 = 0; r < 4; r++) {
    v0 = (v0 + v1) >>> 0;
    v1 = ((v1 << 5) | (v1 >>> 27)) >>> 0;
    v1 = (v1 ^ v0) >>> 0;
    v0 = ((v0 << 16) | (v0 >>> 16)) >>> 0;
    v2 = (v2 + v3) >>> 0;
    v3 = ((v3 << 8) | (v3 >>> 24)) >>> 0;
    v3 = (v3 ^ v2) >>> 0;
    v0 = (v0 + v3) >>> 0;
    v3 = ((v3 << 7) | (v3 >>> 25)) >>> 0;
    v3 = (v3 ^ v0) >>> 0;
    v2 = (v2 + v1) >>> 0;
    v1 = ((v1 << 13) | (v1 >>> 19)) >>> 0;
    v1 = (v1 ^ v2) >>> 0;
    v2 = ((v2 << 16) | (v2 >>> 16)) >>> 0;
    if (r === 0) {
      v0 = (v0 ^ last) >>> 0;
      v2 = (v2 ^ 0xff) >>> 0;
    }
  }
  return (v1 ^ v3) & 0x3fffffff;
}

/** A keyed MurmurHash3 finaliser over the key's own hash: an integer's value, a reference's identity, or its hashKey. */
/** @tsl.inline */
// SAFETY: the hash can depend on an address. It only chooses a chain, and iteration is by position, so no result can.
function hashOf<K>(k: K): u32 {
  let h: i32 = keyHash(k) ^ key0;
  h = h ^ (h >>> 16);
  h = Math.imul(h, 0x85ebca6b);
  h = h ^ key1 ^ (h >>> 13);
  h = Math.imul(h, 0xc2b2ae35);
  return (h ^ (h >>> 16)) >>> 0;
}

/**
 * A number as a key: its bits, with -0 as +0 and every NaN one NaN, so that comparing keys as integers is JS's
 * SameValueZero. `jsKeyNum` gives the number back. Inlined (R4): a lookup's every key goes through it, and at -O1 it
 * was a call each.
 */
/** @tsl.inline */
// SAFETY: scratch is 8 bytes of the global allocator's, this module's alone and never given back, read as the u64 a
// double was just written as.
export function jsNumKey(x: f64): u64 {
  if (x !== x) return NAN_KEY;
  const s = scratchWord();
  ptrAt(f64, s).write(x + 0);
  return ptrAt(u64, s).read();
}

/** The number a key from `jsNumKey` is. */
// SAFETY: as jsNumKey.
export function jsKeyNum(k: u64): f64 {
  const s = scratchWord();
  ptrAt(u64, s).write(k);
  return ptrAt(f64, s).read();
}

/**
 * The scratch word, made the first time; out of memory traps 14 (R6). With a map's own objects and arrays in the per-call
 * region, the word can be the first thing of a map's the global allocator is asked for, and a null one was written at 0.
 * Inlined, as jsNumKey is.
 */
/** @tsl.inline */
function scratchWord(): u64 {
  if (scratch === 0n) {
    const s = heap.allocBytes(8);
    if (s === 0n) trap(Trap.OutOfMemory);
    scratch = s;
  }
  return scratch;
}

/**
 * One move or clear. `next` is always newer. A generation made by a move has `end`, how many positions the old table had,
 * `base`, where what's inserted after the move starts goes, and where the move put each old position: in the old table's
 * chain while that table is the map's (`live`), and in `ranks`, the chain's buffer taken over, once it isn't (R3).
 */
export class JsMapGen {
  cleared: bool = false;
  next: JsMapGen | null = null;
  ranks: JsArray<u32> | null = null;
  end: u32 = 0;
  base: u32 = 0;
  live: bool = false; // the ranks are the map's old chain, the move still on (R3)
  keep: JsArray<u32> | null = null; // a reused generation's array for ranks, empty while it's unused (R3)
}

/** Where an iteration is: `for...of`, `forEach`, spread and the iterators each hold one. */
export class JsMapCursor {
  pos: u32 = 0; // the next position to look at
  cur: u32 = 0; // what the last advance found
  done: bool = false;
  inOld: bool = false; // pos is in the table `gen`'s move is emptying
  curOld: bool = false; // and so is cur
  link: JsMapCursor | null = null; // a closed cursor's next, in the cursors to reuse (R3)
  constructor(public gen: JsMapGen) {}
}

// What maps that `freesTables` reuse (R3): generations once no cursor can read them, and cursors once closed. @tsl/jsrt's
// own objects are never freed (a `leak` package), so such a map makes them only when none is free to reuse, and what it
// has in use at once is what it needs, not what it ever made.
let freeGens: JsMapGen | null = null;
let freeCursors: JsMapCursor | null = null;

/**
 * R11: what a map whose tables a counted object holds (`tablesIn`) calls as it makes a table: `steps`, the freeing steps
 * an allocation of the counted heap takes, before each, and `drain`, which frees everything the counted heap has waiting,
 * when @tsl/std has nothing left, before asking once more. A lowered `rc` package's maps name @tsl/gc's `rcAllocSteps` and
 * `rcCollect`. A program has one counted heap, so this is module state, not a map's, held in an object as a function value
 * in memory is (TSL1010).
 */
export type TableSteps = () => void;

function noSteps(): void {}

class Tables {
  constructor(
    public steps: TableSteps,
    public drain: TableSteps,
  ) {}
}

const tables = new Tables(noSteps, noSteps);

/**
 * Where k is in a table, at or above `low`, or -1 as a u32. Positions fall along a chain, so the first below `low` ends it.
 * Inlined (R29): with no bounds checks left in its steps it's small, and a lookup's call to it cost its caller a frame.
 */
/** @tsl.inline */
function seek<K>(
  heads: JsArray<u32>,
  chain: JsArray<u32>,
  keys: JsArray<K>,
  k: K,
  h: u32,
  low: u32,
): u32 {
  const b = heads.length;
  if (b === 0) return NONE;
  let s: u32 = heads.get((h & wrapU32(b - 1)) >>> 0);
  // R29 (D79): i below LINKS is a link's position, which JsMap's claim proves below the keys' and the chain's lengths, so
  // neither read below has a bounds check left at -O1 and -O2.
  let i: u32 = (s - 2) >>> 0;
  while (i < LINKS) {
    if (i < low) return NONE;
    // SAFETY: comparing keys is a question about values: an integer's, identity, or the key's own sameKey.
    if (keySame(keys.get(i), k)) return i;
    s = chain.get(i);
    i = (s - 2) >>> 0;
  }
  return NONE;
}

const NONE: u32 = 0xffffffff;

/** As seek, and takes it out of its chain. */
function unlink<K>(
  heads: JsArray<u32>,
  chain: JsArray<u32>,
  keys: JsArray<K>,
  k: K,
  h: u32,
  low: u32,
): u32 {
  const b = heads.length;
  if (b === 0) return NONE;
  const at: u32 = (h & wrapU32(b - 1)) >>> 0;
  let s: u32 = heads.get(at);
  let prev: u32 = NONE;
  let i: u32 = (s - 2) >>> 0; // as in seek (R29)
  while (i < LINKS) {
    if (i < low) return NONE;
    const next: u32 = chain.get(i);
    // SAFETY: as in seek.
    if (keySame(keys.get(i), k)) {
      if (prev === NONE) heads.set(at, next);
      else chain.set(prev, next);
      chain.set(i, TOMB);
      return i;
    }
    prev = i;
    s = next;
    i = (s - 2) >>> 0;
  }
  return NONE;
}

/**
 * JS's `Map` (D47): `get` of a missing key gives `undefined`, entries are in insertion order, keys are the same by
 * SameValueZero (a number by `jsNumKey`, an object by identity), and changing it during an iteration does what JS does.
 * A key is what @tsl/unsafe's `keyHash` takes: an integer, a reference, or a class or dispatch interface (D70) with
 * `hashKey` and `sameKey`, as `JsString` is. No operation does work proportional to the table: growth moves STEP entries
 * an insert or delete. Lowered programs print their maps as this class (`tmk lower --emit tsl`), and a person can write
 * it too.
 *
 * Both tables' arrays are held in place (R3): the map's own, and the old table's, which a move empties. Starting a move
 * gives the table's buffers to the old table's arrays (`adopt`) and makes the table's again; ending it gives the old
 * buffers back, where the map `freesTables`, and otherwise keeps them, as before R3, in arrays nothing else reads.
 *
 * R29 (D79): every link either table's `heads` and `chain` hold names a position below that table's `keys` and `chain`
 * lengths, which tslc proves over every write to them (compiler/host/links.ts), so a lookup's chain steps have no bounds
 * checks at -O1 and -O2. A table's `chain` is as long as its `heads` (the positions it has room for), not as its `keys`.
 * @tsl.links heads chain < keys chain
 * @tsl.links oheads ochain < okeys ochain
 */
export class JsMap<K, V> {
  private keys: JsArray<K>;
  private vals: JsArray<V>;
  private chain: JsArray<u32>;
  private heads: JsArray<u32>;
  private okeys: JsArray<K>; // the old table's, while a move is on; empty otherwise (R3)
  private ovals: JsArray<V>;
  private ochain: JsArray<u32>;
  private oheads: JsArray<u32>;
  private count: u32 = 0;
  private gen: JsMapGen | null = null;
  private first: JsMapGen | null = null; // the oldest generation, which a cursor may still read (R3)
  private readers: u32 = 0; // cursors open and not yet closed, where the map `freesTables` (R3)
  private moving: bool = false; // a move is on: the old table's arrays hold what it hasn't moved
  private mv: u32 = 0; // the next old position to move
  private end: u32 = 0; // how many positions the old table has
  private to: u32 = 0; // where the next entry moved goes
  private base: u32 = 0; // where what's inserted during the move starts
  private outK!: K; // what `put`, `cut` and `entryAt` handed back (R2)
  private outV!: V;
  private tables: bool = false; // `freesTables`: what it stops holding, and its tables, go back (R2)
  private counted: bool = false; // `tablesIn`: a counted object holds it, so making a table takes freeing steps (R11)

  /**
   * `withVals` false is a Set's table, which keeps no values. `giveBack` false keeps each array it outgrows, as a `leak`
   * package's lowered maps always have (JsArray's).
   */
  constructor(
    private kd: ElemOf<K>,
    private vd: ElemOf<V>,
    private withVals: bool,
    private giveBack: bool,
  ) {
    this.keys = new JsArray(kd, 0, giveBack, true);
    this.vals = new JsArray(vd, 0, giveBack, true);
    this.chain = new JsArray(u32, 0, giveBack, true);
    this.heads = new JsArray(u32, 0, giveBack, true);
    this.okeys = new JsArray(kd, 0, giveBack, true);
    this.ovals = new JsArray(vd, 0, giveBack, true);
    this.ochain = new JsArray(u32, 0, giveBack, true);
    this.oheads = new JsArray(u32, 0, giveBack, true);
  }

  get size(): u32 {
    return this.count;
  }

  /** @tsl.inline */
  private find(k: K, h: u32): u32 {
    return seek(this.heads, this.chain, this.keys, k, h, 0);
  }

  /** Where k is in the old table, if a move is on and hasn't got to it. */
  private findOld(k: K, h: u32): u32 {
    if (!this.moving) return NONE;
    return seek(this.oheads, this.ochain, this.okeys, k, h, this.mv);
  }

  /** `undefined` if the key isn't there. A scalar's is a flag and a value in registers (3.3, rule 12). */
  get(k: K): V | undefined {
    const h = hashOf(k);
    const i = this.find(k, h);
    if (i !== NONE) return this.vals.get(i);
    if (!this.moving) return undefined;
    const j = this.findOld(k, h);
    if (j === NONE) return undefined;
    return this.ovals.get(j);
  }

  /** `otherwise` if the key isn't there: a reference's `get`, with `null` for `undefined`. */
  getOr(k: K, otherwise: V): V {
    const h = hashOf(k);
    const i = this.find(k, h);
    if (i !== NONE) return this.vals.get(i);
    if (!this.moving) return otherwise;
    const j = this.findOld(k, h);
    if (j === NONE) return otherwise;
    return this.ovals.get(j);
  }

  has(k: K): bool {
    const h = hashOf(k);
    return this.find(k, h) !== NONE || this.findOld(k, h) !== NONE;
  }

  set(k: K, v: V): void {
    const h = hashOf(k);
    const i = this.find(k, h);
    if (i !== NONE) {
      this.vals.set(i, v);
      return;
    }
    if (this.moving) {
      const j = this.findOld(k, h);
      if (j !== NONE) {
        this.ovals.set(j, v);
        return;
      }
    }
    this.insert(k, v, h);
  }

  /** A Set's `add`: the key, with no value. */
  add(k: K, none: V): void {
    const h = hashOf(k);
    if (this.find(k, h) === NONE && this.findOld(k, h) === NONE) this.insert(k, none, h);
  }

  private insert(k: K, v: V, h: u32): void {
    if (this.moving) this.steps(STEP);
    if (this.keys.length >= this.heads.length) this.grow();
    const at: u32 = wrapU32(this.keys.length);
    const heads = this.heads;
    const b: u32 = (h & wrapU32(heads.length - 1)) >>> 0;
    this.keys.push(k);
    if (this.withVals) this.vals.push(v);
    const s: u32 = heads.get(b);
    this.chain.set(at, s > END ? s : END);
    heads.set(b, (at + 2) >>> 0);
    this.count = (this.count + 1) >>> 0;
  }

  /**
   * Room for `want` slots in an array emptied by `adopt` or `trim` (R2); `grow` gives each its length once all four have
   * room (R29). Where a counted object holds the map (R11), making it takes the counted heap's freeing steps first, and if
   * @tsl/std has nothing left, everything the counted heap has waiting is freed, its maps' tables with it, before it's
   * asked once more.
   */
  private reserveFor<T>(a: JsArray<T>, want: u32): void {
    if (this.counted && a.capacity < toUsize(want)) {
      const steps = tables.steps;
      steps();
      if (!a.tryReserve(want)) {
        const drain = tables.drain;
        drain();
        a.reserve(want);
      }
    } else a.reserve(want);
  }

  /**
   * An array's buffer let go of without giving it back: what a map that doesn't `freesTables` does with a table it
   * outgrows or clears, which stays allocated, as the direct route's runtime map's does (R3: before, the map made new
   * arrays and kept the old ones; now its arrays are held in place, so the buffer goes to an array nothing else reads,
   * which keeps what it's made with too, as each new array before R3 was kept).
   */
  private forget<T>(d: ElemOf<T>, a: JsArray<T>): void {
    const kept = new JsArray(d, 0, false, true);
    kept.adopt(a);
  }

  /**
   * From now on, what the map stops holding is zeroed where it was, its tables go back as it outgrows or clears them,
   * and its cursors are closed (`close`), so what its iterations, moves and clears make is reused: a lowered `rc`
   * package's map, whose holder counts what it holds and frees it (R2, R3). Otherwise each outgrown or cleared table is
   * kept, as a `leak` or `manual` program's runtime map's is.
   */
  freesTables(): void {
    this.tables = true;
  }

  /**
   * `freesTables`, for a map a counted object holds (R11): each table it makes from here on first takes the freeing steps
   * an allocation of the counted heap takes (`steps`), and where @tsl/std has nothing left, the counted heap frees all it
   * has waiting (`drain`), which gives back the tables of the maps waiting with it, before @tsl/std is asked again. So
   * churning maps frees as the counted heap's own allocations do, and running out of memory means what's live doesn't fit,
   * as the direct route's map's vectors, which are the counted heap's, have it (D39).
   */
  tablesIn(steps: TableSteps, drain: TableSteps): void {
    tables.steps = steps;
    tables.drain = drain;
    this.tables = true;
    this.counted = true;
  }

  /**
   * Full: a new table, with room for twice what's live and for the move to finish before inserts fill it, at STEP old
   * positions each. The new table's buffers are made first, in the old table's arrays, empty since the last move ended,
   * and only then do the two tables swap (R4), so running out of memory while they're made leaves the map as it was; the
   * old table's arrays then hold what's to be moved, and with nothing to move, the old buffers go back (or are kept, as
   * above).
   */
  private grow(): void {
    // Can't happen: the new table has room for the move to finish. If it did, finishing here is correct, if slow.
    if (this.moving) this.steps(this.end);
    const used: u32 = wrapU32(this.keys.length);
    const live: u32 = this.count;
    let need: u32 = (live << 1) >>> 0;
    const forMove: u32 = (live + ((used + STEP - 1) >>> 2) + 1) >>> 0; // STEP is 4
    if (forMove > need) need = forMove;
    let want: u32 = MIN_BUCKETS;
    while (want < need) want = (want << 1) >>> 0;
    this.reserveFor(this.okeys, want);
    this.reserveFor(this.ovals, this.withVals ? want : 0);
    this.reserveFor(this.ochain, want);
    this.reserveFor(this.oheads, want);
    // everything allocated: from here nothing can fail. The old table's arrays are empty, since the last move ended; their
    // lengths, the heads' and chain's first, at 0 so tslc's links proof sees no link in them (R29, D79), then what's live
    // and the room for positions, zero
    this.oheads.setLength(0);
    this.ochain.setLength(0);
    this.okeys.setLength(live);
    this.ovals.setLength(this.withVals ? live : 0);
    this.ochain.setLength(want);
    this.oheads.setLength(want);
    this.keys.swap(this.okeys);
    this.vals.swap(this.ovals);
    this.chain.swap(this.ochain);
    this.heads.swap(this.oheads);
    if (used > 0) this.startMove(used, live);
    else this.oldGone(null);
  }

  /** A generation: one reused where the map `freesTables` and one is free (R3), a new one otherwise. */
  private newGen(): JsMapGen {
    if (!this.tables) return new JsMapGen();
    const g = freeGens;
    if (g === null) return new JsMapGen();
    freeGens = g.next;
    g.next = null;
    return g;
  }

  /** A move starts, of `used` old positions with `live` entries, the old table's arrays holding them. */
  private startMove(used: u32, live: u32): void {
    const g = this.gen;
    if (g !== null) {
      const fresh = this.newGen();
      fresh.live = true;
      fresh.end = used;
      fresh.base = live;
      g.next = fresh;
      this.gen = fresh;
    }
    this.moving = true;
    this.mv = 0;
    this.end = used;
    this.to = 0;
    this.base = live;
  }

  /**
   * The old table's buffers, given back where the map `freesTables` and kept otherwise: its move has ended (R3). First,
   * where its move put each position, in its chain, is taken over by the generation `g` that reads it, if one does (R3).
   * Only the newest generation can: one is made at a move's start, or during it by `genNow`, and nothing makes another
   * until the move ends or the map clears. (R29: one method, so the old chain left empty and the rest of its table gone
   * are one step to tslc's links proof.)
   */
  private oldGone(g: JsMapGen | null): void {
    if (g !== null && g.live) {
      let r = g.keep;
      if (r === null) {
        r = new JsArray(u32, 0, this.giveBack, true);
        if (this.tables) g.keep = r;
      }
      r.adopt(this.ochain);
      g.ranks = r;
      g.live = false;
    }
    if (this.tables) {
      this.okeys.trim();
      this.ovals.trim();
      this.ochain.trim();
      this.oheads.trim();
    } else {
      this.forget(this.kd, this.okeys);
      this.forget(this.vd, this.ovals);
      this.forget(u32, this.ochain);
      this.forget(u32, this.oheads);
    }
    this.moving = false;
  }

  /** Moves up to n old positions, in order: a live entry to the next place at the front, and either way, where it went. */
  private steps(n: u32): void {
    if (!this.moving) return;
    const okeys = this.okeys;
    const ochain = this.ochain;
    let mv: u32 = this.mv;
    const end: u32 = this.end;
    let left: u32 = n;
    while (left > 0 && mv < end) {
      const r: u32 = this.to;
      if (ochain.get(mv) !== TOMB) {
        const k = okeys.get(mv);
        if (this.withVals) this.vals.set(r, this.ovals.get(mv));
        // freesTables (R2): the old table no longer holds what the new one does, as the direct route's clears it
        if (this.tables) {
          okeys.zero(mv);
          if (this.withVals) this.ovals.zero(mv);
        }
        this.link(r, k, hashOf(k));
        this.to = (r + 1) >>> 0;
      }
      ochain.set(mv, (MOVED | r) >>> 0);
      mv = (mv + 1) >>> 0;
      left = (left - 1) >>> 0;
    }
    this.mv = mv;
    // a generation that reads where the move put each position keeps that, and the old table goes (R3)
    if (mv >= end) this.oldGone(this.gen);
  }

  /**
   * A moved entry's key into position r, and r into its chain, below what's been inserted since the move started, so
   * positions still fall. The key is stored here, before any link to r (R29: so r is known below the keys' length).
   */
  private link(r: u32, k: K, h: u32): void {
    this.keys.set(r, k);
    const heads = this.heads;
    const chain = this.chain;
    const b: u32 = (h & wrapU32(heads.length - 1)) >>> 0;
    const s: u32 = heads.get(b);
    if (s <= END || (s - 2) >>> 0 < r) {
      chain.set(r, s > END ? s : END);
      heads.set(b, (r + 2) >>> 0);
      return;
    }
    let p: u32 = (s - 2) >>> 0;
    for (;;) {
      const n: u32 = chain.get(p);
      if (n <= END || (n - 2) >>> 0 < r) {
        chain.set(r, n > END ? n : END);
        chain.set(p, (r + 2) >>> 0);
        return;
      }
      p = (n - 2) >>> 0;
    }
  }

  delete(k: K): bool {
    if (this.moving) this.steps(STEP);
    const h = hashOf(k);
    const i = unlink(this.heads, this.chain, this.keys, k, h, 0);
    if (i !== NONE) {
      this.count = (this.count - 1) >>> 0;
      if (this.tables) this.vacate(this.keys, this.vals, i);
      return true;
    }
    if (!this.moving) return false;
    const j = unlink(this.oheads, this.ochain, this.okeys, k, h, this.mv);
    if (j === NONE) return false;
    this.count = (this.count - 1) >>> 0;
    if (this.tables) this.vacate(this.okeys, this.ovals, j);
    return true;
  }

  /**
   * A position's key and value handed back (`outKey`, `outVal`) and its slots made zero, as the direct route's map clears
   * a slot it stops holding (`__v_clear`), so no table holds what the map no longer does (R2).
   */
  private vacate(keys: JsArray<K>, vals: JsArray<V>, i: usize): void {
    this.outK = keys.get(i);
    keys.zero(i);
    if (this.withVals) {
      this.outV = vals.get(i);
      vals.zero(i);
    }
  }

  /**
   * `set` for a map of counted keys or values (R2): true if it inserted, and then the map holds the key it was given;
   * false if the key was there already, and then the value it replaced is `outVal()`'s.
   */
  put(k: K, v: V): bool {
    const h = hashOf(k);
    const i = this.find(k, h);
    if (i !== NONE) {
      if (this.withVals) {
        this.outV = this.vals.get(i);
        this.vals.set(i, v);
      }
      return false;
    }
    if (this.moving) {
      const j = this.findOld(k, h);
      if (j !== NONE) {
        if (this.withVals) {
          this.outV = this.ovals.get(j);
          this.ovals.set(j, v);
        }
        return false;
      }
    }
    this.insert(k, v, h);
    return true;
  }

  /**
   * `delete`, with the entry handed back: true if it was there, and then its key and value are `outKey()`'s and
   * `outVal()`'s. Only for a map that `freesTables`.
   */
  cut(k: K): bool {
    return this.delete(k);
  }

  /** The key `cut` or `entryAt` last handed back. */
  outKey(): K {
    return this.outK;
  }

  /** The value `put`, `cut` or `entryAt` last handed back. */
  outVal(): V {
    return this.outV;
  }

  /**
   * How many positions the map has, live or not, in its table and, during a move, the old one's not yet moved: freeing a
   * lowered `rc` package's map takes one a step (R2, D39), as the direct route's frees a vector's slot a step.
   */
  positions(): usize {
    const n = this.keys.length;
    return this.moving ? n + toUsize(this.end - this.mv) : n;
  }

  /**
   * Whether position p holds an entry; if it does, its key and value are `outKey()`'s and `outVal()`'s, and with `take`
   * the entry is out of the map, its slots zero. Taking leaves its chain as it was, so a map is only ever taken from as
   * it's freed, and `trim` follows.
   */
  entryAt(p: usize, take: bool): bool {
    const n = this.keys.length;
    if (p < n) {
      if (this.chain.get(p) === TOMB) return false;
      if (!take) return this.peek(this.keys, this.vals, p);
      this.chain.set(p, TOMB);
      this.vacate(this.keys, this.vals, p);
      this.count = (this.count - 1) >>> 0;
      return true;
    }
    if (!this.moving) return false;
    const q: u32 = (this.mv + wrapU32(p - n)) >>> 0;
    if (q >= this.end) return false;
    const s: u32 = this.ochain.get(q);
    if (s === TOMB || s >= MOVED) return false;
    if (!take) return this.peek(this.okeys, this.ovals, q);
    this.ochain.set(q, TOMB);
    this.vacate(this.okeys, this.ovals, q);
    this.count = (this.count - 1) >>> 0;
    return true;
  }

  private peek(keys: JsArray<K>, vals: JsArray<V>, i: usize): bool {
    this.outK = keys.get(i);
    if (this.withVals) this.outV = vals.get(i);
    return true;
  }

  /**
   * Every array's buffer given back, the map left with none: the last step of freeing a lowered `rc` package's map (R2).
   * Both tables' arrays are the map's own (R3), so nothing of it is left behind in @tsl/jsrt but the generations and
   * cursors its iterations closed, which other maps reuse.
   */
  trim(): bool {
    // each array's own call, its result noted: a chain of eight `||`s here once inlined left -O2's cfg pass with
    // unreachable blocks (TIR verifier), R3
    let any = false;
    if (this.okeys.trim()) any = true;
    if (this.ovals.trim()) any = true;
    if (this.ochain.trim()) any = true;
    if (this.oheads.trim()) any = true;
    this.moving = false;
    if (this.keys.trim()) any = true;
    if (this.vals.trim()) any = true;
    if (this.chain.trim()) any = true;
    if (this.heads.trim()) any = true;
    this.count = 0;
    return any;
  }

  /** Emptied: what the tables held isn't reachable from here any more. */
  clear(): void {
    const g = this.gen;
    if (g !== null) {
      g.cleared = true;
      const fresh = this.newGen();
      g.next = fresh;
      this.gen = fresh;
    }
    // a move on: a generation that read the old chain keeps where the move put each position (R3)
    if (this.moving) this.oldGone(g);
    if (this.tables) {
      // freesTables (R2): emptied in place, its buffers back
      this.keys.trim();
      this.vals.trim();
      this.chain.trim();
      this.heads.trim();
    } else {
      // kept, as before R3, and the arrays made again as new ones are, with room for 4
      this.forget(this.kd, this.keys);
      this.forget(this.vd, this.vals);
      this.forget(u32, this.chain);
      this.forget(u32, this.heads);
      this.keys.reserve(4);
      this.vals.reserve(4);
      this.chain.reserve(4);
      this.heads.reserve(4);
    }
    this.count = 0;
    this.mv = 0;
    this.end = 0;
    this.to = 0;
    this.base = 0;
  }

  private genNow(): JsMapGen {
    const g = this.gen;
    if (g !== null) return g;
    const fresh = this.newGen();
    if (this.moving) {
      fresh.live = true;
      fresh.end = this.end;
      fresh.base = this.base;
    }
    this.gen = fresh;
    this.first = fresh;
    return fresh;
  }

  /**
   * A cursor before the first entry: `advance` moves it on, and `keyAt` and `valAt` read where it stopped. Where the map
   * `freesTables`, it's open until `close` (R3), and one closed before is reused.
   */
  cursor(): JsMapCursor {
    if (!this.tables) return new JsMapCursor(this.genNow());
    const g = this.genNow();
    this.readers = (this.readers + 1) >>> 0;
    const c = freeCursors;
    if (c === null) return new JsMapCursor(g);
    freeCursors = c.link;
    c.link = null;
    c.gen = g;
    c.pos = 0;
    c.cur = 0;
    c.done = false;
    c.inOld = false;
    c.curOld = false;
    return c;
  }

  /**
   * An iteration over, where the map `freesTables` (R3): tslc's expansion closes each cursor of a lowered `rc` package's
   * map where its variable's scope ends, by every way out, so `c` isn't used again. With none left open no cursor can
   * read a generation, so they're reused, and an old chain one kept goes back. Otherwise nothing: a cursor that's
   * dropped costs nothing more, as before.
   */
  close(c: JsMapCursor): void {
    if (!this.tables || this.readers === 0) return;
    c.link = freeCursors;
    freeCursors = c;
    this.readers = (this.readers - 1) >>> 0;
    if (this.readers === 0) this.retire();
  }

  /** Every generation free to reuse, its ranks given back: no cursor of this map is open (R3). */
  private retire(): void {
    let g = this.first;
    while (g !== null) {
      const n = g.next;
      const k = g.keep;
      if (k !== null) k.trim();
      g.ranks = null;
      g.live = false;
      g.cleared = false;
      g.end = 0;
      g.base = 0;
      g.next = freeGens;
      freeGens = g;
      g = n;
    }
    this.first = null;
    this.gen = null;
  }

  /** Where old position q went, once the move has passed it: in the old chain while it's the map's, else in `ranks`. */
  private rankOf(g: JsMapGen, q: u32): u32 {
    if (q >= g.end) return g.base;
    if (g.live) return (this.ochain.get(q) & ~MOVED) >>> 0;
    const r = g.ranks;
    if (r === null) return 0;
    return (r.get(q) & ~MOVED) >>> 0;
  }

  /**
   * The next live entry, by JS's rules: what's added is seen, what's deleted isn't, and once finished it stays finished.
   * During a move, the entries not yet moved are in the old table, between what's been moved and what's been inserted
   * since.
   */
  advance(c: JsMapCursor): bool {
    if (c.done) return false;
    let pos: u32 = c.pos;
    let g = c.gen;
    let inOld = c.inOld;
    // To the newest generation. A move made each one after the first, unless the one before it was cleared.
    for (;;) {
      const n = g.next;
      if (n !== null && g.cleared) {
        pos = 0;
        inOld = false;
        g = n;
        continue;
      }
      if (inOld) {
        if (n !== null || !this.moving) {
          pos = this.rankOf(g, pos);
          inOld = false;
        } else if (pos < this.mv) {
          pos = this.rankOf(g, pos);
          inOld = false;
        }
      }
      if (n === null) break;
      inOld = true;
      g = n;
    }
    c.gen = g;
    for (;;) {
      const moving = this.moving;
      if (inOld && moving) {
        const end: u32 = this.end;
        while (pos < end) {
          const s: u32 = this.ochain.get(pos);
          if (s !== TOMB && s < MOVED) {
            c.cur = pos;
            c.curOld = true;
            c.pos = (pos + 1) >>> 0;
            c.inOld = true;
            return true;
          }
          pos = (pos + 1) >>> 0;
        }
        pos = this.base;
      }
      inOld = false;
      const used: u32 = wrapU32(this.keys.length);
      while (pos < used) {
        if (moving && pos === this.to && pos < this.base) {
          // What hasn't moved yet comes next: it's in the old table, from the move's place on.
          pos = this.mv;
          inOld = true;
          break;
        }
        if (this.chain.get(pos) !== TOMB) {
          c.cur = pos;
          c.curOld = false;
          c.pos = (pos + 1) >>> 0;
          c.inOld = false;
          return true;
        }
        pos = (pos + 1) >>> 0;
      }
      if (!inOld) break;
    }
    c.pos = pos;
    c.inOld = false;
    c.done = true;
    return false;
  }

  /** The key where `advance` last stopped. */
  keyAt(c: JsMapCursor): K {
    if (c.curOld && this.moving) return this.okeys.get(c.cur);
    return this.keys.get(c.cur);
  }

  /** The value where `advance` last stopped. */
  valAt(c: JsMapCursor): V {
    if (c.curOld && this.moving) return this.ovals.get(c.cur);
    return this.vals.get(c.cur);
  }

  /** `forEach`, value first as JS has it, with JS's rules for what the callback adds and deletes. */
  forEach(f: (v: V, k: K) => void): void {
    const c = this.cursor();
    while (this.advance(c)) f(this.valAt(c), this.keyAt(c));
    this.close(c);
  }
}

/**
 * JS's `Set` (D47): a JsMap's table with no values, so changing it during an iteration does what JS does, and growth is
 * as incremental.
 */
export class JsSet<K> {
  private m: JsMap<K, u8>;

  constructor(kd: ElemOf<K>, giveBack: bool) {
    this.m = new JsMap(kd, u8, false, giveBack);
  }

  get size(): u32 {
    return this.m.size;
  }

  has(k: K): bool {
    return this.m.has(k);
  }

  add(k: K): void {
    this.m.add(k, 0);
  }

  delete(k: K): bool {
    return this.m.delete(k);
  }

  clear(): void {
    this.m.clear();
  }

  /** As JsMap's (R2). */
  freesTables(): void {
    this.m.freesTables();
  }

  /** As JsMap's (R11). */
  tablesIn(steps: TableSteps, drain: TableSteps): void {
    this.m.tablesIn(steps, drain);
  }

  /** `add` for a set of counted keys (R2): true if it inserted, and then the set holds the key it was given. */
  put(k: K): bool {
    return this.m.put(k, 0);
  }

  /** `delete`, with the key handed back as `outKey()`'s. */
  cut(k: K): bool {
    return this.m.cut(k);
  }

  outKey(): K {
    return this.m.outKey();
  }

  positions(): usize {
    return this.m.positions();
  }

  entryAt(p: usize, take: bool): bool {
    return this.m.entryAt(p, take);
  }

  trim(): bool {
    return this.m.trim();
  }

  cursor(): JsMapCursor {
    return this.m.cursor();
  }

  /** As JsMap's (R3). */
  close(c: JsMapCursor): void {
    this.m.close(c);
  }

  advance(c: JsMapCursor): bool {
    return this.m.advance(c);
  }

  keyAt(c: JsMapCursor): K {
    return this.m.keyAt(c);
  }

  forEach(f: (k: K) => void): void {
    const c = this.m.cursor();
    while (this.m.advance(c)) f(this.m.keyAt(c));
    this.m.close(c);
  }
}
```

`JsString` (D67), in `@tsl/jsrt`: a JS string, D42's representation in TSL, which class printing prints a lowered program's strings as (4.5), and which a person can write too. `@tsl/jsrt` is a `leak` package, so what it makes is never freed and a method can return a new string; in a lowered build it takes the build's mode, as every function there does. Units are UTF-16 with lone surrogates kept; a string is flat or a view, concatenation appends in place at a buffer's tail, and a substring shares only from 32 units and a quarter of what it keeps alive.

```ts
// file: ex-jsrt-string.ts
import {
  tail,
  toI32,
  toU64,
  toUsize,
  Trap,
  trap,
  u16,
  withTail,
  wrapI32,
  wrapU16,
  wrapU32,
  type bool,
  type i32,
  type u32,
  type u64,
  type usize,
} from "@tsl/core";
import { copyBytes, ptrAt, ref, sourcePages, tailAddr } from "@tsl/unsafe";
import { jsUnitsHash } from "./ex-jsrt-map.ts";

const MAX_LEN: i32 = 536870888; // V8's limit; JS throws RangeError past it, which the caller checks for first
const SHARE_MIN: i32 = 32; // shorter than this, a substring copies
const CONCAT_FLAT_MAX: i32 = 64; // this short, concatenation always copies
const GROWN: i32 = 2; // in `hw`: made by concatenation, so a second append makes a buffer

// A string is one of two classes behind the dispatch interface `JsString` (D70): `JsFlat`, its units its own tail (D69),
// or `JsView`, which reads units another object owns. What a view reads is a `JsOwner`: a flat string, or a `JsBuf`, a
// concatenation's buffer, which is never a string itself. Nothing a string holds is freed in `leak` or `manual` (3.5,
// D42), and a buffer outgrown by concatenation stays for the views made into it. The one-unit table has its own page.

// A count or index of units, from 0 to MAX_LEN, in bytes: below 2^30 twice over, so nothing here can overflow, and
// there's nothing to check (`toUsize(n) * 2` would check it twice).
function bytesOf(n: i32): u64 {
  return toU64((n << 1) >>> 0);
}

// SAFETY: both runs are units of live strings, n of them, within the strings' lengths (each caller checks).
function copyUnits(to: u64, from: u64, n: i32): void {
  if (n > 0) copyBytes(to, from, toUsize(bytesOf(n)));
}

// SAFETY: i is below the length of the units at p, which the caller has checked.
function unitAt(p: u64, i: usize): i32 {
  return ptrAt(u16, p).add(i).read();
}

let empty: JsFlat | null = null;
let chars: u64 = 0n; // 256 references, null until each one-unit string is made

/**
 * A JavaScript string (D42, D67): immutable UTF-16 code units, lone surrogates kept, one reference. Each is a `JsFlat`
 * or a `JsView`, told apart by a class id (D70); a call on one is a compare of its id and a direct call. Concatenation
 * appends in place where the left side ends at its buffer's end, so `s += x` in a loop is linear with no flattening. A
 * substring shares only when it's at least a quarter of what it would keep alive. Lowered programs print their strings
 * as this interface (`tmk lower --emit tsl`).
 */
export interface JsString {
  /** The length in units. */
  len(): i32;
  /** The code unit at i, which is below the length (`charCodeAt` past it is JS's NaN, and the caller says so). */
  unit(i: usize): i32;
  /** Writes unit i of a string `JsFlat.zeroed` just made, before anything else has it: strings are immutable after. */
  put(i: usize, u: i32): void;
  /** Copies n units of s from si into this string, made by `JsFlat.zeroed` and no one else's yet, from di. */
  copyFrom(di: usize, s: JsString, si: usize, n: usize): void;
  /** The address of units si to si + n, which are checked to be within it: a run of reads after one class test. */
  unitsAt(si: usize, n: usize): u64;
  /** How many units the code point at i takes, 1 or 2: `for...of` steps by these. A lone surrogate is one. */
  cpLen(i: i32): i32;
  /** `this + b`, whose length the caller has checked is within JS's (it throws RangeError past it). */
  concat(b: JsString): JsString;
  /** `a + this`, `concat`'s second step, once a's class is known. */
  concatOntoFlat(a: JsFlat): JsString;
  /** `a + this`, likewise. */
  concatOntoView(a: JsView): JsString;
  /** The n units from i, which are within it. */
  sub(i: i32, n: i32): JsString;
  /** By code unit, as JS orders strings: negative, zero or positive. */
  compare(b: JsString): i32;
  /** D42's hash word: bit 0 when the hash is known, the hash in the bits above 1, and GROWN. compiler/rt's strHash. */
  hashWord(): i32;
  /** Keeps the hash word strHash worked out; how the string was made (GROWN) stays the class's own. */
  setHashWord(w: i32): void;
  /** Whether this reads another object's units, a view (D42): what tests of the sharing bound look at. */
  isView(): bool;
  /** Unit 0's address, where a native caller writes a string argument's units (`__str_units`, 4.5). */
  unitsAddr(): u64;
  /** A map key's hash (D72): D42's keyed HalfSipHash of the units, kept in the hash word. `keyHash` calls it. */
  hashKey(): u32;
  /** A map key's equality: the same units, as JS's `===`. `keySame` calls it. */
  sameKey(b: JsString): bool;
  /** Whether its units are the n at p, where hw, the other string's hash word, may say no first: sameKey's second step. */
  sameUnits(p: u64, n: i32, hw: i32): bool;
}

/** What a view reads units from: a flat string, or a concatenation's buffer. Only a buffer has room to grow into. */
export interface JsOwner {
  /** How many units it holds, used or not: what a view of it keeps alive. */
  room(): i32;
  /** Appends n units from `from` at `at`, if at is where its used units end and there's room: whether it did. */
  appendAt(at: i32, from: u64, n: i32): bool;
  /** Puts n units from `from` just before `head`, if head is where its used units start and there's room. */
  prependAt(head: i32, from: u64, n: i32): bool;
}

/** `a === b` for strings that may be `undefined` (null): the same units, or both missing. */
export function jsEq(a: JsString | null, b: JsString | null): bool {
  if (a === b) return true;
  if (a === null || b === null) return false;
  const n = a.len();
  if (n !== b.len()) return false;
  const pa = a.unitsAt(0, toUsize(n));
  const pb = b.unitsAt(0, toUsize(n));
  for (let i: usize = 0; i < toUsize(n); i++) if (unitAt(pa, i) !== unitAt(pb, i)) return false;
  return true;
}

/** A hash word strHash worked out, with how the string was made (GROWN) kept from the word it had. */
function keptHash(w: i32, hw: i32): i32 {
  return (w & ~GROWN) | (hw & GROWN);
}

/** The hash word that keeps h, a key's hash jsUnitsHash worked out (D72), and how the string was made from hw. */
function hashWordOf(h: u32, hw: i32): i32 {
  return keptHash(wrapI32((h << 2) >>> 0) | 1, hw);
}

/** Two strings' units the same, by JS's `===`; two hash words that both have the hash and differ say no first. */
// SAFETY: la and lb are the lengths of the units at pa and pb.
function unitsSame(pa: u64, la: i32, ha: i32, pb: u64, lb: i32, hb: i32): bool {
  if (la !== lb) return false;
  if ((ha & hb & 1) !== 0 && (ha | 3) !== (hb | 3)) return false;
  if (pa === pb) return true;
  for (let i: usize = 0; i < toUsize(la); i++) if (unitAt(pa, i) !== unitAt(pb, i)) return false;
  return true;
}

// SAFETY: n is p's length, so i and i + 1 are read only below it.
function cpLenAt(p: u64, n: i32, i: i32): i32 {
  if (i < 0 || i >= n) trap(Trap.Bounds);
  const c = unitAt(p, toUsize(i));
  if (c < 0xd800 || c > 0xdbff || i + 1 >= n) return 1;
  const d = unitAt(p, toUsize(i + 1));
  return d >= 0xdc00 && d <= 0xdfff ? 2 : 1;
}

// SAFETY: la and lb are the lengths of the units at pa and pb.
function compareAt(pa: u64, la: i32, pb: u64, lb: i32): i32 {
  const n = la < lb ? la : lb;
  for (let i: usize = 0; i < toUsize(n); i++) {
    const d = unitAt(pa, i) - unitAt(pb, i);
    if (d !== 0) return d;
  }
  return la - lb;
}

/**
 * `a + b` once both classes are known: la and pa are a's length and units, av is a when it's a view, and likewise for b;
 * ga and gb say whether each was made by concatenation. Inlined into each of the four pairs, where the nulls fold.
 */
/** @tsl.inline */
// SAFETY: an append writes past a buffer's end or before its head, which no view reads (each reads only its own n
// units), and only where it's within the buffer's room.
function joinParts(
  a: JsString,
  la: i32,
  pa: u64,
  av: JsView | null,
  ga: bool,
  b: JsString,
  lb: i32,
  pb: u64,
  bv: JsView | null,
  gb: bool,
): JsString {
  if (la === 0) return b;
  if (lb === 0) return a;
  // The caller has checked n against MAX_LEN (JS's RangeError): not again here (pipe-dispatch). Past it, nothing is
  // written out of bounds: a buffer is at least n, and an append in place checks its room.
  const n = la + lb;
  if (n <= CONCAT_FLAT_MAX) return JsFlat.joined(pa, la, pb, lb);
  if (av !== null && av.owner.appendAt(av.start + la, pb, lb))
    return JsView.grown(av.owner, av.start, n, pa);
  if (bv !== null && bv.owner.prependAt(bv.start, pa, la))
    return JsView.grown(bv.owner, bv.start - la, n, pb - bytesOf(la));
  if (!ga && !gb) return JsFlat.joined(pa, la, pb, lb);
  // The second append to the same string: from here on it pays to have room. Doubling makes it linear in all.
  const cap = n >= 268435456 ? (n > MAX_LEN ? n : MAX_LEN) : n * 2;
  const buf = withTail(toUsize(cap), new JsBuf());
  const at = ga ? 0 : cap - n;
  const base = buf.unitsAddr();
  copyUnits(base + bytesOf(at), pa, la);
  copyUnits(base + bytesOf(at + la), pb, lb);
  buf.head = at;
  buf.end = at + n;
  return JsView.grown(buf, at, n, base + bytesOf(at));
}

/**
 * A flat string: its units are its own tail (D69), one allocation of 12 bytes and its units (the class id, the hash word
 * and the tail's length, which is the string's). As an owner it has no room past its units, so nothing is ever appended
 * to it in place.
 */
export class JsFlat {
  hw: i32 = 0; // GROWN, or nothing: what D42's hash word says of how it was made; the module's own
  private units = tail(u16);

  /** `n` units, each zero, for a builder to `put` and `copyFrom` into before anyone else sees it. */
  /** @tsl.inline */
  static zeroed(n: i32): JsFlat {
    if (n < 0 || n > MAX_LEN) trap(Trap.OutOfMemory);
    return withTail(toUsize(n), new JsFlat());
  }

  /** A literal from its UTF-8 bytes: the text as JS has it, for every literal that's well-formed UTF-16. */
  // SAFETY: the count pass and the writing pass decode the same bytes the same way, so k never passes n.
  static of(bytes: Uint8Array): JsFlat {
    let n: i32 = 0;
    for (let i: usize = 0; i < bytes.length; i++) {
      const b = bytes[i]!;
      if (b < 0x80 || b >= 0xc0) n += b >= 0xf0 ? 2 : 1;
    }
    const s = JsFlat.zeroed(n);
    let k: i32 = 0;
    let i: usize = 0;
    while (i < bytes.length) {
      const b = toI32(bytes[i]!);
      let c: i32 = b;
      let more: usize = 0;
      if (b >= 0xf0) {
        c = b & 7;
        more = 3;
      } else if (b >= 0xe0) {
        c = b & 15;
        more = 2;
      } else if (b >= 0xc0) {
        c = b & 31;
        more = 1;
      }
      for (let j: usize = 1; j <= more; j++) c = (c << 6) | (toI32(bytes[i + j]!) & 63);
      i += more + 1;
      if (c >= 0x10000) {
        s.put(toUsize(k), 0xd800 + ((c - 0x10000) >> 10));
        s.put(toUsize(k + 1), 0xdc00 + ((c - 0x10000) & 0x3ff));
        k += 2;
      } else {
        s.put(toUsize(k), c);
        k += 1;
      }
    }
    return s;
  }

  /** A literal from its units, for one UTF-8 can't say: a lone surrogate. */
  static ofUnits(u: Uint16Array): JsFlat {
    const s = JsFlat.zeroed(toI32(u.length));
    for (let i: usize = 0; i < u.length; i++) s.put(i, toI32(u[i]!));
    return s;
  }

  /** The string of one unit: below 256, one kept string each, as JS engines keep them. */
  /** @tsl.inline */
  // SAFETY: u is below 256, so its slot is in the table, which holds only these strings or null.
  static ofUnit(u: i32): JsFlat {
    const tab = chars;
    if (tab !== 0n && u >= 0 && u < 256) {
      const slot = ptrAt(ref<JsFlat | null>(), tab).add(toUsize(u >>> 0));
      const had = slot.read();
      if (had !== null) return had;
    }
    return JsFlat.unitMade(u);
  }

  // SAFETY: as ofUnit; the table is a zeroed page no one else has, from the registered page source (3.8), never given
  // back, so every slot starts null.
  // Never inlined: it's the table's miss, and a copy of its checks in each caller made `ofUnit`'s callers too big to
  // inline themselves (pipe-h).
  /** @tsl.noinline */
  private static unitMade(u: i32): JsFlat {
    if (u >= 0 && u < 256) {
      if (chars === 0n) {
        const page = sourcePages(1);
        if (page === 0n) trap(Trap.OutOfMemory);
        chars = page;
      }
      const slot = ptrAt(ref<JsFlat | null>(), chars).add(toUsize(u >>> 0));
      const had = slot.read();
      if (had !== null) return had;
      const c = JsFlat.zeroed(1);
      c.put(0, u);
      slot.write(c);
      return c;
    }
    const s = JsFlat.zeroed(1);
    s.put(0, u);
    return s;
  }

  /** `""`, one string of none. */
  static empty(): JsFlat {
    const e = empty;
    if (e !== null) return e;
    const s = JsFlat.zeroed(0);
    empty = s;
    return s;
  }

  /** la units at pa and lb at pb, copied into a new flat string made by concatenation. */
  /** @tsl.inline */
  // SAFETY: the runs are la and lb units of live strings, and the new string holds la + lb.
  static joined(pa: u64, la: i32, pb: u64, lb: i32): JsFlat {
    const r = JsFlat.zeroed(la + lb);
    const p = r.unitsAddr();
    copyUnits(p, pa, la);
    copyUnits(p + bytesOf(la), pb, lb);
    r.hw = GROWN;
    return r;
  }

  len(): i32 {
    return wrapI32(this.units.length); // at most MAX_LEN, as `zeroed` made it
  }

  // SAFETY: a flat string's units are its own tail, which lives as long as it does.
  unitsAddr(): u64 {
    return tailAddr(this);
  }

  // SAFETY: i is below the length, so the unit is in this string's units.
  unit(i: usize): i32 {
    if (i >= this.units.length) trap(Trap.Bounds);
    return unitAt(this.unitsAddr(), i);
  }

  // SAFETY: i is below the length, so the unit is in this string's own units.
  put(i: usize, u: i32): void {
    if (i >= this.units.length) trap(Trap.Bounds);
    ptrAt(u16, this.unitsAddr()).add(i).write(wrapU16(u));
  }

  // SAFETY: both ranges are checked to be within their strings, s's by unitsAt.
  copyFrom(di: usize, s: JsString, si: usize, n: usize): void {
    if (di + n > this.units.length) trap(Trap.Bounds);
    const from = s.unitsAt(si, n);
    if (n > 0) copyBytes(ptrAt(u16, this.unitsAddr()).add(di).addr, from, n * 2);
  }

  // SAFETY: the range is checked to be within the units.
  unitsAt(si: usize, n: usize): u64 {
    if (si + n > this.units.length) trap(Trap.Bounds);
    return ptrAt(u16, this.unitsAddr()).add(si).addr;
  }

  cpLen(i: i32): i32 {
    return cpLenAt(this.unitsAddr(), this.len(), i);
  }

  /** @tsl.inline */
  concat(b: JsString): JsString {
    return b.concatOntoFlat(this);
  }

  /** @tsl.inline */
  concatOntoFlat(a: JsFlat): JsString {
    const ga = (a.hw & GROWN) !== 0;
    const gb = (this.hw & GROWN) !== 0;
    return joinParts(
      a,
      a.len(),
      a.unitsAddr(),
      null,
      ga,
      this,
      this.len(),
      this.unitsAddr(),
      null,
      gb,
    );
  }

  /** @tsl.inline */
  concatOntoView(a: JsView): JsString {
    const ga = (a.hw & GROWN) !== 0;
    const gb = (this.hw & GROWN) !== 0;
    return joinParts(a, a.n, a.data, a, ga, this, this.len(), this.unitsAddr(), null, gb);
  }

  /** A view keeps its owner alive, so only one at least a quarter of it shares. */
  sub(i: i32, n: i32): JsString {
    const len = this.len();
    if (i < 0 || n < 0 || i + n > len) trap(Trap.Bounds);
    if (n === len) return this;
    if (n === 0) return JsFlat.empty();
    const p = this.unitsAddr();
    if (n === 1) return JsFlat.ofUnit(unitAt(p, toUsize(i)));
    if (n >= SHARE_MIN && n * 4 >= len) return new JsView(n, i, p + bytesOf(i), this);
    const r = JsFlat.zeroed(n);
    copyUnits(r.unitsAddr(), p + bytesOf(i), n);
    return r;
  }

  compare(b: JsString): i32 {
    const lb = b.len();
    const la = this.len();
    return compareAt(this.unitsAddr(), la, b.unitsAt(0, toUsize(la < lb ? la : lb)), lb);
  }

  hashWord(): i32 {
    return this.hw;
  }

  setHashWord(w: i32): void {
    this.hw = keptHash(w, this.hw);
  }

  hashKey(): u32 {
    const w = this.hw;
    if ((w & 1) !== 0) return wrapU32(w) >>> 2; // the hash is known
    const h = jsUnitsHash(this.unitsAddr(), this.len());
    this.hw = hashWordOf(h, w);
    return h;
  }

  sameKey(b: JsString): bool {
    return b.sameUnits(this.unitsAddr(), this.len(), this.hw);
  }

  sameUnits(p: u64, n: i32, hw: i32): bool {
    return unitsSame(this.unitsAddr(), this.len(), this.hw, p, n, hw);
  }

  isView(): bool {
    return false;
  }

  room(): i32 {
    return this.len();
  }

  /** A flat string has no room past its units: nothing is appended to it in place. */
  appendAt(_at: i32, _from: u64, _n: i32): bool {
    return false;
  }

  /** Nor before them. */
  prependAt(_head: i32, _from: u64, _n: i32): bool {
    return false;
  }
}

/**
 * A view: n units another object owns, from its unit `start`, at `data`. 32 bytes: the class id, the hash word, the
 * length, the start, unit 0's address and the owner. Its fields are the module's own, and never change after it's made
 * but for the hash word.
 */
export class JsView {
  hw: i32 = 0; // GROWN, or nothing, and strHash's cache
  constructor(
    public n: i32, // the length in units
    public start: i32, // the first unit in its owner
    public data: u64, // unit 0's address, in its owner's units
    public owner: JsOwner, // the flat string or buffer whose units it reads
  ) {}

  /** A view made by concatenation, into a buffer that may have room for the next append. */
  /** @tsl.inline */
  static grown(owner: JsOwner, at: i32, n: i32, data: u64): JsView {
    const r = new JsView(n, at, data, owner);
    r.hw = GROWN;
    return r;
  }

  len(): i32 {
    return this.n;
  }

  unitsAddr(): u64 {
    return this.data;
  }

  // SAFETY: i is below n, so the unit is in the units this view reads.
  unit(i: usize): i32 {
    if (i >= toUsize(this.n >>> 0)) trap(Trap.Bounds);
    return unitAt(this.data, i);
  }

  /** A view has no units of its own to write: every index is past them. */
  put(_i: usize, _u: i32): void {
    trap(Trap.Bounds);
  }

  /** Likewise. */
  copyFrom(_di: usize, _s: JsString, _si: usize, _n: usize): void {
    trap(Trap.Bounds);
  }

  // SAFETY: the range is checked to be within the units this view reads.
  unitsAt(si: usize, n: usize): u64 {
    if (si + n > toUsize(this.n >>> 0)) trap(Trap.Bounds);
    return ptrAt(u16, this.data).add(si).addr;
  }

  cpLen(i: i32): i32 {
    return cpLenAt(this.data, this.n, i);
  }

  /** @tsl.inline */
  concat(b: JsString): JsString {
    return b.concatOntoView(this);
  }

  /** @tsl.inline */
  concatOntoFlat(a: JsFlat): JsString {
    const ga = (a.hw & GROWN) !== 0;
    const gb = (this.hw & GROWN) !== 0;
    return joinParts(a, a.len(), a.unitsAddr(), null, ga, this, this.n, this.data, this, gb);
  }

  /** @tsl.inline */
  concatOntoView(a: JsView): JsString {
    const ga = (a.hw & GROWN) !== 0;
    const gb = (this.hw & GROWN) !== 0;
    return joinParts(a, a.n, a.data, a, ga, this, this.n, this.data, this, gb);
  }

  /** A view of a view is judged against, and reads, the first owner: what a share would keep alive is all of it. */
  sub(i: i32, n: i32): JsString {
    const len = this.n;
    if (i < 0 || n < 0 || i + n > len) trap(Trap.Bounds);
    if (n === len) return this;
    if (n === 0) return JsFlat.empty();
    if (n === 1) return JsFlat.ofUnit(unitAt(this.data, toUsize(i)));
    if (n >= SHARE_MIN) {
      const room = this.owner.room();
      if (n * 4 >= room) return new JsView(n, this.start + i, this.data + bytesOf(i), this.owner);
    }
    const r = JsFlat.zeroed(n);
    copyUnits(r.unitsAddr(), this.data + bytesOf(i), n);
    return r;
  }

  compare(b: JsString): i32 {
    const lb = b.len();
    const la = this.n;
    return compareAt(this.data, la, b.unitsAt(0, toUsize(la < lb ? la : lb)), lb);
  }

  hashWord(): i32 {
    return this.hw;
  }

  setHashWord(w: i32): void {
    this.hw = keptHash(w, this.hw);
  }

  hashKey(): u32 {
    const w = this.hw;
    if ((w & 1) !== 0) return wrapU32(w) >>> 2; // the hash is known
    const h = jsUnitsHash(this.data, this.n);
    this.hw = hashWordOf(h, w);
    return h;
  }

  sameKey(b: JsString): bool {
    return b.sameUnits(this.data, this.n, this.hw);
  }

  sameUnits(p: u64, n: i32, hw: i32): bool {
    return unitsSame(this.data, this.n, this.hw, p, n, hw);
  }

  isView(): bool {
    return true;
  }
}

/**
 * A concatenation's buffer: room for units in its tail, of which those from `head` to `end` are used, by views only. It
 * is never a string, so only a view reaches it, and appends and prepends write outside what any view of it reads.
 */
export class JsBuf {
  head: i32 = 0; // the first unit used; the module's own
  end: i32 = 0; // one past the last unit used
  private units = tail(u16);

  // SAFETY: the buffer's units are its own tail, which lives as long as it does.
  unitsAddr(): u64 {
    const base = tailAddr(this);
    return base;
  }

  room(): i32 {
    return wrapI32(this.units.length); // at most MAX_LEN or the result's length, as `joinParts` made it
  }

  // SAFETY: at + n is within the room, and past every unit a view of this buffer reads.
  appendAt(at: i32, from: u64, n: i32): bool {
    if (at === this.end && at + n <= this.room()) {
      copyUnits(this.unitsAddr() + bytesOf(at), from, n);
      this.end = at + n;
      return true;
    }
    return false;
  }

  // SAFETY: head - n is at least 0, and before every unit a view of this buffer reads.
  prependAt(head: i32, from: u64, n: i32): bool {
    if (head === this.head && head >= n) {
      const h = head - n;
      copyUnits(this.unitsAddr() + bytesOf(h), from, n);
      this.head = h;
      return true;
    }
    return false;
  }
}
```

`Slab`:

```ts
// file: ex-std-slab.ts
import { Slab as AllocSlab } from "@tsl/alloc";
import { Trap, trap, type usize } from "@tsl/core";
import { heap } from "./ex-std-global.ts";

const CHUNK_SLOTS: usize = 32;

/** Where an object lives in `strict` if it has to outlive a call: `@tsl/alloc`'s Slab over the global allocator. */
export class Slab<T extends object> {
  private s: AllocSlab<T> = new AllocSlab<T>(heap, CHUNK_SLOTS);

  get size(): usize {
    return this.s.size;
  }

  /** @tsl.moves item */
  add(item: T): T {
    const placed = this.s.add(item);
    if (placed === null) trap(Trap.OutOfMemory);
    return placed;
  }

  /** @tsl.moves item */
  tryAdd(item: T): T | null {
    return this.s.add(item);
  }

  /** Every stored reference to it traps 5 from now on. Traps 5 if it isn't in this Slab. */
  remove(item: T): void {
    this.s.remove(item);
  }

  forEach(f: (item: T) => void): void {
    this.s.forEach(f);
  }
}
```
