## 8. Testing and verification

### 8.1 Test layers

| Layer | What | Runner |
|-------|------|-------|
| `corpus/pos/` | Each program + a sibling `<name>.cases.json`, run on V8, JSC, Wasm (V8), Wasm (JSC), C backend (native on host via clang, from M3), AArch64 (QEMU, from M5) | `tmk corpus` |
| `corpus/neg/` | Must-fail programs. Each has `// expect: TSL3001 at 12:5`. Exact code and position. | `tmk corpus --neg` |
| `corpus/trap/` | Programs that must trap with a given code on every backend and under `js-checked` | `tmk corpus --trap` |
| `rc`'s own (`tools/rc-tests.ts`, `tools/rc-fuzz.ts`) | Test builds of the counted heap under QEMU: live counts across repeats, a poisoning build with a fault injected to show it fires, steps per allocation, `corpus/lower/rc-only`'s pinned results, and random programs against V8. For the collector, user code between every step at every budget, and faults put into it, which have to be caught | `tmk milestone native-d`, `native-e` |
| Exceptions and classes (`corpus/lower/exc`, `tools/exc-gen.ts`, `tools/exc-fuzz.ts`) | Programs in every memory mode against V8: application-shaped ones, every kind of frame and thrown value, runtime errors, and the generated tests of every way out of every position of a `try` nested in every position of another. Random programs with `try`, `catch`, `finally`, closures, overriding methods and counted objects, in the poisoning build at small freeing budgets, and with nothing alive after a reset. Injected faults in the exception pass and the class representation, which have to be caught | `tmk milestone lang-a`, `tmk exc-gen` |
| `tir/` unit tests | Verifier accept and reject; canonical round trip: parse(print(x)) = x; each pass preserves semantics on TIR samples via a TIR interpreter | `node --test` |
| `tslfuzz` (from M3) | Generates random terminating well-typed TSL programs (Csmith-style [P21]) with checksummed outputs. Differential across all backends. | `tmk fuzz --seconds N --seed S` |
| Pass-disable | Run corpus and fuzz at `-O0`, `-O1`, and with each pass off. Divergence means a bad pass. As built (phase A): every corpus at `-O0` and `-O2` and the quick tier at `-O1` through `TMK_OPT`, and random TIR with each pass off by name | `tmk milestone opt-a`; `tmk corpus -O2`, `--no-pass p` |
| The optimiser's own (`tools/tir-fuzz.ts`, `tools/opt-tests.ts`, `compiler/tir/passes/passes.test.ts`) | Random TIR, which reaches what source can't (several results, calls through pointers, recursion, every trap, frame slots, switches, constants at each type's edges), run natively at `-O0`, `-O1` and `-O2` and compared, with no V8. `rc`'s random programs at `-O0` and `-O2` with every counter compared case by case. Bugs put into the passes, each of which must be caught. Pins at `-O1` and `-O2`, the same on Node and Bun | `tmk milestone opt-a`, `tmk test` |
| `kernel/sim` | Kernel logic and drivers under Node, with a simulated memory, GIC, timer, and virtio device backends | `node --test kernel/**/*.test.ts` |
| Boot tests | Serial-checked QEMU runs under HVF and TCG | `tmk boot-test` |
| Fault injection | Corrupt store blocks, cache headers, DTB fields, kill compiler, bad image | `tmk boot-test --faults` |
| `tmk audit` | S8 metrics, unsafe imports | Part of `tmk ci` |
| Repro | Builds twice with different paths, thread counts, env, and engines; compares bytes | `tmk repro` |
| Quick tier (D45) | The milestones' own tests on fewer configurations, about 3 minutes: static checks, every host configuration, 685 pinned tirhashes, the native corpus on HVF with TCG for `corpus/mem`, `rc`'s adversarial programs and the `Map`, `Set` and strings corpus, and smaller counts of the rest. Then a representative set at `-O2` (the native corpus in `pos`, `trap`, `mem`, `std`, `leak` and `rc`'s poisoning build, `rc`'s adversarial programs on TCG) and the optimiser's two differential fuzzers, about 3.5 minutes in all. It verifies nothing: a milestone from `tmk clean` does. `--catch-rate` runs it once per injected bug the tools know Its steps are jobs of the gate's pool (D51): `327 s` from clean in M5's measurement, against 491 s one after another. `--changed` runs only the steps a change since the baseline can reach, by the import graph and each step's declared data, with a smoke set always, and any gate unit that reaches a change no step does | `tmk test`, `tmk test --changed` |
| Gate (D51) | Every milestone's boxes as units of one registry (`tools/registry.ts`), each at the configurations its milestones need, run once each in one pool of jobs; a milestone is a view of their results. A phase gate runs a rotating subset of the heavy sweeps, and `--full` all of them | `tmk gate`, `tmk gate --full`, `tmk milestone <name>` |

`tmk corpus --native [--trap|--lower|--all] [--accel hvf|tcg|both]` is the AArch64 configuration, from phase A. It builds one image per program
with its cases in it, using a driver written in TIR that places arguments and calls the export. Through the RAM channel (8.2) come result leaves,
final typed-array bytes, and for lowered code a snapshot of the arena. The harness rebuilds JS values from those and compares them like
any other configuration. `corpus/native/` holds programs for this configuration alone (3.10, item 7).

**The differential rule:** the reference for every positive test is the same source on V8, run as in 3.10.
Results are compared as
canonical JSON, with bigints as strings, floats as hex bit patterns (NaN canonicalised), and typed-array
output by SHA-256.

**`.cases.json` format:**

```json
[{ "fn": "crc32", "args": [{ "bytes": "68656c6c6f" }, 0], "expect": null },
 { "fn": "mul64", "args": ["18446744073709551615n", "3n"], "expect": null }]
```

Argument forms: JSON number; a bigint as a string ending in `n`; `true`/`false`; and typed arrays as
`{ "bytes": hex }`, `{ "i32s": [...] }`, `{ "u32s": [...] }`, `{ "f64s": [...] }` (add others as needed). The
runner compares
the return value and the final contents of every typed-array argument, since mutation through a buffer is a result too.
`expect: null` means "derive from V8". Pin values with a concrete `expect` only when testing V8 itself would be circular
(for example, known-answer SHA-256 vectors). A concrete `expect` is a return value in argument form, or
`{ "args": [null, { "bytes": hex }] }` to pin an argument's final contents. In `corpus/trap/`, a case has `"trap": code`.
Floats that JSON can't write are `{ "f64": "NaN" | "Infinity" | "-Infinity" | "-0" }`, and a record is a JSON object.

### 8.2 QEMU tests over serial

Guests report with one line per event on the PL011: `TMK:PASS <name>`, `TMK:FAIL <name> <detail>`,
`TMK:READY`, `TMK:PANIC ...`,
`TMK:FATAL ...`, `TMK:DONE`, followed by PSCI SYSTEM_OFF. Sentinels on serial are the source of truth, not the
exit code. A test image also reports per case: `TMK:C <case> R|T|A|P ...`, `TMK:M <address> <hex>`, `TMK:E <case>` (`tools/native-driver.ts`).

**The RAM channel (D45).** A byte through the PL011 costs 1.6 to 2.4 µs under HVF and about 0.8 µs under TCG (MEASURED), and the
chain sent 3.6 GB that way. So a test image built by the corpus, `rc`'s, strings' and the random programs' runners puts its per-case
lines in RAM instead: the same text, in a region past the guest's RAM and an unmapped 2 MiB guard, mapped normal and never
executable, 512 MiB of which only what's written costs anything. Guest RAM is then a file in the run's scratch directory
(`memory-backend-file` with `share=on`), which the harness reads after QEMU exits, however it exits. Serial keeps the sentinels,
and one more: `TMK:BULK <bytes> <checksum>` before `TMK:DONE`, a 32-bit FNV-1a over the channel's 4-byte words. The rules:
- With `TMK:BULK`, the channel must have exactly that many bytes, with that checksum and no zero byte, or the run fails as
  `bad-channel`. `TMK:DONE` with no `TMK:BULK` fails too.
- With no `TMK:BULK` (a panic, a fault nothing catches, a hang killed by the timeout), what's there up to the first zero is
  what the guest got through, and every case after it is reported as never finished, by name. `TMK:PANIC` and `TMK:FATAL` go to
  serial, and the guest stops using the channel first.
- Past the channel's end the guest reports `TMK:FATAL bulk channel full` and stops: never a quiet cut.
- A run of `TMK:M` lines is decoded into guest memory straight from the bytes, a case at a time, and never becomes strings.
- Benchmarks, the harness's own tests, the JPEG check and `tmk lower --target aarch64` build no channel and are byte-identical
  to before. `TMK_CHANNEL=serial` puts every test image back on the PL011, to compare or debug. `native-g` box 9b shows the
  harness catching a wrong value, a byte changed after the checksum, a short count, no trailer, a truncated result whose count
  and checksum agree, a fault nothing catches and a hang partway, naming the case, and an overflow, on HVF and TCG.

**Harness requirements (`tools/qemu-run.ts`):**

- Spawn QEMU in its own process group with stdin closed, `-monitor none` by default, and `-serial stdio`.
- Unix-socket monitor only with `--monitor`, in a per-run temp directory.
- **Hard timeout** (default 20 s; `SIGTERM`, then `SIGKILL` the group after 2 s). On timeout: fail with the
  last 40 lines
  of serial output.
- Treat `TMK:DONE` as the signal to give QEMU up to 2 s to exit, then kill it.
- Leave no QEMU processes running. Before a suite and at exit, kill only processes started by this harness (track PIDs).
  The record is one file per harness process, `logs/qemu-pids/<pid>.pids` in its build directory, and a harness reaps only
  the records of harnesses that are no longer running, so two harnesses at once no longer kill each other's QEMUs (D51). A
  gate reaps a job's record when the job ends, and kills its jobs' groups and reaps their records when it's stopped.
- Scratch files go in a unique temp dir per run, and are deleted on pass and kept on failure, with the path printed.
- Run concurrently: 4 by default (`--jobs`, on the suite that calls it). Each with its own copies of writable images.
- Save the full serial log under `build/logs/<test>.log`, with what came through the RAM channel after it. The RAM file is
  deleted after it's read, also when the scratch directory is kept.
- Both accelerators: `--accel hvf`, `--accel tcg`, `--accel both`. Performance tests are HVF only.
- HVF unavailable: report a skip, never a pass.

All Node-side tests run through `tools/guarded-run.ts`, which enforces a wall-clock timeout and samples RSS every 500 ms
and kills above 3 GiB, reporting which test did it.

### 8.3 How each milestone is proved

Each milestone has a single command, `tmk milestone mN`, which runs its acceptance tests, prints `PASS`/`FAIL` per item,
exits nonzero on failure, and writes `build/milestones/mN.json`. A milestone isn't done until this passes from a clean
checkout with `tmk clean`.

**The registry and the gate (D51).** A milestone's boxes are units in `tools/milestones/<name>.ts`: one or more boxes that
share what they compute, named by their places ("3", "2,5-7"). A box that says another milestone passes is that milestone's
view, at its level or the one it names (`opt-a` names `native-g` at `-O0` and at `-O2`, and the quick tier at `-O1`). The
gate plans every view the top milestones need and every unit each view needs, at its configuration, once: a unit that can't
depend on the optimiser's level runs once for both levels. Each unit is a job, `tmk job <milestone> <unit>`, in a process of
its own under the 3 GiB watchdog, with its own build directory (`build/jobs/<job>/`, TMK_BUILD_DIR), so nothing a job writes
is seen by another. Jobs run in one pool, longest first by the last run's times or the registry's: first the solo phase,
units that need the host still (the harness's own tests, which count every QEMU on the host, and the unit tests, whose check
that a killed group's grandchild is gone at once fails when processes are made around it), alone; then the quiet phase, the
units whose verdict is a gate on a time (G1, G2 and S4, `-O1`'s compile time, and `native-e`'s list slowdown), with nothing
else; then the rest, `{parallel}` at a time. Then each milestone's boxes are read off the jobs' records, in their places, and
the boxes that say a milestone passes from that milestone's view. `tmk milestone <name>` is that milestone's views; `tmk gate`
is the views of the milestones nothing else runs (`maps` today, which runs `lang-a`), the same jobs. The registry can give a job
fewer suites at once than `--jobs` (`jobs` in `tools/registry.ts`), where its own process's memory needs it: `native-d`'s box 4.
`tmk gate --sample` compares each picked job's verdicts, boxes and the counts of the suites both runs recorded: which suites a
record keeps depends on their times (one under 50 ms isn't kept), so the lists themselves aren't compared.

**Which units can't depend on the level** is proved, not assumed: every job runs with TMK_LEVEL_TRACE, and the optimiser
notes in it any level a process takes from the environment rather than being given one (compiler/tir/passes/manager.ts,
and `tmk lower`'s default). A unit whose jobs at `-O0` and `-O2` noted nothing, in their processes, workers and children,
and whose results were the same at both levels before this work, is level-free (`free` in the registry), and runs once. A
free unit's job that notes a level fails, so the proof is checked by every run.

**Phase gates and full runs** (owner, 2026-11-07: "full sweeps run nightly, a rotating subset at phase gates"). `tmk gate`
runs a subset of the heavy sweeps: a quarter of the random programs' seeds, of the generated `finally` programs, of the cases
of iteration under mutation, and of the collector's budgets above 3, each a different quarter by the UTC day
(`tools/sweep.ts`, TMK_SWEEP), so four gates cover all of it; every slice taken is in the manifest. The injected bugs are
caught in every quarter: those that aren't (the runtime's faults against random programs) run whole. `tmk gate --full`,
the nightly run, and every `tmk milestone` run everything, and only those verify.

**The manifest.** Every gate, milestone or `tmk test` run writes `build/gate/manifest.json` (and a dated copy): a content hash
of every input (the compiler, runtime, tools, packages, corpora, benchmarks, the spec and its backups, the root configs; not README.md or decisions.md, which no run reads),
the versions of Node, Bun, QEMU, clang and the rest, the real corpus's manifest, whether it started from `tmk clean`, the
views and levels, the accelerators and HVF, the sweep (full, or the subset's key), and every job's result, boxes, suite counts,
level trace and peak memory. `tmk verify-manifest [file]` checks one against the tree as it is: every input the same, the
tree unchanged while it ran, from clean, every job the registry needs there and passing, and each view's verdict what its
boxes say. `tmk gate --sample N [--manifest f] [--seed s]` runs N of its jobs again, each in a new directory, and compares
verdicts, boxes and suite counts: a reviewer's spot check. The manifest isn't a cache: nothing is skipped because of it.

A milestone's JSON has `timing` (D45): seconds per box, and per suite, each suite being one call of a test function with its
arguments, its counts (cases, programs, agreed and the rest it returns), and its phases. A nested milestone's view goes in
the box that names it. Each run prints the slowest jobs first (`TIME` lines). Nothing reuses a result: there's no result
cache (D45), so every milestone run is a full one.

**The build store (D76).** Inside one run of `tmk gate`, `tmk test` or `tmk milestone`, what a compiler or a reference
engine makes is made once and handed to every later asker (`tools/store.ts`): tslc's `lowerFile` (in the test process, its
compile workers, `lower-compile.ts`'s batches and the dual route), and the output of children that are a function of their
inputs: the pins tools (`*-hashes.ts`), the source of a program on V8 or JSC (`lower-exec.ts` and `corpus-exec.ts` in source
mode) and a printed package on V8 or JSC (`printed-exec.ts`). Every QEMU run still runs, every comparison is still made: the
store holds builds and reference outputs, never a verdict. An entry is keyed on its kind, the engine (Node's or Bun's version),
the input file's path and bytes, the options, and every `TMK_*`, `TSL_*` and `BUN_*` variable but those that only name a job's
paths; a path outside the tree in a child's arguments is keyed by its bytes (a printed package by its whole directory), and
every file a compile read from outside the tree is checked by its bytes when the entry is used. The tree itself is fixed for
the run (the gate hashes it before and after). The run names its own directory, `build/store/<run>/`, which every job and
child inherits through `TMK_STORE` and which is removed when the run ends, so nothing outlives a run and a run from `tmk clean`
made everything it used. Checked, not trusted: one reuse in 16, by the key and the run, is made again from scratch and compared
by value (`TMK_STORE_VERIFY=all` every one, `off` none); a difference throws in the suite that asked and fails the run, and
`tmk verify-manifest` rejects a manifest that records one. Making a build noted the level it took from the environment in the
job's trace, so reusing it notes it again. A unit that measures, times compiles or needs a still host runs without it
(`quiet`, `measures`, `solo`, and `noStore` in the registry: `pipe-a` box 8). The manifest records each kind's reuses, builds,
checks and mismatches; `TMK_STORE=off` runs as before.

**Selecting a change, declaration by declaration (D76).** `--changed` reads the test code (`tools/`) by its declarations
(`tools/deps.ts`): each top-level declaration is a node, as is each `M.unit` call in a milestone's define function, each quick
step, what a module runs when it's loaded (its initialisers that can run anything, and statements), and the rest of a define
function, which every one of its units runs. A node depends on what it names, through imports, `await import(...)`, namespaces
by the properties used (the whole module when a namespace is used any other way) and the module code of every module it reaches;
a file named by a path (a child's script, a worker) is reached whole, with everything it can load, as is anything outside
`tools/`. A unit's roots are what `tmk job` runs for it: tmk.ts's own code and job command, every module it loads, its
milestone's define function and its own unit, not its siblings. A baseline keeps every node's hash, of its tokens (whitespace
and comments run nothing), and a change reaches a unit when it changes a node the unit can run, or a file it reaches whole, or
its data. Checked against what runs: `tools/deps-check.ts` reads V8's coverage of a job, its children and workers included,
and every function of `tools/` that ran has to be among its unit's dependencies. It reads the test code with the TS API, as
`tools/coverage.ts` does (both are listed beside `compiler/host` in the lint rule that confines it, 4.2): it compiles nothing.

**Compiles made cheaper, and off the test process's thread (D76, T2).** What a compile asks of the libraries is done once
per process, not once per compile (`compiler/host/program.ts`): the parsed and bound forms of the modules of `packages/`,
`compiler/rt` and TypeScript's own lib files, keyed by their text and the settings that shape a parse; module resolution
from those directories, and the lib files' resolution, through caches the process keeps; and a package's `tsl.json`, read
once per compile rather than once per question. The printer's rounds of `!` sites (tslc.ts, compileViaTsl) are checked up to
elaboration and no further: they read tsc's errors alone, which are all found by then, and the final printing is checked
in full as before. None of it changes what a compile gives, and that's checked, not trusted: one compile in 16 (by its key
and the run) is made again with all of it off (`TMK_COMPILE_REUSE=off`, which takes exactly the paths before it) and
compared by value; a difference fails the asking suite, and is recorded as a store mismatch (kind `reuse`), which fails the
run and which `verify-manifest` rejects. `TMK_COMPILE_REUSE=verify` checks every compile. On Node, what TypeScript makes
of a TSL file for a reference run (`tools/ts-hook.mjs`) is kept in the run's store (kind `transpile`) by TypeScript's
version, the options, the file and its text, checked one in 16 as the store's are, so a reference run no longer loads
typescript.js to transpile the packages again. The dual route's builds (`dualRoute`, `tools/dual-build.ts`) are made on the
compile workers with each route's image, a few programs ahead of those running: a build on the test process's own thread
held back the results of its QEMU runs and reference engines, and under a gate's load a finished run's 60 s timer could
fire before its exit was seen. A compile worker takes every `TMK_*` and `TSL_*` variable the test process has when it asks
(an injected printer bug, `TMK_TEST_EMIT`, included), and the test process's memo of six builds is keyed on all of them.
`pipe-d` box 13's printer bugs and `native-f` box 9's runtime bugs run in parts (`tools/parts.ts`), as `opt-a` box 12's
do: each part a process and build directory of its own, two at once, the box's text put together from their answers in
its own order, a part that doesn't finish failing the box. The hosted runtime (macos-arm64, D57a) writes its output when
its buffer of 64 KiB fills and at exit rather than at each line: a program whose results are read from memory printed its
pages a line at a time, a `write` each (500,000 for `adv_exc_drop`, 0.9 s of its 1.05 s in the kernel); the bare-metal
images are unchanged. The optimiser's `removeUnreachable`, asked after every inlined site, reads blocks by id from arrays
(the same blocks removed, in the same order). Nothing is tested less: the same programs, cases, levels, comparisons, pins
and injected bugs, every QEMU run, and no limit moved.

**A CPU budget, memory margin, and counts the load can't move (D76, R12).** T2 left the gate oversubscribed: each lane's job
had its own four compile workers, its parts two processes with four more each, and its QEMUs and reference engines besides.
The pool now serves a token a core on a Unix socket (`tools/cpu-budget.ts`, TMK_CPU_SOCK), and every leaf of every job takes
one while it runs: a compile on a worker (`tools/compile-pool.ts`), a QEMU run (`tools/qemu-run.ts`), and a child that's a
compile batch, a reference engine's run or a pins tool (`tools/guarded-run.ts`'s `isLeaf`). A token is a connection, given
back when it closes, so a process that dies gives its tokens back; nothing holding one waits for another, so the budget can't
deadlock; it's taken before a leaf's time limit starts, so a full budget delays a run and never times one out; and the
waiter of the longest job (TMK_CPU_PRIO, the pool's estimate) goes first. A job's own thread isn't a leaf. With no budget (a
job run alone) nothing waits. The gate's manifest records the budget, the most tokens held, and the most cores the run's
processes used (ps's %cpu), since the host's load average counts every ready thread, V8's helpers included, and isn't how
many cores are busy. A process runs at most two of the dual route's builds at once (`ROUTES_AT_ONCE`: pipe-a box 3 alone
2.63 GiB with three, 2.29 GiB with two), and `lang-a` box 10 two suites at once (2.54 GiB with four, 1.68 GiB with two):
fewer at once, not a higher limit. And an injected bug's `answers` is load-independent at the root: `pipe-d` box 21 counted
410 under load against 223 quiet because a reference on V8 that guarded-run killed at its 30 s limit ("over the 30000 ms
wall-clock limit") wasn't seen as out of time, and every case of its program was then a wrong answer against nothing. Now
that wording is out of time (`ranOutOfTime`), a program whose reference didn't finish isn't compared case by case (its own
pins still are), a case one route's run never reached because the run ran out of time says so in the dual route, and the
boxes that printed `failures.length` for a bug print its wrong answers (`faultCount`); with the budget, six copies of box
21's run at once give 223, the quiet figure, each (`tools/fault-time.test.ts`).

**A compile worker let go when the process is large (R27).** pipe-d box 48 runs the dual route four times in one process, one
injected bug each, and its peak rose round by round to 2.70 GiB in R26's gate against the 3 GiB watchdog. Measured alone under
a gate's load (2.69 GiB, R27's `TMK_POOL_LOG`, which writes a line for each job a worker finishes: its live heap, V8's heap as
it holds it, and the process's RSS), the test process's own heap was about 30 MiB and each of its two workers' live heap under
400 MiB after a job; the rest was what the workers' isolates kept beyond their live heaps, which goes back only when a worker
does (a worker's 640 MiB limit doesn't hold under the job's `--max-old-space-size`, R16). So a worker that finishes a job while
the process's RSS is past 1.5 GiB (`RECYCLE_RSS_MB`) goes, as one past `RECYCLE_HEAP_MB` already did, at most one every 3 s
(`RECYCLE_RSS_GAP_MS`: a fresh worker loads the compiler again), and a fresh one takes the next job; and the dual route lets its
idle workers go when a run of it ends (`releaseIdleWorkers`). Box 48 alone then peaked at 2.12 GiB, 86 workers over its four
runs. MEASURED, the other ways tried: every worker past 1.5 GiB let go at once, 2.07 GiB but 509 workers and about 45% longer
under the same load; past 1.75 GiB, 2.22 GiB; one every 10 s, 2.46 GiB; that with the idle workers let go, 2.27 GiB. Nothing a
worker makes depends on which worker it is, so only when work is done changes; every case still runs.

**`auto`'s own builds in the differential, and timing a program's cases (R14).** The dual route can take its TSL side
from `auto` (`dualRoute`'s `auto`, dual-build.ts): a program counts only where `auto` took the TSL route and its printing
was reshaped, so what `auto` switches over is what's compared, natively and on V8 and JSC, rather than the forced printing
beside it (`tmk milestone pipe-d` boxes 47 and 48). A test image can run its cases many passes over, each case's run (not
what's printed after it) timed by the counter, each pass's sum printed (`Driver.main`'s timing passes, `RcHarness.timePasses`);
`tools/r14-time.ts` builds both routes' images of a program so and interleaves their runs, or with `TMK_ICOUNT=1` on TCG
counts instructions, the same each run. Numbers only, never a gate.

**Programs that run until memory is out, judged at equal work (R29; the owner's ruling, 2027-01-21).** A program that fills
memory and counts until it traps 14 is compared at equal work, not by its time to the trap: class printing fits more in the
same memory (a map's table twice the entries in the same pages), so it does more work before the trap, and doing more before
memory runs out is better use of memory, not slowness. The speed rule itself is unchanged: no slower than the direct route at
-O1 and -O2. tools/r14-time.ts finds such a program by a stated property, not a list: a case pinned to trap 14 in the mode it
times (`lowered_trap` 14, `memory_trap`'s entry for the mode 14, or an `rc`-only corpus's `trap` 14), whose first argument is
then its count of work (tools/equal-work.ts's `untilOut`). For each such case it finds each route's limit, the largest count
the case runs at without the trap, the cases before it run first (by halving the interval, to 1%), and times the program with
the case at the smaller limit; equal work needs every timed pass the same through both routes (no such case traps, and each
case traps or doesn't alike), so where one doesn't, every such count is halved, at most 8 times. Where equal work is never
reached, or a pinned case has no count, the program is judged by the old measure, as before; the old measure, time to the trap
with the pinned counts, is reported beside the new for every such program. Only the speed comparison changed: every test of
the trap itself is as it was, each route running each such case at its pinned count until memory is out and its trap checked.
In `rc` the property takes corpus/lower/memory/map_grow_oom.ts and exhaust.ts, exc/exc_exhaust.ts, rc-only/exhaust_drains.ts
and cyc_exhaust.ts, and rc-tsl's r2_maps, r2_arrays, r3_closures and r3_map_iter (r14-time times those `auto` takes);
cyc_exhaust never reaches equal work (its first pass leaves memory full, so every later case traps through both routes) and is
judged as before. corpus/lower/strmap/frag.ts doesn't run until memory is out (no case of it traps), so it's judged as every
other program is.

**A timing verdict over medians, and native-e box 3's memory (R16).** `native-e` box 9 asks whether the lowered list's

**The freeing step's bound and the holes flag (R17).** `tmk milestone pipe-d` box 53 runs corpus/lower/r17/r17_free.ts through the dual route with class printing forced in `rc`, `leak` and `manual` at -O0 and -O2, the printed TSL on V8 and JSC too; checks in TIR that `Rc`'s `make` is inlined at -O1 and -O2 (no call to it left in adv_forof_mutation.ts's `churn`, only its slow paths') and that an array of numbers prints with no holes and one of objects with them; and runs corpus/rc/rc_steps*.ts, whose step counts are pinned and which the host's simulation, calling every release function, has to agree with: corpus/rc/rc_steps_leaves.ts puts leaves on the queue alone and between objects of three references, and counts the steps one `new` takes, the objects it gives back and the steps freeing all of it takes, at the default budget and at 1, 2 and 3. Box 54 puts in five bugs and needs each caught by a wrong answer: the quick path for objects with no slots freeing one past its budget, and giving a block back without taking its step (both by the pinned counts); tslc taking every release function as one that does nothing (by the counts, and the rc corpus's leaks); `JsArray`'s pop leaving a reference in its slot whatever the flag, and a longer length of an array with no holes not zeroing what it adds (both by corpus/std/leak/js_array.ts's cases). Box 21's bugs put into `@tsl/gc`'s freeing (the release not called, unbounded freeing at an allocation, a freeing step doing a whole object's slots at once) are put where R17's code has them; one of them, the whole object's slots at once, had targeted text R4 removed, so from R4 to R16 its patch threw in every build and the box counted that as caught, and it's now a bug that runs (tools/gc-tests.ts).
slowdown is the free list losing the list's order: the variant whose blocks are reused (budget 32) must be slower than the
one whose blocks never are and than the one freeing at most one a step (budget 2), and only the first may lose the order
(under 10% of nodes on the next one's page at iteration 199, the other two over 90%). Each time was one sample, iteration
199's, and one scheduling hiccup (6.8 ms against about 0.35 to 0.8 ms, R15's gate at load 165) flipped it, as one had in B1's
gate. Now each variant's time is the median of its iterations 180 to 199 (`listDiagnosis`'s `tails`, all 20 required), the
same two inequalities over those medians, and the page shares as before, at 199, with the same thresholds
(`tools/r16-tests.ts`'s `box9Check`). It isn't weaker: the claim is about the steady state the list has reached by then
(Phase E's record has it 0.758 ms at iteration 60 and 0.801 at 199, so it has settled long before 180), each of the 20 is a sample of the same time that iteration 199's
is, and a median of 20 is that time with a single outlier's weight gone, where one sample can be flipped by one hiccup either
way, a false pass included: the medians are wrong only where at least 10 of a variant's 20 samples are, and a real slowdown
that only one sample in 20 shows no longer passes. Two bugs put into the diagnosis each fail the box (run in it each time):
the reused variant's freed blocks never reused, as a free list keeping the list's order would make it (the page share
catches it; its median is within 1% of the never-reused one's, which a timing verdict alone shouldn't be asked to decide),
and the reused variant timed over a tenth of the work (the medians catch it, the page share doesn't). `native-e` box 3 (no
leak, rc's corpus on HVF and TCG) peaked at 2.84 GiB in R15's gate against the 3 GiB watchdog, and it was two things in the
test process: `rcPrograms` lowered all 92 programs there to see which are usable, leaving its heap near its 1.5 GiB limit
for the rest of the run, and the compile workers' heaps, which grew past 1 GiB each, since a job run with
`--max-old-space-size` (the gate's nested milestones) overrides a worker's own 640 MiB limit (MEASURED: 866 MiB used with
the limit set to 256). Now the list is worked out in a child process of its own (`tools/rc-programs.ts`, a leaf; the same
code and list), and a worker whose heap is past 512 MiB after a job is let go and a fresh one takes the next
(`compile-pool.ts`'s `RECYCLE_HEAP_MB`, which every suite has). Alone, with a store of its own: 2.06 and 2.17 GiB at -O0
before, 1.81 after; -O2 2.11 before (with the child alone), 1.85 after. What's left is the build of `math_values.ts`'s image
of 12,400 calls (its 3,100 cases four times over), about 600 MiB in one worker for one job. Nothing is tested less.

**An injected bug has to be in the build (R18).** A box that asks whether a bug is caught has first to know the bug is there. A bug
put in by patch (`TSL_TEST_PATCH`, a file, the text it replaces and what replaces it) is applied by one rule,
`compiler/host/test-patch.ts`'s `applyTestPatch`: the text has to be in the file exactly as many times as the patch says, once unless
it says `times`, or the build throws `TSL_TEST_PATCH: …`, never compiling the source as it was; and a file names a file at a `/`, not
any name ending the same. Every runner puts a patch in through `tools/faults.ts`: `patchEnv` checks it against the source before
anything runs, and `faultFailures` throws on a failure that says a patch didn't apply. Either throw is a harness failure of the box
(`FaultHarnessError`), which fails it, saying so; it is never counted as caught. Before R18 a box that counted any failure as caught
passed a bug whose text was gone (pipe-d box 21's freeing bug from R4 to R16, JsMap's `no-norm` from R6, JsArray's `grow-last` from
R16), and a patch whose text was there twice changed only the first (four of `@tsl/std`'s map bugs, ExactMap's alone since the maps
step, and JsArray's `pop-empty`). `registeredFaults` lists every injected bug the tools know, the patches and those put in by name
through a hook (`TMK_TEST_*`, `TMK_OPT_FAULT`), and tools/faults.test.ts, a unit test (so the first job of `tmk test --changed`,
which every change selects), checks that each patch's text is in its file as many times as it says and each name is in the
compiler's source; so an edit that orphans a bug fails in seconds, not in a box an hour into a gate. A bug put in by name whose hook
is gone does nothing, which its box reports as not caught.

**Stack objects in `rc` class printing (R18).** `tmk milestone pipe-d` box 55 runs corpus/lower/r18/r18_stack.ts through the dual
route with class printing forced in `rc`, `leak` and `manual` at -O0 and -O2, the printed TSL on V8 and JSC too; checks in the
printing and TIR at -O1 and -O2 that its classes the lowering keeps on the stack are tagged and have no store, and those counted
because an object of them escapes, or is made in a loop, aren't and have one; runs corpus/neg/lowered-rc (a tagged object returned,
kept in module state, held by a counted object, and a tagged class holding a reference, each refused at its place) and
corpus/rc/rc_stack_tag.ts. Box 56 puts in each of R18's bugs and requires a catch: the printer tagging every class of numbers, or a
class a counted holder holds (tslc refuses the build at TSL3001 or TSL3002), each with tslc's escape checking also not taking a tagged
class's `new` as a stack object (wrong answers through the dual route), the expansion sharing and dropping a tagged class's
references (a stack object released by `@tsl/gc`: wrong answers and trap codes), the escape checking off alone, and the expansion
taking a tagged class that holds a reference (corpus/neg/lowered-rc's programs not refused).

**`rc` class printing's remaining costs (R19).** `tmk milestone pipe-d` box 57 runs corpus/lower/r19/r19_rooms.ts (64 pages) through
the dual route with class printing forced in `rc` at -O0 and -O2, the printed TSL on V8 and JSC too: arrays grown to lengths that
alternate between arrays of one class and read back weighted by index, literals of one and of two objects and arrays of numbers
grown into a room made and dropped far past the pages there are, objects of three sizes kept alive together and read back,
closures of three kinds chosen at run time and called in loops, and a map grown and read back. It checks in the printing and TIR
at -O1 and -O2 that the environments' `call` is `@tsl.inline` and the kind's load invariant, and runs corpus/lowered-rc/r19_fields.ts,
a hand-written lowered `rc` package, natively at -O0, -O1 and -O2 against its pinned answers (a field a method stores through a call
nothing inlines, and one only its constructor stores). Box 58 puts in each of R19's seven bugs and requires a wrong answer: a room
array's growth copying one element short, the inlined call switch's first two kinds swapped, tslc's invariance rule missing a store
a method makes (r19_fields.ts's pins), a map table's growth leaving the entry it moves first out of every chain, `freeFlat` visiting
a holder's slots from the third (a freed literal of two objects with its second still counted: trap 14), `tailFast` keeping the last
length's size class for a new one, and a fresh slot cut half a slot past the last. Two older bugs, `gc-tests`' "release not called"
and "a freeing step that visits every slot of an object at once", now say `times: 2`: their text is `freeSteps`' and, since R19,
`freeFlat`'s, which does that work for an object freeing starts with the cursor idle, so both copies are patched, or the bug
wouldn't be where freeing is (each still caught: 4 and 7).

**The runtime's short copies, and partial inlining past a frame slot (R20).** `tmk milestone pipe-d` box 59 runs
corpus/r20/r20_steps.ts, TSL proper, natively at -O0 and -O2 against its pinned answers (a byte array's `set` from a run of itself,
a copy over itself down and up, of every length to 40 and distance to 9, and `fill` of every length to 24 at every start to 8,
each counted against a byte loop), and corpus/lower/r20/r20_copies.ts through the dual route with class printing forced in `rc`
and `leak` at -O0 and -O2, against V8 natively as well (the runtime is both routes', so the routes agreeing alone proves
nothing), the printed TSL on V8 and JSC too: strings of every length to 70 joined and cut, arrays of booleans and numbers shifted
and spliced at every length to 40, and a function whose entry moves a count and keeps a frame slot for a rare path's object,
called in a loop. Box 60 puts in R20's four bugs and requires a wrong answer: a copy's last bytes missing their 4-byte step, a
copy up over itself missing its last byte, a short fill missing its 2-byte store, and partial inlining taking a callee's entry with
a frame slot as free of effects whatever follows the slot (`inline-alloca-pure-block`, also in `OPT_FAULTS`, so opt-a box 12 runs
it, R20's program its first step). *Box details in a stable order:* a suite that runs its programs on a pool returns its failures
sorted (by file, mode and level, then function and case index, digits as numbers: tools/stable.ts), and a box that quotes its
first failure, or prints a count map, quotes the first in that order and prints the keys in it, so `tmk gate --sample` sees the
same words whichever job finished first (R19's lang-a box 9 and pipe-d box 39); the sampler's comparison is unchanged.

### 8.4 Benchmarks

`tmk bench all` (D51) runs every benchmark the milestones ran inside their gates, at full counts, one at a time, at each
level they ran at. In a milestone a benchmark's box is "it exists and runs", a short run (`--quick`), unless the box's verdict
is a gate on what it measures: `m2`'s benchmark outputs and G1, `native-a`'s `tmk bench native` and G2 with S4, which stay
whole and run in the gate's quiet phase. `native-b`'s alloc, `native-c`, `native-d` and `native-e`'s memory, `native-f`'s
strmap and copy-on-write, `native-g`'s std, and `lang-a`'s exceptions and S4 again are short runs.

`tmk bench <name>`: run each configuration in a fresh process, discard warm-up (at least 200 iterations for
JIT), take the
median of ≥ 101 iterations, repeat over 5 processes, report median and spread. Include the engine version, git
hash, and the
host's load average in the JSON output. Warn if load is high: the numbers in Appendix B came from a busy host,
and they are
only rough baselines.

## 9. Repo layout and tooling

### 9.1 Layout

```text
ts-microkernel/
  SPEC.md  README.md
  package.json  pnpm-workspace.yaml  tsconfig.base.json  tsconfig.json
  .oxlintrc.json  .oxfmtrc.json  .gitignore
  packages/
    tsl-core/            @tsl/core: types and host runtime (Appendix A)
    tsl-unsafe/          @tsl/unsafe
    tsl-arch-aarch64/    @tsl/arch-aarch64
    tsl-alloc/           @tsl/alloc: Heap, Slab, Vec, in TSL, with tsl.json
    tsl-std/             @tsl/std: Vec, Map, Set, Slab, Str, StrBuilder, and the global allocator, over @tsl/alloc (D43)
    tsl-gc/              @tsl/gc: Rc and Counted, reference counting as a library, over @tsl/alloc's Heap (D63)
  compiler/
    host/                tslc-host: TS checker adapter, TSL checker, down-lowering
    rt/                  strings, Map, Set, number text: ordinary TS, lowered into what reaches it (D42)
    tir/                 ir.ts, text.ts, verify.ts, interp.ts, range.ts, passes/ (the optimiser: manager, simplify, cfg, dce, inline, sroa, keep; phase B's memory, loops, gvn, licm, unswitch, checks)
    backend-wasm/  backend-c/  backend-aarch64/
    tslc/                M8: self-hosted compiler, in TSL, with tsl.json
  seed/                  M10: seed0.hex, asm1.hex, asm2.asm, tslc0.asm, tslc1/
  kernel/
    boot0/               boot0.s
    loader/
    core/                in TSL, with tsl.json
    arch/aarch64/        start.s, vectors.ts, switch.ts (asmFn)
    api/                 sys.ts, proto/
    sim/                 Host-side simulated devices and kernel harness
    init/
  drivers/               virtio-rng, virtio-blk, virtio-net, ...
  bincheck/
  corpus/                pos/ neg/ trap/ gen/ std/ memory/ lower/ mem/ spec/
  bench/                 jpeg/vendor/, jpeg/run.ts, native/
  tools/                 tmk.ts, ts-hook.mjs, qemu-run.ts, guarded-run.ts, mkstore.ts, fuzz/
  docs/
  build/                 (git-ignored)
```

### 9.2 Config

- **package.json:** `"private": true`, `"type": "module"`, `engines.node >= 25`. Dev dependencies, exact versions:
  `typescript@5.9.3`, `oxlint@1.80.0`, `oxfmt@0.65.0` (same as Moire). Script: `"tmk": "node tools/tmk.ts"`.
- **Installing:** `pnpm install` needs network access. `pnpm` on this host's `PATH` is 11.2.2 (Appendix B), while Moire
  pins 9.15.0 in `packageManager`. Don't set `packageManager` until checked. If there's no network, see if `pnpm install
  --offline` works
  with `--store-dir ~/projects/moire/.pnpm-store`, without writing into Moire. If not, ask the owner.
- **tsl.json, per package:** `"unsafeModules"` (3.8), `"noFloat": true` (3.6, 5.5), `"noStd": true` (the package and what it imports can't import `@tsl/std`, TSL1018), and
  `"memory": "strict" | "leak" | "manual" | "rc"`, default `strict`, where `rc` is lowered by `tmk lower` (D39) and expanded onto `@tsl/gc` by `tslc` (3.5, D38, D74). `"cycles": true | false`, for `rc`, default on (D41), and `--cycles` overrides it. `tmk lower` takes the package's mode if a `tsl.json` is above the file, and `--memory` overrides it. A file with no package and no flag is `strict`. The flag is then its declaration, so `--memory manual` has no `unsafeModules` to check.
- **`@tsl/gc`:** a package in `packages/tsl-gc` with a `tsl.json`, whose one unsafe module is `ex-gc-rc.ts`, the spec's block (3.5, D63), through `tools/spec-extract.ts`. Any package can import it, as it can `@tsl/alloc`; `noStd` doesn't keep it out, and `kernel-core` doesn't use it by policy.
- **`@tsl/std`:** a package in `packages/tsl-std` with a `tsl.json`, whose unsafe modules are `ex-std-global.ts` and `ex-std-jsarray.ts` (D66). Its modules are the spec's blocks, as `@tsl/alloc`'s are, through `tools/spec-extract.ts`. A program imports `@tsl/std`, and names an allocator with `@tsl.global-allocator` or has the default (3.5). `@tsl/std` has no setting of its own.
- **`@tsl/jsrt`:** JS's run-time classes in TSL (D67), a package in `packages/tsl-jsrt` whose `tsl.json` says `"memory": "leak"` and lists its one unsafe module, `ex-jsrt-string.ts`, the spec's block, through `tools/spec-extract.ts`. In a lowered build its functions and classes take the build's mode (`compiler/host/escape.ts`), as every function there does.
- **A lowered package (D62):** `tmk lower` writes one under `build/tsl/<hash>/`, with `"lowered": { "memory": "strict" |
  "leak" | "manual" | "rc", "runtime": [...], "from": "<the TS file>" }` and no other setting. It can import `@tsl/lowered`
  (`packages/tsl-lowered`), and tslc links into it the lowering's runtime for its mode, as the direct route does. Nothing else
  can import it or be one (TSL1023). `TMK_ROUTE=direct|tsl|auto` picks the route for every lowering in a process, `auto`
  unless given, and is part of the memo's key; `TMK_TEST_EMIT` names a bug to put into the printer, for `tmk milestone pipe-a`
  only.
- **The runtime for strings and maps:** `compiler/rt/*.ts` isn't a package, and isn't configured: `lowerFile` adds it to the program in a memory mode (D42), and `tools/gen-case-tables.ts` writes `compiler/rt/case-tables.ts` from V8.
- **The test harness (D45):** `TMK_CHANNEL=serial` turns the RAM channel off (8.2). `tmk` sets `NODE_COMPILE_CACHE` to
  `build/cache/v8` for itself and its children: V8's bytecode for what they load, `typescript.js` above all, keyed by V8 on the
  source, so it can't change what any program does, and `tmk clean` removes it. The test process lowers and links on up to 4
  worker threads (`tools/compile-pool.ts`), each with a hard timeout per job and replaced when it fails or overruns, and retired
  when idle. A worker remembers its last 6 lowerings, by the root file's bytes, every option and the injected bug. All of it is
  under the test process's RSS limit. `TMK_TEST_RC` is for `tmk test --catch-rate` only: options merged into every `rc` build. `TMK_TEST_EXC` is for `tmk milestone lang-a` only (and `TMK_EXC_DEBUG` names the site it changed): a mistake put into the exception pass or the class representation (a missed check or release, `finally` too late, a wrong dispatch arm, a wrong `instanceof`, fields before `super()`), taken by workers and keyed in the memo like the rest. Batches of lowering hold at most 4 programs each, `jobs` of them at a time, so no one batch's wall-clock limit is the sum of many slow `-O2` compiles.
- **The gate (D51):** TMK_BUILD_DIR is a job's build directory (`tools/build-dir.ts`): every scratch path under `build/`
  goes there, the V8 bytecode cache excepted. TMK_LEVEL_TRACE names a file where a process notes a level it took from the
  environment; a `-O` on a `tmk` line, and the pin tools that set `-O0`, drop it, since then the level is theirs.
  TMK_SWEEP=subset with TMK_SWEEP_KEY (the UTC day) runs the heavy sweeps' rotating subset, and TMK_SWEEP_LOG gets every
  slice taken. `--parallel n` is jobs at once in the pool, `{parallel}` unless given; `--jobs n` stays each suite's own.
  `build/gate/durations.json` is the last run's seconds per job, for longest first; `build/gate/baseline.json` is the tree
  `--changed` compares with, written by every passing `tmk test`, gate and milestone, and by `tmk baseline`.
- **The optimiser (D44, D46):** `TMK_OPT` is the level, `0`, `1` or `2`, for every compile in a process and everything it
  starts, workers and children alike; `-O0`, `-O1` or `-O2` on a `tmk` line sets it. With none, the library and the harnesses
  are `-O0`, and `tmk lower` is `-O2`. The tools that print pinned tirhashes set `-O0` themselves, whatever the caller runs
  at. `TMK_OPT_DISABLE` is a comma list of passes to switch off (`--no-pass p` on a `tmk` line). `TMK_OPT_VERIFY=1` checks
  the TIR after every pass, and `tmk` sets it for `test`, `milestone`, `corpus` and `ci`. `TMK_OPT_FAULT` names a bug to put
  into the passes, for `tmk milestone opt-a` only. `TMK_OPT_COUNT_CALLS=1` adds one to `__rc_s_calls` before each call in the
  program's code, a measurement no one ships. A worker takes all of these from its parent with each job, and each is part
  of what keys the test process's memo of lowerings.
- **tsconfig.base.json (verified options):**

```json
{ "compilerOptions": {
    "strict": true, "noEmit": true, "target": "es2022", "module": "nodenext", "moduleResolution": "nodenext",
    "lib": ["es2023", "esnext.disposable"], "allowImportingTsExtensions": true,
    "noUncheckedIndexedAccess": true, "skipLibCheck": true, "verbatimModuleSyntax": true } }
```

Host-only packages (`compiler/host`, `tools/`, `bench/`) add `"types": ["node"]`, `"erasableSyntaxOnly": true`
and a dev dependency on `@types/node`.
Non-TSL host code can use full TS but must stay erasable, so Node runs it directly with no build step. TSL
packages may use `enum` and parameter properties, so running them
on Node takes `node --import ./tools/ts-hook.mjs`, a load hook that calls `ts.transpileModule` on `.ts` files
with `useDefineForClassFields: true`, which layout classes rely on (MEASURED on Node 25.8.1 and 26.13.0). Bun
needs nothing.

- **oxlint:** same plugin set as Moire (`import`, `typescript`, `unicorn`, `oxc`), with `no-restricted-imports` banning
  `@tsl/unsafe` and `@tsl/arch-aarch64` except by override per unsafe module, and banning `typescript` outside
  `compiler/host/**` and `tools/ts-hook.mjs`. **oxfmt:** `printWidth: 100`, `sortPackageJson: false`. Don't
  copy Moire's ban on `.ts` extensions in
  imports: this repo needs them for type stripping.

### 9.3 Commands to create

All run as `pnpm tmk <cmd>`, or `node tools/tmk.ts <cmd>` with no install. All take `--json` and return
nonzero on failure.

| Command | Milestone | Effect |
|---------|-----------|--------|
| `doctor` | M1 | Checks tools and versions against Appendix B; prints what's missing |
| `check <files>` | M1 | Runs `tsc`, then the TSL checker |
| `compile <file> --target wasm\|c\|aarch64 [-O0\|-O1\|-O2] [--no-pass p] [--emit tir\|js-checked]` | M1+ | Compile one module. `-O0` unless given (D44): `-O2` is to be the kernel's when there is one. `tir` takes the same |
| `tir <file>` | M1 | Print canonical TIR and `tirhash` |
| `corpus [--neg\|--trap\|--matrix\|--lower] [--native [--all\|--mem\|--modes\|--std\|--lower [--memory leak\|manual\|rc]] [--accel hvf\|tcg\|both]] [--filter x] [--jobs n]` | M1+ | Differential corpus. `--lower` is down-lowering's, in `corpus/lower/`: `pos/` for each rule in 4.5, `fallback/` for programs that must fall back, each checked against headers such as `// expect-fallback: fn blocker`, and `memory/` for programs only a mode makes sense for, with `// memory-pages: n` limiting the page source. `--native --lower --memory m` runs all of them in that mode where no fallback is left, and `rc` adds `corpus/lower/rc`, adversarial programs against V8. `corpus/lower/rc-only` isn't compared with V8, and each case pins its value: it's in `tmk milestone native-d`. `--modes` is TSL proper's packages with modes, in `corpus/memory/`. `--std` is `corpus/std/`, TSL programs on `@tsl/std`, against V8 and JSC |
| `lower <file> [--memory leak\|manual\|rc] [--cycles on\|off] [-O0\|-O1\|-O2] [--no-pass p] [--target aarch64] [--report] [--no-fallback] [--profile p.json] [--emit tir\|tsl] [--route auto\|tsl\|direct] [--out base]` | M2, D62 | Down-lower with diagnostics. `--emit tsl` prints the program as TSL, one module per source module (D65; to `--out dir` as a package directory, with its tsl.json), or says why the TSL route can't take it yet; `--route` picks the route, `auto` (the TSL route where it can) unless given. A mode writes TIR and `DownMeta` and no Wasm, and `--target aarch64` links that with no cases. In `rc`, `--report` adds the count sites, what was borrowed, and which classes can form a cycle with their allocation sites. `-O2` unless the line or `TMK_OPT` says otherwise (D44), and at `-O1` and `-O2` `--report` adds the optimiser's remarks: what was inlined where, and why not |
| `coverage [--real] [--compiler dir] [--budget ms] [--label l]` | D48 | The fraction of functions that lower natively in `rc`, by root cause: the local corpora, and with `--real` the projects pinned in `corpus/real/manifest.json`, read from the cache. A function that touches an import that didn't resolve and falls back counts as `unresolved-import`, with what that hides printed. `--compiler` measures another tree's compiler. Every function reachable from an export counts, constructors, methods and `get`/`set` accessors of an exported class included, static or not, through a probe module that exists only in the coverage program; a generic class's members, private and protected ones and computed names aren't counted. Writes `build/coverage/` |
| `corpus-fetch` | D48 | Fetches each project in `corpus/real/manifest.json` at its pinned commit into `~/.cache/ts-microkernel/real-corpus`. Runs nothing of theirs |
| `exc-gen` | D49 | Writes `corpus/lower/exc/gen_finally_*`: every way out of every position of a `try` nested in every position of another |
| `bench all\|jpeg [--quick] [--large-full]\|native\|alloc\|memory\|strmap\|cow\|std\|exc\|maps` | M2, M5 | Benchmarks; `all` is every one the milestones used to run, at full counts (D51). `maps` is the worst single operation on a `Map` or `Set` grown to 2^20 entries and one more, by the counter around each call, and the throughput of a build and a mix (D47). `--quick` is a smoke run, not a measurement. The 4000×3000 fixture uses 10 + 21 iterations in one process unless `--large-full` asks for the counts in 8.4 |
| `profile <file> <fn> [--time\|--instructions] [--route direct\|tsl\|printed] [--memory rc] [--cycles on\|off] [--n 20000] [--calls k] [--warm k] [--samples k] [--top n] [--focus re] [--annotate re] [--per ops] [-O0\|-O1\|-O2]` | R1f | Where a native program's time or instructions go, by function and by instruction, from the image `bench memory` times: `fn(n)` called in a loop, the TSL proper file compiled (`--route tsl`), or the ordinary TS lowered by the direct route, or printed as TSL classes that tslc compiles (`--route printed`, R2). `--time` (HVF) samples the guest's program counter through the QEMU monitor; a function's share of samples is its share of time, within about the square root of its samples. `--instructions` (TCG) is exact: QEMU logs each translated block (`-d in_asm`) and each block run (`-d exec,nochain`) into a pipe the tool reads as it comes, and a block's runs times its instructions, at each of its addresses, is every instruction run; a function's entries are the runs of its first block. With `--warm k` it runs `k` calls and `k + calls` and takes the difference, so a first call's heap growth isn't in a steady state's figures. `--annotate` lists every instruction of the functions it names with what ran there, disassembled by the image's own decoder; `--per` divides by the operations a call makes. It starts and stops only its own QEMU, by the process group it started; a hard timeout, a line limit on the trace and an RSS watchdog guard it. No gate: numbers for finding a cost |
| `fuzz --seconds n --seed s` | M3 | Differential fuzz |
| `qemu <image> [--accel hvf\|tcg] [--timeout s] [--monitor]` | M3 | Guarded run |
| `boot-test [--filter x] [--accel both] [--faults]` | M3+ | Boot tests |
| `audit` | M4 | S8 metrics. Present from phase B, with what exists so far |
| `mkstore --out store.img --from <dir>` | M7 | Build store image |
| `repro` | M5 | Reproducibility check |
| `ddc` | M8 | Diverse double-compile |
| `milestone mN`, `milestone native-a`, `milestone native-b`, `milestone native-c`, `milestone native-d`, `milestone native-e`, `milestone native-f`, `milestone native-g`, `milestone opt-a`, `milestone lang-a`, `milestone maps`, `milestone pipe-a`, `milestone pipe-b`, `milestone pipe-c`, `milestone pipe-d` | All | Acceptance run for a milestone. `pipe-a` is the pipeline's phase 1, TS → TSL → TIR (D62), with the dual-route differential. `pipe-b` is phase 2's first two steps: `@tsl/gc` and handles (D63), objects as TSL classes (D64), and the sampler comparing counts. `pipe-c` is zeroed construction (3.5) and one TSL module per source module (D65). `pipe-d` is arrays as `@tsl/std`'s `JsArray` (D66). `native-a` and `native-b` are phases A and B of the native proof (M5). `native-c` is `noStd` and the memory modes (D38). `native-d` is `rc` (D39). `native-e` is `rc`'s cycle collector (D41). `native-f` is `Map`, `Set` and run-time strings (D42). `native-g` is `@tsl/std` (D43), and the RAM channel's box (D45). `opt-a` is the optimiser's phase A (D44, D46), which runs `native-g` twice, at `-O0` and `-O2`. Each is a view of the registry's jobs with the ones before it (8.3, D51), runs everything in full, and writes a manifest. A milestone takes `-O0`, `-O1` or `-O2` like anything else, and its pins stay `-O0`'s |
| `gate [--full] [--parallel n] [--rotation k] [--changed [--since f]] [--sample n [--manifest f] [--seed s]]` | D51 | Every milestone's units, each configuration once, in one pool; the top milestones' views; a manifest. Without `--full`, the heavy sweeps' rotating subset. `--changed` runs the units a change can reach; `--sample` reruns some of a manifest's jobs and compares. `--help` (or `-h`) prints its usage and starts nothing (R21) |
| `verify-manifest [file]`, `baseline`, `job <milestone> <unit> --out f` | D51 | Check a manifest against this tree; record the tree `--changed` compares with; run one unit (what the gate's jobs are) |
| `test [-O0\|-O1\|-O2] [--changed [--since f]] [--fail-fast] [--order re] [--catch-rate [--only re]]` | D45 | The quick tier (8.1): about 3.5 minutes, writes `build/test.json`, prints what it leaves out, and verifies nothing. Its last steps are at `-O2` whatever the line says, and the rest at the line's level. `--catch-rate` runs it once for each bug the tools can inject (`@tsl/std`'s, the collector's, the runtime's, and counts left out), and says which step caught each. `--changed` plans the gate's tops too wherever it picks a job the quick tier hasn't got, a `test` job at another level included (R21: a new `.test.ts` file no quick step reads picked `test/1@1`, never planned it, and the run said FAIL with every job it ran passing). `--help` (or `-h`) prints its usage and starts nothing (R21) |
| `ci`, `clean` | M1 | All passing suites; remove `build/`, the V8 bytecode cache in `build/cache` with it |
