In the 256 MiB image the throws run in `leak` through both routes now (they ran out through the TSL route), and run out in `manual` through both. What's left in `leak` is read off the TIR of `down`: the two literals a throw stores are a load and a null test of module state each, where the direct route has a static address; that it is the 1–2% is inferred, not measured.
- **Speed, `tmk bench memory --classes --strings`** (as pipe-f measured it), TSL route against direct, `leak` and `manual`:

  | | -O1 before | -O1 now | -O2 before | -O2 now |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | appends | 1.36×, 1.27× | 1.23×, 1.15× | 1.38×, 1.31× | 1.22×, 1.24× |
  | short joins | 1.21×, 0.94× | 1.23×, 0.97× | 1.22×, 0.97× | 1.19×, 0.94× |
  | substrings | 1.10×, 1.03× | 1.05×, 1.01× | 1.10×, 1.05× | 1.04×, 0.98× |
  | scan | 1.17×, 1.05× | 1.13×, 1.02× | 1.18×, 1.08× | 1.09×, 1.01× |
  | split and join | 1.14×, 1.08× | 1.10×, 1.04× | 1.14×, 1.07× | 1.05×, 1.00× |

  Found in the inliner's remarks and fixed in TSL proper: `strIndex` cost 139 where the direct route's costs 27, as partial inlining had copied the one-unit table's miss (`unitMade`, its checks and the units' bump) into it, twice; `unitMade` is `@tsl.noinline` and `strIndex` costs 37 and inlines. `strCharCodeAt` cost 40, from a unit's address as a checked shift and add and a `x !== x` on an `i32` that nothing folded; a unit's address is an element step now, and the optimiser folds an integer compared with itself (helping every program: see the pins), so it costs 20 and inlines.
- **The two allocations, tested:** in the machine code a flat string through the TSL route is a call to `__leak_alloc` for the object and an inline bump for its units, and the direct route's is one call; a short join's two strings take 96 bytes to the direct route's 64. Measured with `TSL_TEST_PATCH`, for timing only: with short flat strings' units written at the bump's place without taking it, `leak`'s short joins go from 1.20× to 0.93× (`manual`'s from 0.94× to 0.75×), so the units' own allocation is the short joins' gap (which part, the bump or the 32 more bytes of fresh memory, isn't separated). It isn't the appends' gap: an append in place makes one object in both routes. Without the appended unit's copy into the buffer, appends go from 1.25× to 1.06× in `leak` (1.27× to 1.03× in `manual`), so the gap is in that write, which is the same `__rt_memmove` call of 2 bytes in both routes; why it costs more through the TSL route isn't found.
- **Proposed, not built: TSL classes ending in a variable-length array** (for the owner; D67). A class's last field may be `units!: Tail<u16>` (a scalar element type only), and `newWithTail(JsString, n)` from `@tsl/core` makes one with n elements in the same allocation, the length kept in a field the class names; `this.units.get(i)` and `.set(i, v)` check against it, and the tail's address is the object's plus a fixed offset. It is legal strict TypeScript as written (`Tail<T>` is a class in `@tsl/core`, and on V8 a typed array). What it would buy: a flat string as one allocation, as D42's and the direct route's are (the short joins' 1.20× in `leak`, measured above as the units' own allocation), and units at a fixed offset from the object, so a native caller's string ABI could go back to D36's. What it would cost the language: an object's size is no longer its class's, so every allocator, `Slab` and arena takes a size per object, `manual`'s free has to find it (from the length field), and `sizeof` and `D36`'s published layouts get a variable part; such a class can't be placed on the stack unless n is a constant, can't be copied whole, can't be a field of another class or an array element by value, and can't be inherited from (TSL has no inheritance, so that is free); a tail of references would need descriptors that read the length, so it is scalars only; the V8 simulation needs the typed array beside the object; tslc's escape analysis, layout, zeroed construction (the tail zeroed or not) and the checker each gain a case. Not built, as asked; the alternative inside TSL that was considered, keeping a few units in the fields a flat string leaves unused (`owner`, `start`, `cap`), stores raw units in a reference field's place, which TSL can't say without `unsafe`, so it wasn't tried.
- **Test hygiene:** `native-e` box 7 (the collector's latency) and `native-f` box 12 (strmap's quick benchmark) are `measures` in the registry, so `tmk gate --sample` compares their words, not their figures (pipe-b box 5 checks both). `native-g` box 6's "the named allocator ignored": diagnosed from the gate's own records of that tree (build/jobs/native-g_6@0 and @2): the 3 cases are named.ts's, and the other 14 at -O0 were std_new_safety.ts's cases 49 to 61 never finishing (its guest log stops after case 48, `trySetFailsPartWayKeys`, with no bulk report): with the named allocator ignored, that case exhausts the whole guest instead of its pool, and at -O0 in a loaded gate its image ran out of time there; run alone it's 3 at -O0 and at -O2, three times. The box now counts the cases that gave a wrong result or trap code, and not those that ran out of time, which depend on the host's load ("caught by time alone" if that were all).
- **Injected, each caught:** in JsString, a unit chunk's end taken from the next chunk's size (by the hand-written program's new `chunks` cases, which cross every chunk size, and the dual route), the first chunk 16 pages again (the new `corpus/std/leak/js_string_small.ts`, 12 pages, traps 14; the dual route on `exc_exhaust.ts` in `manual` no longer sees it, since `Dyn` is 56 bytes), and a cached hash one more than the hash (the dual route on `app_interp`, `app_parser` and `app_visitor`), in pipe-d box 11; in the printer, `Dyn` sharing a field between two fields of one class it holds (the dual route on corpus/lower/exc, pipe-d box 13) and a local set to `this` once and then moved on printed as `this` (the dual route on `class_tsl.ts`'s new `walkDown`, pipe-b box 8); in the optimiser, an integer compared with itself folded as though they differed (`fold-self-compare`, opt-a's fault box).
- **Pins** (tools/pipe-h-pins.ts, found by computing the opt, pre-std, pre-strings, strict, rc-off and modes pins with pipe-h's printer, optimiser and JsString and without, and from the gate's pin boxes): 99 programs. 16 lowered programs at -O1 and -O2 in every mode (corpus/lower/strmap's 12 programs, fallback's `js_throw_through.ts`, `throw_value.ts` and `try_catch.ts`, and rc-only's `cast_lie.ts`, rc and its poisoning build included, which class printing doesn't reach), by the self-compare fold; `corpus/lower/rc/adv_temporaries.ts` in `leak` and `manual` at every level, by a field store printed on `this`; `corpus/std/leak/js_string.ts`, by its new case and JsString's changes. And corpus/lower/exc's 79 programs in `rc` at -O2, by the same fold (every one throws, so has `tmkExcDescribe` and its number text): those are pinned in corpus/memory/maps-tirhash.json, which pipe-a box 7 and maps box 9 compare exactly, so its 79 `@rc@O2` entries were pinned again, and nothing else in it changed; and 31 programs through the TSL route at -O2 in `leak` and `manual` (corpus/memory/pipe-tirhash.json, the exceptions corpus, fallback's three, `cast_lie.ts` and strmap's, the fold again, -O0 unmoved), whose 62 entries were pinned again likewise. None at -O0 but `adv_temporaries.ts`, and none in `strict`.

**Pipeline, phase 2, exceptions printed as TSL (pipe-g), `tmk milestone pipe-d` boxes 12 to 14, MEASURED 2026-11-09** (same host, load 2 to 4 on 10 CPUs for the benchmarks). D68: class printing desugars exceptions itself.

- **The desugaring:** `compiler/host/emit-exc.ts`, written apart from down-exc.ts, from the tree as it was before it (`DownResult.excSource` keeps each function's earlier body, result, name and export, and class printing swaps them in while it prints and back). The shape is D68's: `__exc_on: bool` and `__exc_val: Dyn | null` as module state, `if (__exc_on)` after each call that can throw, `$tryN:` and `$finallyN:` labelled blocks with `t_completion`, and the native caller's four functions printed over `Dyn`. In `corpus/lower/exc/app_retry.ts`'s `withRetry` (a `try`/`catch`/`finally` in a loop, `continue` on a `TransientError`, `throw e` otherwise, the lock released in `finally`), phase 1's printing reads `if ((load<i32>(addr("__exc_on"), 0) !== 0)) { return pack<f64>(cast<f64>(0)); }`, `let e: Ref = load<Ref>(addr("__exc_val"), 0);` and `load<i32>(t_t_7, 0) === 8` for the class test; class printing reads `if (__exc_on) { return 0; }`, `let e: Dyn | null = __exc_val;` and `t_t_7.cid === 8`, with `(__exc_val = e); (__exc_on = true); break $finally3;` for the rethrow and `if ((t_completion === 3)) { continue; }` after the `finally` code.
- **`unknown` as a class:** an `unknown` and everything it can hold print as one class, `Dyn` (D68), and so do the classes read out of one after `typeof` (the boxes), found as the locals an `unknown` goes into. A string field prints as `JsString` with strings on, and an `unknown` field as `Dyn | null`. The runtime's number text keeps its stack typed arrays as phase 1 prints them, in `compiler/rt`'s functions only.
- **The harness:** the native caller's `__exc_take` and the description are typed by the module's signatures (a class reference is an `i64` through TSL, as a JsString is), and the driver prints a description's units at the address JsString keeps, for builds whose strings are JsString (`strAbs`). Neither moves a direct-route image.
- **Coverage, with classes and strings forced, `leak` at -O2:** 47 of 139 programs where 29 printed, and all 63 generated `finally` programs. What stops the rest of corpus/lower/exc: the hash of a string (`strHash`'s load at the lowering's offset, 4 programs), an optional field and a `Set`'s void vector.
- **Differential (box 12):** corpus/lower/exc with its generated programs, 77 programs, 308 builds, 12,184 cases in `leak` and `manual` at -O0 and -O2: 12,180 the same. The 4 others are `exc_exhaust.ts` in `manual` at -O0 and -O2 (`keepThrowing(50)` traps 14 at 31 kept errors, and `stillWorks` then gives 30): its 32 pinned pages run out sooner through the TSL route. Diagnosed: the same program with no message agrees, and with JsString's unit chunk patched from 16 pages to 4 (`TSL_TEST_PATCH`) it agrees too, so it is JsString taking its units 16 pages, 64 KiB, at a time, half of this heap (D67). Listed in box 12 (`EXC_KNOWN`), which fails if it goes away; pipe-b box 7 and pipe-d box 3 leave corpus/lower/exc to box 12. Everything else class printing takes, in every other directory, agrees as before.
- **Injected (box 13), on corpus/lower/exc in `leak` at -O2:** the way out taken again before the `finally` code (923 failures in 63 programs), no check after the first call to a program's own throwing function (67 in 6), and a value held across `finally` rethrown as `undefined` (107 in 40): each caught.
- **Speed, `tmk bench memory --classes --exceptions`** (new: bench/exc/exc_cost.ts through both routes, median of 31 after 10, three processes): a call that can throw and doesn't, the same in a `try` and in a `try`/`finally`, 1.00× to 1.01× the direct route at -O1 and -O2 in `leak` and `manual`. The throws (caught 1, 10 and 100 frames up, 20,000 a run) trap 14 through the TSL route in `leak` and through both in `manual`, where nothing is freed: the TSL route's thrown object is a 72-byte `Dyn` (every held class's fields side by side) where the direct route's `Fail` is 56 bytes, both from `__leak_alloc`; that this is why `leak` runs out only through the TSL route is inferred, not shown. Not switched over: every exception program has strings, which aren't `auto`'s (`AUTO_STRINGS`), and the throw path isn't measured.
- **Pins:** none moved. Every lowered program's `auto` tirhash in `leak` and `manual` at -O0 and -O2 (808) is the same with the change and with `TMK_EMIT_EXC=0`, which prints as before: `auto` doesn't print strings, and every exception program has them. New: emit-exc.ts, boxes 12 to 14 and the benchmark's `--exceptions`.

**Pipeline, phase 2, strings as a TSL runtime class (pipe-f), `tmk milestone pipe-d` boxes 9 to 11, MEASURED 2026-11-09** (same host, load 2 to 4 on 10 CPUs for the benchmarks). `@tsl/jsrt`'s `JsString` (D67), and class printing of a lowered program's strings through it.

- **The class:** `packages/tsl-jsrt/ex-jsrt-string.ts`, the spec's block, the one unsafe module of a `leak` package. By hand, `corpus/std/leak/js_string.ts`: the sharing bound at its edges (32 units, a quarter, a view of a view judged against the first owner), substrings reading their owner's units, two appends to one prefix landing in their own places, `for...of` steps over pairs and lone surrogates, a literal's units from its UTF-8, equality and order: 21 cases on HVF and TCG.
- **Printing:** `corpus/lower/pipe/strings.ts` (16 functions, 43 cases with non-ASCII, emoji, lone surrogates and empty strings) prints in 714 lines with no load, store, `text()` or `charTable()`. Before, with classes forced, it couldn't print (a string is a reference the native caller reads); in phase 1's printing a concatenation of a literal reads `strConcat(a, addr(strlit_0, 16))`, a length `load<i32>(a, 0)`, and the literal `const strlit_0 = text("x", "__strlit_0")`. After: `a.concat(strlit_0!)` inside `strConcat`'s length check, `a.length`, and `strlit_0 = JsString.of(lit("x"));` in `__init`.
- **Coverage, with classes forced, `leak` at -O2:** 29 of 139 programs where 27 printed. 24 had a string as their first blocker; 2 print now, and the rest stop next at exceptions (13: `__exc_on` or `__exc_val` module state), maps (`__hash_key`, a `Set`'s void vector), closures, `num.ts`'s typed arrays made in a function, and an optional field. Differential: 116 builds, 14,952 cases at -O0 and -O2 in `leak` and `manual`, all the same, `strings.ts` against V8 as well.
- **Injected:** a pair split (`cpLen` taking two high surrogates as one) and a tail shared (an append without the left side ending at the tail) caught by both the dual route and the hand-written program; a view past the 4× bound by the hand-written program only, as it changes no result.
- **Speed, `tmk bench memory --classes --strings`**, `bench/strmap/str_lowered.ts` (strmap's string work without maps and number text, which class printing doesn't take), median of 101 after 20, three processes, TSL route against direct. First, at -O2: appends 1.80× in `leak` and 1.71× in `manual`, substrings 1.27× and 1.21×, split and join 1.31× and 1.24× (short joins and the scan ran out of the bench image's memory in both routes, and were made smaller). Diagnosed from the machine code (`strConcat` disassembled through both routes at -O2 in `leak`, the append path read instruction by instruction): the TSL route's `strConcat` was 557 instructions to the direct route's 227; each unit address cost about 14 (a range check both ways for `i32` to `usize`, a checked multiply with `umulh` and a 53-bit test, a checked add), 20 such multiplies in all; the length-check wrapper called `concat`, which wasn't inlined, and the one-unit strings went through a `JsArray`. Fixed in TSL proper, in this order: `@tsl.inline` on concatenation's parts and a split fast path for one-unit strings (appends 1.49× and 1.42×); offsets as shifts of values below 2^30 with nothing to check (356 instructions; appends 1.38× and 1.34×); the wrapper keeping only its lets and the check, a raw table for one-unit strings (338); the units' bump inlined. After, -O2, `leak` and `manual`: appends 1.38× and 1.31×, short joins 1.22× and 0.97×, substrings 1.10× and 1.05×, the scan 1.18× and 1.08×, split and join 1.14× and 1.07×. -O1: 1.36× and 1.27×, 1.21× and 0.94×, 1.10× and 1.03×, 1.17× and 1.05×, 1.14× and 1.08×. Not inferred further: that the rest of `leak`'s short joins is the second allocation of a flat string is suggested by `manual`'s being no slower, where the direct route's one allocation is the slower heap's, and isn't shown by a measurement of its own. So `AUTO_STRINGS` is off and `auto` prints no strings; -O0 wasn't measured, being exempt (D44).
- **Pins:** none moved. The lowering's tags change no TIR, `auto` doesn't print strings, and a lowered build's class modes change only builds that import `@tsl/jsrt`, which nothing did before. New: the two programs above, the class, and the benchmark.

**Maps phase, `tmk milestone maps`, MEASURED 2026-11-07** (same host, load 7 to 12 on 10 CPUs during development, so rough). Two maps and incremental growth (D47), `Map` and `Set` opaque at the native boundary (4.5, from design/linking-explore.md's "decide now" list), and fixes. 12 boxes; it runs `lang-a`, which runs the rest.

- `@tsl/std`: `Map` and `Set` are JS's and `ExactMap` is the old trapping map. Oracle: `corpus/std/map_js.ts`, 2,096 cases (every change at every position of a `forEach`, nested ones, `get` of missing scalar and reference values, random programs), whose expected results are JS's own `Map` and `Set` (`tools/std-map-oracle.ts`); the same on V8 running `@tsl/std` and natively. `model.ts` moved to the JS `Map` with `get(k) ?? x`, as its oracle always read it, and gained `exactModel`; the other std programs moved to `ExactMap`, which is what they tested. One existing case changed: `addInSetForEach` trapped 13, and now sees what it adds (`Set` is JS's). `Map<u32, u32>.get` returns two `i32` registers and calls no allocator. The std corpus, 2,371 cases in 21 programs, native against V8 on HVF.
- Lowered `Map` and `Set`: the incremental move. `corpus/lower/maps`, 3,537 cases in 3 programs against V8, in `rc`, its poisoning build, `leak` and `manual`; the existing 9,580 iteration-under-change cases and 698 strmap cases unchanged. No leak over 4 repeats; a 131,072-object map and a 65,536-string set dropped mid-move with a cursor's generation: at most 32 steps an allocation, no full drain.
- **The worst single operation** (`tmk bench maps`, by the counter around each call, HVF): growing to 2^20 entries and one more, `Map<number, number>` 19.2 ms before and 11.0 ms after; string keys 23.4 and 11.1 ms; a `Set` 15.3 and 7.4 ms (at 2^19 it was 8.2 ms, near the 8.6 ms recorded in phase F). What's left is the new table's allocation, zeroed by the test runtime's page source: with that fill taken out, to see it, the worst is 23.5 µs (`Map<number, number>`), 34 µs (a `Set`) and 1.1 ms (string keys, not diagnosed). So the map's own work is bounded and the allocator's zeroing isn't: D47 isn't met in full (3.5). Throughput: a build of 2^20 and a read of each, 85.0 to 114.8 ms (35% slower); a mix of set, get and delete over a window of 64, 64.8 to 74.2 ms (14%): lookups during a move look in two tables, and a move copies and releases each entry once. Not diagnosed further.
- Native boundary: `DownMeta` lists no fields for a map; a guest that walks returned maps through `size`, `has`, `iter`, `step`, `key` and `val` agrees with V8 on 7 of 7, mid-move ones included. The harness's dump reader is the one reader of the layout, by `internal`.
- Lowering gaps (4.5): `cast_unknown.ts`, 37 cases in `rc`, its poisoning build, `leak` and `manual` at `-O0` and `-O2`, and `rc-only/cast_lie.ts`, 11 pinned cases of which 7 trap 17. Found on the way and fixed: a `boolean` in an `unknown` wasn't narrowed, so `String(false)` through one gave `"true"`; `tmkExcDescribe` had the pattern, so the exceptions corpus's pins moved. Not fixed: `if (e)` on an `unknown` still tests only for null, so a boxed `false`, 0 or `""` is truthy where V8's isn't.
- Coverage of the 18 pinned real projects, with methods, constructors and accessors of exported classes counted: 317 lowered and 4,679 fallbacks of what's reached (6.3%) before, 492 and 5,816 (7.8%) after; pixijs 36 to 150 lowered. Same compiler, old tool against new.
- Injected bugs, each caught: a lookup that checks only the new table during a move (75 failures), a move that skips an entry (3,098), `ExactMap` not trapping on a missing key and on a delete during `forEach`, `Map` giving a value for a missing key, compacting during `forEach` (449) or losing its place on `clear` (214), and a cast narrowing that doesn't check (14). The existing runtime faults (a stale cursor, a finished one waking, a deleted entry visited, `-0` kept) are still caught.
- Pins, before the integer fix: strict's all unchanged; in a mode the programs that use `Map` or `Set`, `@tsl/std`'s map, or throw (the `tmkExcDescribe` fix) moved, and no other. The integer fix then moved nearly every lowered program's (below). All are listed in `tools/maps-pins.ts`, with why; TSL proper's `corpus/pos` pins don't move. The maps and exceptions corpora are pinned at `-O0` and `-O2` in `corpus/memory/maps-tirhash.json`.
- **A correctness bug, fixed first** (the coordinator's report): `sumSquares(n)`, summing `i * i` for `i < n`, lowered `s` and `i` to `i32` with checked `mul` and `add`, so `sumSquares(3000)` trapped with code 1 natively where V8 gives 8,995,500,500. Diagnosed: `arith` in `down.ts` gave an integer operation its operands' ranges didn't prove a range clamped to i32 and a check, so the unbounded value never reached the location's facts and the fixed point settled on `i32`; it wasn't the loop or the `f64` bound as such. Fixed: such an operation is `f64`, and a loop's condition now bounds its counter (4.5). `corpus/lower/pos/int_overflow.ts`, 24 cases past 2^31 and 2^53 (sums, products, factorials to 25!, counters from near i32's and 2^53's ends, doubling to 2^60, a length-bounded sum of large elements, negating i32's least), against V8 on Wasm and natively in strict, `rc` and `leak` at `-O0` and `-O2`: all agree, and 12 of 24 failed on the compiler before. Existing programs that passed only because their cases were small: 189 exported functions in the lowered corpora changed from an `i32` result to `f64`. Three tests encoded the bug and changed: `number_int`'s `overflow(3)` expected trap 1 and its header pinned `add.chk.s.i32`, and now gives V8's 3,298,534,883,328 with larger cases added for each function there; `number_float`'s `floorHuge(1.5)` expected trap 4 from `Math.floor(x * 1e10) + 1`, and now gives V8's 15,000,000,001; `grow_reuse` measures freeing in `manual` against `leak` at 40 pages, and its elements became `f64`, which put both at 101 pages, so its push is `(i + r) | 0`, which keeps them `i32` and its cases' results. **The price, MEASURED** (quick runs, load 4 to 5): the JPEG decoder natively 1.231× V8 (0.81× before) and on Wasm 1.447× (G1, 0.95× before); S4's median 1.339× `clang -O2` (1.126×). Gates G1 and S4/G2 still pass (≤ 2×). The decoder's checked i32 operations went from 315 to 3, mostly offsets and fields such as a reader's position, whose bounds the analysis can't see. Pins: nearly every lowered program moved, strict's included, listed in `tools/maps-pins.ts`; TSL proper's didn't.
- The gate: `native-d`'s box 4 at `-O2` alone peaked at 2.46 GiB with 4 suites at once, 2.16 GiB of it the job's own process and 0.36 GiB its QEMUs; 2 compile workers instead of 4 gave 2.45, so they weren't it, and 2 suites at once 2.01 GiB, in 200 s rather than 80. The registry now gives it 2. `--sample` compared lists of suites a 50 ms filter had kept: the opt-a box 4 alarm was 21 suites in one list and 7 in the other with every shared count equal; it now compares counts of the suites both kept.

**Language phase A, `tmk milestone lang-a`, MEASURED 2026-11-06** (same host, load 4 to 15 on 10 CPUs during development, so rough). Exceptions (D49) and class inheritance (D50) in down-lowered code, in `leak`, `manual` and `rc`, by the owner's priority (D48: the language before optimiser phase B). 15 boxes, from `tmk clean`, and it runs `opt-a`, which runs the rest at `-O0` and `-O2`. The result from clean is at the end of this record. It doesn't cover `any` or dynamic values beyond what a thrown value needs, prototypes, `Symbol`, generators, `async`, the library, the Wasm backend (where `try` and `extends` stay fallbacks in `strict`), `ExactMap`, optimiser phase B, TSL proper's exceptions (which keep the trap path) or the kernel.

- Corpus: 16 programs in `corpus/lower/exc`, with no fallback: a parser with error recovery, a validation library with an error hierarchy and causes, a retry loop with a lock released in `finally`, `using` under throw with `SuppressedError`, an interpreter that throws signal objects for `return` and `break`, shapes, an AST with visitors, an event system whose handlers override a base, exceptions through constructors, methods, getters, `map`, `forEach`, `Map` and `Set` callbacks, `for...of` and recursion, every kind of thrown value (strings, numbers including -0, booleans, null, undefined, a user object, each Error class), runtime errors as V8's `RangeError`, a million-node drop by an exception, exhaustion while making an Error, and effects on module state straight after every call to a throwing function (where a missing check would show). Plus 63 generated files, 1,323 functions: every way out (normal, return, break, continue, throw, labelled break and continue) from every position of a `try` sitting in every position of another, 2,646 cases. All agree with V8 in `rc`, its poisoning build, `leak` and `manual`, at `-O0` and `-O2`, on HVF, and on TCG in the milestone.
- Random programs (`tools/exc-fuzz.ts`): 40 at `-O0` and 80 at `-O2`, 395 and 781 cases, 52 and 99 of them thrown to the caller, all agreeing with V8 in the poisoning build at freeing budgets 1 to 32, with nothing alive after a reset that drops every global. Its first versions found nothing in the compiler but two bugs of its own.
- `rc` under exceptions: no leak over 4 repeats in any of the exceptions programs, where a case thrown to the caller now counts, as nothing is left held; the freeing bound with a million-node list dropped by an exception and by a caught error: 32 of 32 steps, no full drain, 2.2 million allocations; every `rc` counter the same at `-O0` and `-O2`, 24 programs, 2,879 cases, 60,339 values.
- Injected bugs, each caught: a missed release on the exceptional path (5 of 40 random programs left an object alive), a missed check after the 1st to the 7th call to a throwing function in a module (a missed check is otherwise hidden: the exception stays in flight and the next check propagates it, so the first run caught the 1st and 2nd but not the 6th, which had nothing observable before the next check; `exc_effects.ts` closes that), `finally` after the way out it should precede, each class given its neighbour's method, `instanceof` without subclasses, and fields before `super()`.
- The optimiser: a throw is two stores and a jump and a check a load and a branch, so no pass needed a change, and the verifier passes after every pass. At `-O2` the inliner inlines throwing callees, cold path and all: `callsRisky` grows from 132 bytes at `-O0` to 564 at `-O2`, where `callsPlain` shrinks from 92 to 68. Outlining the throw path is phase B's.
- **Costs** (`tmk bench exc`, 3 processes, median of 31, load 14.6 falling, so rough), ns per operation, V8 / `-O0` / `-O2`: a call that can't throw 1.86 / 2.48 / 2.17; one that can, and doesn't, 1.93 / 2.56 / 2.24, so the check is about 0.07 ns, inside noise; the same in a `try`/`catch` 1.90 / 2.48 / 2.17, nothing more; in a `try`/`finally` 1.90 / 2.79 / 2.18. Throw and catch 1 frame up 1,327 / 58 / 49; 10 frames 1,992 / 71 / 61; 100 frames 5,436 / 761 / 751, about 7 ns a frame, and 4%, 3% and 14% of V8's time, which builds a stack trace at every `new Error`.
- Coverage (`tmk coverage`, before from the tree as it was): the local corpora as they were before this work, 960 functions lowered of 987 reached, from 955 (96.8% to 97.3%); with this work's corpus, 98.9%, from 40.5%. The 17 pinned real projects: 309 of 4,979 reached functions lower natively (6.2%), from 273 (5.5%). That's low because of what's next in D48, not this: `any-type` 1,162, `unresolved-import` 989 (imports of other packages, which hide 589 more `any-type` and 181 `union-mixed`), `string-use` 542, `unsupported` 486, `union-mixed` 398; 9,809 functions aren't reached from their file's exports, mostly methods of exported classes, which a class export doesn't reach. test262, a 1-in-50 sample of 960 files: 8 of 16 reached functions lower, and 911 are unreached, as a test exports nothing; untyped JS is a later phase's.
- Pins: strict's all unchanged; in a mode, 6 programs move, listed in `tools/lang-a-pins.ts`: 4 that use this (`inheritance`, `try_catch`, `throw_value`, `reflection` for `typeof`) and 2 that reach `toString(radix)`, whose RangeError's message was wrong and is now V8's. The exceptions corpus is pinned in `corpus/memory/lang-a-tirhash.json`.
- Found on the way, and fixed: a block's result that `rc` moves out when the block ends wasn't released when an exception left the block early, a constructor that threw or a `map` callback that threw (3 programs leaked a few objects each repeat); the uncaught report described the value while it was still in flight, so the describing code's own checks left early; the runtime's `toString(radix)` message differed from V8's; siblings' fields of one name and different kinds couldn't share a flow class, which keyed subclass fields; a batch of the generated `finally` tests took longer than a batch's 90 s limit, not a compiler fault: `tmk milestone` verifies the TIR after every pass, which costs about 4 times the compile on a 360,000-instruction file, so the 9 files are now 63 and a batch holds 4 programs. Nested milestones crossed the 3 GiB watchdog (5.5 GB peak in `native-d` alone): V8 lets garbage grow toward a heap limit it isn't near, so a nested milestone's main thread is bounded at 1,536 MB and each compile worker's at 640 MB, and `native-d` now peaks at 2.76 GB; the generated tests are left out of `rc`'s no-leak repeats, which lowered them all in one process, and the lowering memo is bounded by size.
- What didn't work: the first dispatch blocked a function whose receiver's classes weren't known yet in an early round, which the fixed point would have supplied; checking a narrowed `unknown` against its flow class's own classes failed for a class that is only ever thrown, now the checker's class and its subclasses.
- **From clean, 2026-11-07: `tmk milestone lang-a` 15 of 15 boxes in 8,820 s** (load 5 to 8 on 10 CPUs): `opt-a` 17 of 17 in 6,305 s (`native-g` at `-O0` 1,910 s and at `-O2` 2,757 s, everything under each passing); the exceptions corpus, 79 programs and 2,890 cases, in `rc`, its poisoning build, `leak` and `manual` at `-O0` and `-O2` on HVF and TCG; the generated `finally` tests 2,646 cases; random programs 120 at `-O0`, 120 at `-O2` and 20 on TCG, none differing or leaking; no leak in any of the 16 exceptions programs; the bound 32 of 32 steps; counters the same at `-O0` and `-O2`, 60,570 values; 29 calls to throwing functions inlined at `-O2`; every injected bug caught; the D36 trap path; 655 of 685 pins the same, the rest as listed; S4 median 1.121 times `clang -O2` at `-O2` (was 1.126), nothing regressed: `sha256_u32` 1.57, `crc32_table` 0.87, `sort_i32` 1.20, `mandel_f64` 1.05, `matmul_f64` 3.77, `fnv1a` 1.00.

**Class ids don't change, `vec_push`, object keys and the sampler (clsid, D73), MEASURED 2026-11-11** (same host; Spotlight indexing at about one CPU, load 6 to 31 on 10 CPUs during the benchmarks, so ratios are of medians taken back to back; "off" is the same tree with the `invariant` step switched off by name).

- **The rule** (3.4's "Class ids don't change", 3.8, 4.3): a class id's load is `load.T.inv` at -O1 and -O2, shared and moved across calls, intrinsics and stores at other bases. Lowering notes such loads outside the canonical text, so no -O0 TIR or tirhash moves. Unit tests in `compiler/tir/passes/passes.test.ts` (36 in all): sharing across a store elsewhere, a call that writes and a copy, not across a store at its own base over its bytes, the store's value read back, the step off by name and -O0 untouched, and LICM moving one out of a loop that calls. `corpus/std/leak/clsid_shapes.ts` (9 cases: a loop making an object a turn and dispatching on one pet a turn, a field stored after construction by a call, two pets with stores between) agrees with V8 at -O0, -O1 and -O2 on HVF. **Injected** (`clsid-ignore-store`, in OPT_FAULTS, so `opt-a` box 12 runs it): tslc's rule missing a store after construction, which makes `Gauge.level` invariant though `raise` stores it: 2 of the program's 9 cases wrong at -O2 (`gauge` gives -1 where V8 gives 304 and 1,516), none at -O0.
- **Appends, machine code at -O2:** `strConcat` is the same 971 instructions with the step on and off, byte for byte, and so is `appendWork` (90). Its class-id loads were already one per object on each path (the string's, the other's and the buffer's), as value numbering shared them before any store or call; what an append runs is a test of the left string's id for 1 and 2, the right's for 1, the left's for 2 again (that its id is 1 or 2 is known only by the path, which no pass reads), and the buffer's for 3. The right string's id and its test are kept from the first test to the second across the rest of the function, and so spilled and read back from the stack (`ldr w8, [x20]; str x8, [sp, #8]; ldr x16, [sp, #8]`). Neither is a load the rule could share. Where it does change code: the strings module's value numbering shares 214 loads where it shared 187, and unswitching splits 21 loops where it split 12 (`scanWork`'s code 266 to 306 instructions). **Appends measured:** 0.380 and 0.416 ms through the TSL route in `leak` and `manual` against 0.373 and 0.413 off; 1.36× and 1.28× the direct route, 1.37× and 1.29× off.
- **`vec_push` (`tmk bench alloc`, 0.238 to 0.277 ms after check elimination): placement ruled out, the loop's branches confirmed.** Check elimination switched on for every function but `vecPush`: 0.239 ms; only in `vecPush`: 0.277; of its five checks made plain, only the loop counter's (`i + 1` in the latch) matters, and keeping it alone gives 0.238. The two loops' code is the same but for that latch, `adds; b.hs; lsr; cbnz; b` against `add; b`. NOPs before the function, 0 to 15 (64 bytes), 0.238 to 0.242 checked and 0.277 to 0.281 not; 1 to 15 NOPs in the latch where the check was, 0.277 to 0.281; two branches never taken (`cbnz xzr`) in the latch, with 0 to 4 NOPs, 0.238 to 0.241; one or three, 0.275 to 0.280; four, 0.271; two at the head of the latch block, 0.238, at the head of the store's block, 0.274, of the block before it, 0.257. So it isn't the code's address or size, nor the loop's shape, which is unchanged, nor the work, which is less: the time depends on which conditional branches the loop runs, and where. That's the processor's front end or branch prediction, which can't be looked into further here (no performance counters under HVF). Nothing is changed for it: putting branches back would be a measurement's artefact, and other loops gained from the same pass (`slab_add_remove` 1.086 to 0.952 ms, phase B's record). A backend that lays out loops with fewer taken branches is where it would be addressed.
- **Object keys (`obj_lowered.ts`, 1.14× at -O2): where the time goes, shown; why, not all of it.** By phase, through both routes in `leak` (a copy of the benchmark split in six, not in the tree): making the nodes 0.99×, growing the map by `set` 1.84×, `get` 1.73× (by difference), the mixed sets, gets and deletes 0.91×, iterating 0.82×, a Set 1.14×; the same in `manual`. *Not the allocator:* instructions counted under TCG (`TMK_ICOUNT=1`): growth 1.06× in all (1.18× for the map's part), calls counted 1.14×, the allocator's functions under 0.3% of the samples below, and each call takes 2,281,472 bytes from the page source against the direct route's 2,260,248 from the call arena. *Where:* a sampling profile through QEMU's monitor (the PC every few milliseconds, 1,182 samples TSL, 9,209 direct): in growth, the TSL route's `seek` is 30% of its time (0.36 ms), stalled after loading a bucket's head, where the direct route's `find` and `seek` are 0.12 ms; `memset` and `memmove` 0.31 ms against 0.12; `steps` 0.27 against 0.17. In 32 rounds of gets on a built map, `seek` is 68%, most of it after loading the key a head points to. *Shown in part, memory reuse:* the direct route's tables are in the call arena, which the benchmark rewinds between calls, so it uses the same memory each call; with it not rewound, growth goes from 0.668 to 0.913 ms against the TSL route's 1.22, and its `memset` share rises to the TSL route's (36% of 0.913 ms). *Ruled out:* first-touch faults (every page of the guest written before timing: no change), where in RAM (the arena and the page source swapped: no change), cache-set aliasing between the tables (each buffer moved by 64 bytes times one to 15: no change), bucket spread (both hashes simulated: 1.15 probes a hit), skipping the zero fill of fresh buffers (1.22 to 1.205 ms), keeping `JsMap.grow` out of `insert` (1.22 to 1.19), and constant-offset addresses kept unshared by value numbering, which halves the stack reloads of spilled addresses (39 to 19) and gives 1.185 ms. *Not shown:* why the same lookups stall longer: the gap grows with the table (gets 1.15× at 500 entries, 1.39× at 2,000, 1.67× at 20,000), and isn't freshness, as the direct route's gets on memory it didn't rewind are 6.03 ms against 5.77. The TSL route's tables are page-aligned buffers from the global allocator, the direct route's packed in the arena (read from the guest's registers and memory through the monitor), but moving the buffers didn't change it. Nothing is fixed for it.
- **The sampler:** `native-c` box 1 quotes `tmk lower --memory rc`'s output, a path in its job's directory cut at 120 characters, so where the cut falls moves with the directory's length. The registry marks it `quotesTool`, and `tmk gate --sample` compares its verdict, the counts in its detail (each `n/m`) and its suites' counts, not its words (`detailCounts`, with a test from the sample that differed).
- **Strings, exceptions and maps through both routes**, `tmk bench memory --classes`, TSL route against direct, `leak` and `manual`: at -O2, appends 1.36×, 1.28×; short joins 1.06×, 0.95×; substrings 1.08×, 1.05×; scan 1.07×, 1.03×; split and join 1.06×, 1.06× (off: 1.37×, 1.29×; 1.09×, 0.95×; 1.08×, 1.03×; 1.10×, 1.03×; 1.11×, 1.06×). At -O1: 1.39×, 1.33×; 1.12×, 0.98×; 1.08×, 1.04×; 1.10×, 1.04×; 1.18×, 1.10×. Exceptions (a 1 GiB guest), every row 0.86× to 1.02× at -O2, on and off, and 0.87× to 1.02× at -O1. Maps (1 GiB) at -O2: number keys 1.05×, 1.06×; object keys 1.14×, 1.14×; `growth_lowered.ts` build and read 1.03×, 1.01×, mix 1.11×, 0.99×; strmap's string-keyed mix 1.19×, 1.20×; word count 1.07×, 1.08×; number-keyed mix 1.01×, 1.02×; Set 1.02×, 1.00×. At -O1: 1.13×, 1.13×; 1.26×, 1.25×; 1.14×, 1.12×; 1.25×, 1.11×; 1.32×, 1.30×; 1.29×, 1.27×; 1.06×, 1.05×; 1.04×, 1.04×. **So nothing switches on:** appends, object and number keys and string keys miss the rule at both levels, `AUTO_STRINGS` and `AUTO_MAPS` stay off, and exceptions, which print only with strings, with them. `auto` class-prints 9 of 184 lowered builds in `leak` and 9 in `manual` at -O2 (corpus/lower and bench's `_lowered.ts`), none with a `JsString`, `JsMap` or `JsSet`, as before.
- **Pins:** none at -O0, by construction. Of the 1,846 pinned -O1 and -O2 tirhashes, 28 move (`tools/clsid-pins.ts`, which computes every one with the step off and on): seven down-lowered programs with class ids in `leak` and `manual` at -O1 and -O2 (`corpus/lower/fallback/escape_global.ts`, `throw_value.ts`, `try_catch.ts`, `corpus/lower/memory/grow_reuse.ts`, `corpus/lower/rc/adv_large_drop.ts`, `adv_temporaries.ts`, `cyc_large.ts`), each listed in `tools/clsid-moved.ts`; none of the files compared exactly.

**Optimiser phase B, in `tmk milestone opt-a`'s boxes, MEASURED 2026-11-11** (same host; Spotlight indexing at one to two CPUs, load 2 to 10 during the benchmarks, so ratios are of medians taken back to back, and "before" is the same tree with phase B switched off by name on the same day). D73's passes (4.3): value numbering, loop-invariant code motion, unswitching, peeling and check elimination, with `range.ts`'s proofs and `memory.ts`'s writes. Built in two parts, B1 (value numbering and LICM, with unswitching and peeling) and B2 (check elimination, and LICM's proofs of a loop's first turn), each ending at the full gate from clean.

- **Tests.** 19 new unit tests in `compiler/tir/passes/passes.test.ts` (37 in all): what each pass shares, moves, copies or proves, and what it mustn't (a load across a store to the same bytes, a call that writes, a load `-O0` dropped standing for a later one before a check, a load that can fault behind the loop's test, a check after another that could trap, `i <= n` against a bounds check, `x + 648` one past its limit). The random TIR (`tools/tir-fuzz.ts`) generates phase B's patterns: loops reading one element every turn through a pointer that's null exactly when the loop runs no turn, in the header or behind the test, after a check that can fire, with the loop writing that element, the next or one it computes; one element loaded twice with a store there, next to it, through a computed index, in one arm of an if/else, a call that writes or one that only reads between; a load `-O0` drops before a bounds check that can fire and the same load used; loops testing an element every turn; induction variables counting below, to or one past a length with `<` or `<=`; `x & (n - 1)` against `n` or a smaller length; and checked adds and subtracts within seven of their limit behind `<` or `<=`. With no V8, at `-O0`, `-O1` and `-O2`: 200 seeds (1,600 cases) on the final tree all the same, and 300 more (2,400) on the way. **Injected bugs, each caught by the first step of `opt-a`'s fault box** (random TIR, 30 seeds): value numbering merging two loads across a store that changes them (24 cases differ); LICM moving a load out of a loop that writes it (30) and above its loop's guard (4); check elimination removing a bounds check whose index may equal the length (25) and an overflow check one past its limit (8).
- **Found on the way:** a preheader made by LICM shared one array between its parameters and its jump's arguments, so a later substitution on the edge rewrote its parameters (the verifier caught it in a unit test, before any program hit it); a self-proof, where a bounds check's own result was used to prove it in its block (caught on `matmul` at once, fixed by taking such facts only from strictly dominating blocks); and the class test's compare, left in a loop as cheap, needed unswitching to lift it.
- **The JPEG decoder, B1 as first gated:** 5% slower (1.33× to 1.38× V8), MEASURED, with LICM moving every invariant value out of loops: switched off one at a time, value numbering alone made it 11% faster and LICM 18% slower; `decodeScan` spilled 43 values with LICM, 25 without (the backend's own count). LICM now moves a cheap pure operation only where a load, a check or dearer arithmetic it moves needs it: 29 spilled, and the decoder 1.17× V8.
- **Targets, machine code at -O2** (the report gives the listings): `matmul`'s inner loop from 33 instructions with 7 checks to 24 with 5: `k + 1` proved (`k < n`, `n` a usize, D23) and `i * n` moved out of both inner loops (first on the first turn, `j < n` and `k < n` proved on entry from `i < n`); the rest (`i * n + k`, `k * n`, `k * n + j`, two bounds checks) depend on `n` against the arrays' lengths, which nothing proves. `sha256`'s module: 19 checked operations and 15 bounds checks proved (every index of `W`, `K` and `BLOCK` in `compress` by its loop's bound), its code 541 instructions before, 509 after B1, 412 after B2. `JsMap.seek`: the checked `heads.length - 1` (proved by `b === 0` above it) and the mask's bounds test (`x & (b - 1) < b`) gone, and a chain step's four length and data loads gone (peeled: the first step reads them, the rest reuse them); the two bounds tests left take an index from the chain's data. `JsString`'s scan: the class test unswitched, the length read once, and `charCodeAt`'s float index tests and bounds test proved, so a turn is the program's own arithmetic and one load; `toUsize(n) * 2` a plain multiply (`n` at most 2^31 − 1 after its range check, which stays: `n` isn't known not negative). Appends: class tests in `strConcat` from 9 loads of a class id to 6 after B1, the rest on different objects, or the same one across a store through another base, which may alias.
- **S4 at -O2:** median 1.126× `clang -O2` before, 1.131× after B1, 1.135× after B2: `sha256_u32` 1.57×, 1.58×, 1.24×; `crc32_table` 0.87×, 0.88×, 0.87×; `sort_i32` 1.21×, 1.23×, 1.24×; `mandel_f64` 1.05×, 1.03×, 1.03×; `matmul_f64` 3.75×, 3.71×, 2.62×; `fnv1a` 1.00× throughout. The median is `sort_i32` and `mandel_f64`'s, which phase B doesn't reach. **JPEG natively:** 1.31× to 1.33× V8 before, 1.38× after B1 as gated, 1.16× to 1.18× after B2 (tower-portrait 7.82, 8.20, 6.94 ms); its code 38,584 bytes to 37,504.
- **Strings, exceptions and maps through both routes**, `tmk bench memory --classes`, TSL route against direct, `leak` and `manual`, before / after B1 / after B2, at -O2: appends 1.36×, 1.29× / 1.33×, 1.32× / 1.37×, 1.27×; short joins 1.09×, 0.96× / 1.08×, 0.96× / 1.08×, 0.95×; substrings 1.09×, 1.05× / 1.10×, 1.06× / 1.08×, 1.03×; scan 1.09×, 1.04× / 1.12×, 1.06× / 1.11×, 1.04×; split and join 1.13×, 1.08× / 1.12×, 1.08× / 1.11×, 1.06×. At -O1 after B2: 1.35×, 1.28×; 1.12×, 0.99×; 1.09×, 1.04×; 1.10×, 1.03×; 1.16×, 1.10×. Exceptions (a 1 GiB guest), every row 0.84× to 1.03× at both levels, before and after. Maps (1 GiB) at -O2 before / after: number keys 1.06×, 1.05× / 1.06×, 1.06×; object keys 1.16×, 1.16× / 1.15×, 1.14×; `growth_lowered.ts` build and read 1.01×, 1.02× / 1.02×, 1.01×, mix 1.14×, 0.99× / 1.10×, 0.98×; strmap's string-keyed mix 1.20×, 1.22× / 1.20×, 1.20×; word count 1.23×, 1.21× / 1.22×, 1.22×; at -O1 after: 1.14×, 1.13×; 1.26×, 1.25×; 1.13×, 1.12×; 1.24×, 1.11×; 1.30×, 1.28×; 1.29×, 1.27×. **Why the ratios hardly move:** the direct route goes through the same optimiser, and gains as much (scan 0.252 to 0.247 ms direct, 0.274 to 0.273 ms TSL; object keys 3.72 to 3.75 ms direct, 4.33 to 4.30 ms TSL); and the loops phase B rewrote are a small part of these benchmarks: `scanWork` spends most of its time building its string by appends before the four scans, and the map benchmarks theirs outside `seek`. **So nothing switches on:** `AUTO_STRINGS` and `AUTO_MAPS` stay off (appends 1.27× to 1.37×, object keys 1.14× to 1.26×, string keys 1.20× to 1.30×, number keys 1.05× to 1.14×), and exceptions, which print only with strings, stay off with them; `auto`'s class printing is unchanged, as no `AUTO_` switch moved. What's left in machine code: an append makes up to five class tests on its operands and an owner, of which value numbering shares only those on one object with no store between (a store of units through the buffer's data pointer, another base, may alias a class id); `seek`'s two bounds tests a step take indexes from the chain, which nothing bounds; the rest of the object-keyed gap isn't diagnosed.
- **The other benchmarks at -O2,** before / after B2: `tmk bench alloc` `vec_push` 0.238 / 0.277 ms (16% slower: with check elimination switched off alone it's 0.238; its TIR differs only in three checked adds and two checked multiplies made plain, 21 instructions fewer; the cause isn't diagnosed), `slab_add_remove` 1.086 / 0.952, `stored_ref_walk` 0.344 / 0.343; `tmk bench std` `vecPushRead` 0.370 / 0.327, `setDedupe` 0.721 / 0.643, `wordCount` 5.06 / 4.81, `sortWork` 20.0 / 18.1 ms; `tmk bench memory`, `strmap` and `exc` within 3% either way on every row (strmap's `numTextRandom` 6.69 / 6.47, `mapStrMix` 2.31 / 2.42).
