The level reaches the backend as `Module.opt`, which isn't printed, and beside a `.tir` file as a `.opt` file where a suite reads TIR back from text. Each part switches off by name (`TMK_OPT_DISABLE`), and each has an injected bug that's caught (`b3-global-addend`, `b3-thread-invert`, `b3-fuse-invert`, `b3-remat-stale`, `b3-layout-stale-next`, opt-a box 12). The runtime and the driver are the same at every level. **R7, `nullchecks`:** an explicit null check (`brif` on `icmp.eq x, 0` to a block that only traps with code 6) whose other side is reached from it alone and runs nothing but pure operations before a load through `x` plus a constant offset below 64 KiB becomes a jump, and the load is listed in the image's table `__rt_null_pcs` with that offset; `__rt_exception` takes a data abort at a listed load, at exactly its offset, for trap 6 (`__rt_null_listed`), inside a driver's case or outside one, so a null reference reports what the check reported, and a fault through a non-null bad address (`manual` or unsafe code) is the full report as at -O0. A listed load the selection then drops or computes again at its uses puts its check back. The table is the backend's, so the TIR and its tirhash don't move; Wasm, whose loads near 0 read memory, never sees it. Its injected bug (`b3-null-past-store`: a store before the load passed over) is caught by tools/r7-tests.ts (opt-a box 12, pipe-d box 32). **R19:** the load may be through the reference's address (`ref.addr`, a reference with a generation tag masked off), as through the reference itself: null's address is 0, so that load faults at its offset, the same trap 6; machine code only, so no tirhash moves (a class printed in `rc` read after a `!`, relative_import.ts's module state). **R21, `shrinkwrap`:** an entry block that tests and either returns at once or goes on to work that needs a frame runs its quick way before the prologue, and the prologue is at the head of the other way, the quick way's return a bare `ret`: only where the entry has no predecessor and each way has the entry as its only one, and nothing on the quick way calls or touches the stack (every value it reads or writes, the arguments' moves, both edges' moves and the results in registers the caller doesn't need kept, every instruction one that computes, compares, converts, loads, stores or checks, and a frame slot the entry gives used on neither, its address worked out after the prologue in the register it had). A call that can throw, which almost never does, is then the direct route's 11 instructions down to 7 through both routes (the backend is both routes'). Machine code only, so no tirhash moves; its injected bug (`r21-shrinkwrap-callee`: a callee-saved register taken as free) is caught by corpus/lower/r21/r21_quick.ts (pipe-d box 62, opt-a box 12). | A base register holding a function's global area: one register lost everywhere, for the one instruction an access saves, which `adrp` with a `lo12` offset saves with none, and globals spread over pages. Jump threading in the TIR: every -O1 and -O2 tirhash would move, and the Wasm and C backends don't need it. Rematerialising any plain load, or a class id's load across a call: a store or a free in between could change what it reads. Copying a block to thread through one with its own work: code growth for a branch. NOPs to align loop heads: the class-id round measured them changing nothing for `vec_push`. | Delegated (decisions.md 2026-12-03: one backend round, B3, before R2). |
| D76 | Tests made faster by doing each thing once (owner, 2026-11-16, "it takes days to make progress"; round T1). Inside one run, a build store makes each compile and each pure child's output (the pins tools, a program's source on V8 or JSC, a printed package on them) once and hands it to every later asker; it lives in the run's own directory and is removed at its end, a sixteenth of its reuses are made again and compared by value, a difference fails the run, and units that measure, time compiles or need a still host run without it (8.3). `--changed` selects by declaration in the test code, checked against V8's coverage of what a job runs (8.3). opt-a box 12's injected bugs each run in a process of their own, two at once (four loaded a gate enough that `pipe-d` box 40's images ran past their 60 s limit), each with a build directory of its own, the box put together from their rows as before. One `ps` a period for every guarded child of a process, not one each. `tmk gate --sample` compares a speed box by its verdict and the decisions its registry entry names (`AUTO_RC on`), not by its measurement's lines. Nothing is tested less: the same programs, cases, levels, comparisons, pins and injected bugs, every QEMU run. T2 (2026-11-16): what a compile asks of the libraries is done once a process (their parsed and bound modules by text, module and lib resolution from them, a package's tsl.json once a compile), and the printer's rounds of `!` sites stop before elaboration; one compile in 16 is made again with all of that off (`TMK_COMPILE_REUSE=off`) and compared, a difference a store mismatch. A reference run's transpile is kept in the run's store, checked as its builds are. The dual route builds on the compile workers, a few ahead, each worker taking every `TMK_*` and `TSL_*` the test process has; `pipe-d` box 13's and `native-f` box 9's bugs run in parts, two at once, as `opt-a` box 12's; the hosted runtime writes when its buffer fills, not a line at a time (8.3). R12 (2026-11-16): a run's CPU budget, a token a core served by the pool and taken by every leaf of every job (a compile on a worker, a QEMU run, a compile batch, a reference engine's or a pins tool's run) before its time limit starts, the longest job's leaves first, so lanes × workers × parts × QEMUs stay within the cores; at most two of the dual route's builds at once in a process, and `lang-a` box 10 two suites at once, so no job nears the watchdog; and what an injected bug's run counts as caught by a wrong answer is load-independent: a child killed at its wall-clock limit ran out of time, a program whose reference didn't finish isn't compared case by case with nothing, and a case a route's run never reached because it ran out of time isn't a wrong answer (8.3). | Results reused across runs (D45's reasons stand: a run from clean couldn't use them, and a stale pass is a new way to be wrong); a store that outlives a run; reusing QEMU runs (about 60 ms each, and each is a check); a smaller test matrix (owner, 2026-11-16); the bugs as gate jobs of their own (job keys are parsed by the registry, the views, the sampler and verify-manifest; parts inside the job give the same parallelism); larger V8 young generations (2% of a compile's CPU, MEASURED). T2: the library modules' checking cached by content across processes (it was 2 to 5% of a compile, and a cache outliving a run is what D45 rejected); stopping the `!` rounds before the `rc` expansion (its tsc errors would be lost, so not provably the same); more parts at once. | Built, 2026-11-16 (T1); T2 built 2026-11-16; for the coordinator to verify. |
| D77 | Fresh-allocation separation (R27; the owner's option 1, 2027-01-01, taken up 2027-01-17). A block from the allocator that only one class's fields hold, and only that class's code reaches, holds no object, so a store into it changes no object's field and an object's field's store doesn't change it. The optimiser keeps a field's read (an array's length, a map's state) across such stores, and across a call that writes only such blocks, and a check the kept value proves goes by the proofs already there (D44, D73): nothing unchecked is added, and a check goes only where proved. **tslc's rule** (compiler/host/separate.ts, whole-program, after `markInvariantFields`): a field F of a class C is separated where (1) F is a `u64` held by value, and C isn't a layout class and has no tail; (2) only C's own methods read or write F; (3) everything they store in F is 0, a fresh block (@tsl/alloc's `Heap.allocBytes`, the per-call region's `callRegionBytes`) or a value read from a separated field of C (a block moved between C's objects, as `adopt` and `swap` move one), and every value worked out from one (a block value) is used only as the address of C's own reads and writes of elements that are numbers or references (never an object in place, `inlineOf`), as a copy's or a fill's address, as `addrInCallRegion`'s or `Heap.freeBytes`' argument, in a compare, stored into a separated field of C or a local, passed between C's own methods, or as a method's result only C's methods take: never stored anywhere else, given to any other code, or used to make, place or view an object; (4) C's methods use no other @tsl/unsafe operation that names memory (`addrOf`, `slotOf`, `viewAt`, `objectAt`, ...) and make no closure, and nothing takes one of them as a value; (5) no object of C, or holding one in place, is an element in place or viewed at an address. So a block a separated field holds can be reached only through C's methods, and no object is ever in one. **The optimiser** (compiler/tir/passes/memory.ts): lowering notes a separated field's read and every object field's read and write, outside the canonical text, as it notes a class id's (D73), so -O0's TIR and every tirhash at -O0 are as they were. An address worked out from a separated field's read (an offset, a cast, an add of one and something that isn't one, a block parameter every edge gives one) is in a separated block, and an access there and an object's field's, a global's or a frame slot's never alias; a call writes only separated blocks where the callee and everything it calls store nowhere but their own frame slots and such blocks (a write summary, settled over the call graph), and such a call, or a fill or copy into a block, changes no object's field. Value numbering, LICM and peeling read writes this way at -O1 and -O2. **What it rests on:** the allocators give a block that no live object or other live block shares until it's given back (@tsl/alloc's `Heap`, the per-call region; their SAFETY comments); C's own unsafe code keeps its SAFETY comments: an address it works out from a block stays inside that block, and a block goes back only once no separated field holds it and isn't used after; @tsl/unsafe's object operations move and name whole objects (`placeObject`'s copy of a moved object into a slot, `objectAt` of a placed one), the copy a move leaves behind never read again (tslc's moves rule); and in `manual`, nothing uses an object after `unsafeFree` (that mode's own contract). Lowered code can't import @tsl/unsafe (TSL1023), so in a lowered package only the libraries' classes can have such a field: @tsl/jsrt's `JsArray.data`, a JsMap's tables among them. **Where it doesn't apply** (r27_sep_neg.ts): a block whose address leaves its class, before or after it's filled, or that's stored in another object's field and read back from there, isn't separated; a call that writes a field keeps every read of one after it. Injected bugs, each caught by wrong answers: a summary missing a write, an alias the separation misses, an escape let through (`tmk milestone pipe-d` boxes 73 and 74, opt-a box 12; M5's R27 record). | A lowered-only unchecked `get` (the owner, 2027-01-01: never). Type-based alias analysis over TIR: TIR has no types on memory; this notes the one fact it needs where tslc proved it. Taking every block from `allocBytes` as separated: a block whose address escapes may hold a viewed or placed object, and a store through it would then change a field the optimiser kept. Proving a map lookup's chain positions in range: that's a fact about a table's contents, which no separation gives (R27's measurement, M5's record). | The owner's ruling, 2027-01-01 (option 1: the optimiser rule, fresh-allocation separation with per-call write summaries), and go-ahead, 2027-01-17; the rule's design delegated |
| D78 | References with no tag, and module state written once (R28, 3.5; M5's R28 record). A lowered `rc` package's heap class (expand-rc.ts's `loweredRcHeapClass`: counted exactly, never `@tsl.stack`, every object in a slot a store's `make` placed) whose references are untagged (R8's `untaggedCounted`) has every reference to it be its object's address, by construction: `placeObject`, `placeTail` and `objectAt` of it give the address, and callRelease's arm for it hands its release function the object as an address (from the slot where the call is given `objectAt` itself, else masked). So its fields are read and written, and its slot found, with no mask. A lowered package can't import @tsl/unsafe (TSL1023), so it can't make one otherwise, and the libraries holding them store and load them whole. A module variable that only its module's top-level `__init` writes, and that nothing calls, is given to a call borrowed, with no count around the call, as no code that runs after `__init` can overwrite it. No check is removed: the mask was never one. No freeing step moves (D39, D41): a count not taken isn't given back, and such a variable's object never reaches zero. | Keeping the mask (R19): relative_import's one instruction a read, and one in every count change, for a tag nothing reads. A release function given a tagged object, its class's reads masked only there: a second form of every field access. Taking every module variable as stable: a call can overwrite one (corpus/lower/r28's `overwriteWhileBorrowed`), and its old value would be freed under the call (the injected bug `r28-init-any`, caught). Literals as static objects, as the direct route has them: a second kind of reference to a lowered class, which would bring the tag back. | The owner's rule (2026-11-17): a check or mask goes only by a proof that it can't matter; this is that proof, delegated |
| D79 | The table-links proof (R29, 3.5, 4.3; the owner's ruling of 2027-01-21 asked for it; M5's R29 record). A class's `@tsl.links l... < b...` claim, that every link its link fields' arrays hold (a `u32` from 2 to 2^31 - 1, naming position link - 2) is below every bound field's array's length, is proved by tslc over every write to them, and a JsArray read it then shows in bounds loses its leading check where the inliner copies it, at -O1 and -O2. **tslc's rule** (compiler/host/links.ts, whole-program, after D77's): (1) each claimed field is @tsl/jsrt's `JsArray` held in place, a link field's of `u32`; (2) the fields are named only in the class's methods (every instance of its declaration) and its group functions (module functions every call of which, all in the class's methods, passes one group's fields in the same places; never exported or a value), and only as a JsArray method's receiver, a local const naming one, an argument of one of the class's methods (followed into at each call) or of a group function, or what another array's `adopt` takes from; no object of the class, or holding one in place, is an element in place or viewed; (3) following each method statement by statement from the claim holding (a constructor's arrays all new), each link field is empty, valid or broken, and: a value stored into one (`set`, `push`) is 0, 1, at least 2^31 (`(c \| x) >>> 0` with c's top bit set), a value read from the group's link fields since its bounds last got shorter, or `(p + 2) >>> 0` with p known below every bound's length; a bound that may get shorter (`setLength`, `trim`, `adopt` from it, a new array) breaks every link field of its group that isn't empty; a link field `trim`med, adopted from, newly made or given length 0 is empty; a run of swaps keeps a group only where it swaps every field of one group with the same place in another; (4) no link field is broken at a return, at a call of the class's own method (unless it only reads) or a group function, or at a call of code that may reach the class's methods (whole-program; a function value reaches only the functions of its type taken as values, a down-lowered closure call anything), and after such a call nothing is known but that the claim holds; (5) a position is known below a length after a bounds-checked access there (`get`, `set`, `zero`), a test against the length, as the length read before a `push` onto that array, or as `(s - 2) >>> 0` for an s read from a link field under a test below 2^31 - 2, while the claim holds. **What's marked:** a JsArray `get`, `set` or `zero` on a claimed field whose index (3, 5) shows below that field's length in every way it's reached (`call.inb`), and JsArray's leading checks (`cmp.chk`); lowering notes both outside the canonical text, and the inliner (4.3) copies such a call with the check's test false. **What it rests on:** JsArray's methods do what D66 and their SAFETY comments say (a bounds check traps past the length, `push` adds one, `setLength` keeps what's below and adds zeros, `trim` and `adopt` empty the array, `swap` exchanges two whole arrays, `reserve` changes no element); its buffer is reached only by its own methods (D77's `JsArray.data`); objects are moved whole (D77's rule 5); in `manual`, nothing uses an object after `unsafeFree`; and the class's own code is what it's proved to be. Lowered code can't name a JsMap's fields (they're private, and tslc's rule refuses one named outside), so it can't break the claim. **Where it doesn't apply** (corpus/r29/r29_links_neg.ts): a link stored past its key, the keys cut with links left, half a table swapped, the keys cut from outside, a read after a call that may empty the table; each keeps its checks. Injected bugs, each caught by wrong answers or traps: the rule letting any stored value through, missing a bound getting shorter or half a swap, missing a field named outside, and the inliner taking every call's check out (`tmk milestone pipe-d` boxes 77 and 78, opt-a box 12). | A lowered-only unchecked `get` (the owner, 2027-01-01: never). Proving the claim in the optimiser, over TIR: the fact is about a class's private fields, which only tslc sees whole. Taking `vals` as a bound: a Set's table has none, so the claim would be false. | The owner's ruling, 2027-01-21 ("Then build the table-links proof"); the rule's design delegated |
| D80 | Values split around cold calls (R30, 4.4; M5's R30 record). At -O1 and -O2 the AArch64 backend's allocator takes a call to be cold where its block isn't on every turn of its innermost loop, or, outside loops, isn't on every way out of the function but a quick way out (a block that only returns, reached by a conditional branch); `native.try` is never cold, and `trap.code` keeps nothing. A value live across cold calls only may then take a register a call clobbers, stored to a slot of its own before each such call (before its arguments are moved) and loaded back after it (after its results are moved); a value live across any other call takes a callee-saved register as before. And a bare-metal frame with no outgoing stack arguments puts its saved registers at its bottom, so its first pair's store makes the whole frame. Coldness is a static guess: it decides only what's saved where, never what's computed, so a wrong guess costs time and never a result. MEASURED (HVF, interleaved with the tree before): the JPEG decoder natively 2.4% faster at -O2 and 0.2% slower at -O1 (6.81 → 6.83 ms on tower-portrait, under the timers' noise but the same way each run), S4's median the same at both. **R31, quick ways out that return a constant:** a block that makes only the constants it returns is a quick way out, as an empty one is. Still only what's saved where. MEASURED (HVF, tower-portrait, nine interleaved runs): the JPEG decoder at -O1 7.050 → 6.989 ms (7.022 with no split), at -O2 6.995 → 6.995 ms (7.179 with no split), so R30's -O1 loss is won back and -O2 keeps its gain (4.4). | Intervals with holes and a general splitting allocator: a rewrite of the allocator for what saves around a few calls give. Branch weights from a profile: there's no profile at -O1. Splitting only where it saves a callee-saved register: it lost -O2's 2.4% on the JPEG decoder, where every register is taken either way and the split values were spilled before. A cost check keeping a value made outside a loop callee-saved across a cold call inside it (R31): JPEG -O2 0.3% faster, but the `rc` runtime's freeing and lookups saved more registers again, and adv_forof_mutation at -O2 went over 1.00. | Delegated (the coordinator's 2027-01-25 brief: "split such values around cold calls") |
### Open questions, with defaults

| Question | Default if unanswered |
|----------|----------------------|
| Should a successful L0 feed Moire hot paths (image decoders, damage)? | Yes, as a separate later Moire decision; nothing here depends on it, and Moire stays unchanged |
| Keep `el1-domain` at all? | Decide at M11 on data |
| Is M10 worth doing? | Decide after M9, with S11 and real effort data |
| Do TSL programs need growable lists over an arena? | No until M3 and M6 show the need. It's the first thing to add if fixed capacity feels too much like C |
| Does ordinary TS need a runtime for escaping allocations? | Closed, 2026-11-03: it needs a declared memory mode (D28, D38), and the runtime is a page source and an allocator, with no collector. `rc` is built (D39) |
| Does `rc` need a cycle collector? | Closed, 2026-11-05: yes, the owner's call, and it's built and on by default (D41, 3.5). What's left is stated there: the worst shape for marking is quadratic, and a large cycle in a program flooding the candidate table can wait for exhaustion |
| Should `rc` have threads, or `Map`, `Set`, run-time strings and copy-on-write? | `Map`, `Set` and strings: closed, 2026-11-05, built (D42), and not over `@tsl/alloc`, for the reason in 4.5. Copy-on-write: strings only. Array copies across the corpus are too short to gain, and a shared buffer costs the collector and the ABI (M5, Phase F). The owner may want to overrule that for a program with large read-only copies. Threads: closed by D40, 2026-11-05: no ordinary reference crosses, with an opt-in shared type |
| D42: `Map`, `Set` and strings in `compiler/rt`, not over `@tsl/alloc`? | Still the owner's, and evidence is in. It held: `@tsl/std` built them over `@tsl/alloc` for TSL proper, which works because a stored reference there is a plain value, and it's 1.6 to 3.4× slower than `rc`'s on the same work (3.5, M5's Phase G). Default: keep |
| Which allocator algorithm? | Not pluggable: a program names a page source, and `Heap` is the algorithm (D43). Default: leave it until a program needs another |
| Should a `Vec` be returnable in `strict`? | It's a stack object, and has a stack object's rules, so a program uses a `Slab<Vec<T>>`, an out parameter, or `leak`. Default: leave it. A value type that moves on return would be a new rule |
| Should `@tsl/std` have threads' per-thread storage? | When threads exist (M6, D40). What it'll take is in 3.5, and `Shared<T>` is written down there |
| Should a guest get entropy to key its hash tables with? | Open. `__hash_key_use` is there for a caller that has some, and with no caller a fixed default stands: hash flooding on untrusted keys is possible until the environment offers a source (D42) |
| Should a `Map` allow values that can be `null`? | Open. `get` needs three states and has two, so it's `nullish-both` today. Default: leave it until a real program needs it |
| Should down-lowering build the environment struct in 4.5's table, for closures that are stored or returned? | Closed, 2026-11-03: yes, in `leak` and `manual` (4.5). In `strict` they stay a fallback, which is a hard error natively |
| Who owns a down-lowered function's returned objects natively, and how should its 40-odd call-arena allocation sites square with D28? | Decided (D36, 4.5): a caller-supplied arena. They live there until the caller resets it. In `leak` and `manual` a result is long-lived instead, and survives the reset (4.5, D38). In `rc` the caller owns one count, and has `__rc_release` (4.5, D39) |
| How should a stored reference to a `manual` object look to a package that isn't `manual`? | Closed, 2026-11-03: it can't get one stored (TSL3008). If an API needs to hand out identity, it hands out a value a safe wrapper checks |
| Two known silent divergences in down-lowering: a field read through a lying cast gives 0, not `undefined`; a returned object can show extra zero fields when a wider shape was unified into its type | Closed, 2026-11-03: both are now fallbacks with a root cause (`unsound-cast`, `shape-widened`, 4.5), with tests in `corpus/lower/fallback`. Neither program can reach native code, where fallback is a hard error |
| Is agreement with one engine's `Math` in the last bit worth having? | Closed, 2026-11-03: yes, against V8 on the development host, and `pow` within 1 ulp. Accepted by the owner, delegated to the author (3.10, item 7) |

## 12. Risks and the smallest worthwhile version

### 12.1 Ranked risks

| # | Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|------|-----------|-------|-----------|
| 1 | **Scope.** A new language compiler, OS kernel and bootstrap chain are each large. Midori took about 8 years and man-decades, with a team, to close the performance gap [P3]. | High | Fatal to the full vision | Gates and the 12.2 stopping points. Every level is useful alone. |
| 2 | **The radical idea doesn't pay for itself.** Specialisation gains may be tiny in a microkernel (6.1), and the seed removes binary blobs but not the need to review source. | High | Removes M9 and M10 value | G5 and G6 measure it. Dropping them keeps most of the value. |
| 3 | **A miscompile undermines security.** | Medium, high over time | High | EL0 default, `bincheck`, differential fuzz, DDC. Residual risk accepted and stated. |
| 4 | **TSL is unpleasant to write** (`>>> 0`, no exceptions, fixed capacities). Version 2 fixed the worst of this with classes, closures and implicit widening. Could still hurt the kernel and especially the self-hosted compiler. | Medium | Medium | Porting from TS incrementally; relax the rules with data; keep the checker's rules simple. Reviewed at M3 and M8. |
| 5 | **Down-lowering breadth.** Real TS has unbounded ways to defeat static analysis. AssemblyScript, Porffor and Static Hermes all show the difficulty; none is a drop-in static TS compiler as of this writing [P26][P27][P28]. | Medium to high, given no runtime in v1 | High: it's the main path outside the kernel, though it doesn't block the kernel | Gate G1, the native JPEG check at M5, and D28's runtime as the fallback plan. |
| 6 | **Native backend quality** vs a mature compiler. Simple register allocation may leave 2× or more on the table. | Medium | Medium | G2 thresholds. Kernel code is load-store and branch heavy, so it's less sensitive than numerics. |
| 7 | **Two frontends drift** (`tslc-host` vs `tslc`) | Medium | Medium | `tirhash` equality in CI |
| 8 | **Language design error found late**, such as escape rules being too limiting for driver code | Medium | Medium | The M3 examples are compiled, and M4 and M6 use the language at once. Fix before M8 freezes much code. |
| 9 | **Spectre variants or HVF oddities.** Example already seen: `PFR0.GIC` reads 0 while GICv3 works. | Medium | Low to medium | Test HVF and TCG. Read ID registers only where verified. |
| 10 | **TS tooling churn.** TS 7 changes the API surface. | High | Low | Confined to `compiler/host`, pinned |
| 11 | **Seed chain freeze** stops language evolution | Medium | Medium | TSL0 is minimal; `tslc1` needs to change only with TSL |
| 12 | **DMA without IOMMU** undermines isolation from device or backend | Certain on virtio-mmio | Low in QEMU | Stated in T11; addressed at M12 |
| 13 | **`@tsl/alloc` has a safety bug.** Its safe API rests on unsafe code that the compiler doesn't check. | Medium | High | Keep it small, count it in S8, run its suite on every backend and under fuzz. |
| 14 | **Escape checking gives baffling errors or rejects reasonable code.** It's whole-program, so the cause can be several calls away. | Medium | Medium | Every error names the storing line and the call chain. Exercised from M3 by kernel code. |
| 15 | **Runaway test processes on the host.** This host panicked once during a heavy parallel test run (cause unproven). | Low | High for the owner | Guards in 8.2 |

### 12.2 The smallest versions worth building

| Level | Contains | Value alone | Stop if |
|-------|----------|------------|--------|
| **L0** | M1 and M2: TSL and down-lowering to Wasm | A static TS compiler usable on Moire's hot paths, with no warm-up and no GC pauses | G1 fails badly: TSL-to-Wasm alone is still a small, usable tool |
| **L1** | + M3 to M7: native backend and a memory-safe capability microkernel built on the Mac, booting with drivers in EL0 | **The honest "managed microkernel in TS".** A real research OS, with no boot-time compile. | G2 or G3 fails with no fix |
| **L2** | + M8, M9: self-hosted; compiles and caches in the guest | The owner's radical idea, without the seed | S10 fails: then L2 is only "self-hosted, reproducible" |
| **L3** | + M10: from-seed boot, a third DDC root | The full vision | |

**Recommendation:** L1 is the real target, and worth doing even if everything after it fails. Treat L2 and L3
as experiments with
written gates.

## Appendix A: Normative library surface

This compiles against stock `tsc` 5.9.3 (Appendix B). In the repo, implementations replace `declare`. tslc
treats these as built-ins and doesn't process their types.

```ts
// file: tsl-core.d.ts  -- module "@tsl/core"
declare const flavor: unique symbol;
export type Num<B extends string> = number & { readonly [flavor]?: B };
export type Int<B extends string> = Num<B>;
export type Big<B extends string> = bigint & { readonly [flavor]?: B };
// A flavour lists everything that widens to it, so u8 assigns to u32 and the reverse is a tsc error.
export type i8 = Num<"i8">;
export type i16 = Num<"i8" | "i16" | "u8">;
export type i32 = Num<"i8" | "i16" | "i32" | "u8" | "u16">;
export type isize = Num<"i8" | "i16" | "i32" | "isize" | "u8" | "u16" | "u32">;
export type u8 = Num<"u8">;
export type u16 = Num<"u8" | "u16">;
export type u32 = Num<"u8" | "u16" | "u32">;
export type usize = Num<"u8" | "u16" | "u32" | "usize">;
export type f32 = Num<"f32">;
export type f64 = Num<"f32" | "f64">;
export type i64 = Big<"i64">;
export type u64 = Big<"u64">;
export type bool = boolean;

// --- traps, conversions (to*: checked, wrap*: truncating), logging
export declare class TslTrap extends Error { readonly code: number; constructor(code: number); }
export declare function trap(code: u32): never;
export declare function assert(cond: bool, code: u32): void;
export declare function panic(msg: string): never;
export declare function log(msg: string): void;
export declare function toI8(x: number | bigint): i8;   export declare function wrapI8(x: number | bigint): i8;
export declare function toI16(x: number | bigint): i16; export declare function wrapI16(x: number | bigint): i16;
export declare function toI32(x: number | bigint): i32; export declare function wrapI32(x: number | bigint): i32;
export declare function toU8(x: number | bigint): u8;   export declare function wrapU8(x: number | bigint): u8;
export declare function toU16(x: number | bigint): u16; export declare function wrapU16(x: number | bigint): u16;
export declare function toU32(x: number | bigint): u32; export declare function wrapU32(x: number | bigint): u32;
export declare function toUsize(x: number | bigint): usize;
export declare function toU64(x: number | bigint): u64;
export declare function toI64(x: number | bigint): i64;
/** x + 0, so an integer -0 from V8 becomes +0 (3.3, rule 10). */
export declare function toF64(x: number): f64;
/** Host: exact for all ranges (uses BigInt when |a| >= 2^31). Traps on b = 0. MIN / -1 depends on T, which doesn't exist at run time, so only tslc and js-checked trap on it (3.10, item 1). */
export declare function idiv<T extends number>(a: T, b: T): T;
export declare function lit(s: string): Uint8Array;

// --- layout helpers: each name is a type above and a value here
export type Scalar<T> = (() => T) & { readonly desc: unknown };
export declare const u8: Scalar<u8>;    export declare const u16: Scalar<u16>;  export declare const u32: Scalar<u32>;  export declare const u64: Scalar<u64>;
export declare const i8: Scalar<i8>;    export declare const i16: Scalar<i16>;  export declare const i32: Scalar<i32>;  export declare const i64: Scalar<i64>;
export declare const f32: Scalar<f32>;  export declare const f64: Scalar<f64>;
export declare const be16: Scalar<u16>; export declare const be32: Scalar<u32>; export declare const be64: Scalar<u64>;
export declare function pad(size: number): never;
export declare function bits<const M extends Record<string, number>>(w: Scalar<number>, m: M): { -readonly [K in keyof M]: M[K] extends 1 ? boolean : number };
export declare function enumOf<E extends Record<string, string | number>>(w: Scalar<number>, e: E): E[keyof E];
export declare function enumValue<E extends Record<string, string | number>>(e: E, x: number): E[keyof E] | null;
export type ArrayOf<T> =
  [T] extends [u8] ? Uint8Array : [T] extends [u16] ? Uint16Array : [T] extends [u32] ? Uint32Array : [T] extends [u64] ? BigUint64Array
  : [T] extends [i32] ? Int32Array : [T] extends [f64] ? Float64Array : never;
export declare function array<T>(elem: Scalar<T>, length: number): ArrayOf<T>;
export interface LayoutArray<T> { readonly length: usize; at(i: usize): T }
export declare function nested<T>(cls: new () => T): T;
export declare function arrayOf<T>(cls: new () => T, length: number): LayoutArray<T>;
/** A plain class's last field: a variable-length array of scalars, sized by withTail (3.4, D69). */
export declare function tail<T>(elem: Scalar<T>): ArrayOf<T>;
/** An object of a class with a tail of n elements, zeroed, made on the heap at its real size. Takes a direct new. */
export declare function withTail<T extends object>(n: usize, made: T): T;

/** The writable scalar fields of T, for make() and set(). */
export type Init<T> = { [K in keyof T as T[K] extends number | bigint ? K : never]?: T[K] };
export declare function make<T extends object>(cls: new () => T, values?: Init<T>): T;
export declare function over<T extends object>(cls: new () => T, bytes: Uint8Array, offset: usize): T;
export declare function set<T extends object>(target: T, values: Init<T>): T;
export declare function sizeOf(cls: new () => object): usize;
export declare function alignOf(cls: new () => object): usize;
export declare function offsetOf<T extends object>(cls: new () => T, field: keyof T & string): usize;
export declare function assertSize(cls: new () => object, n: usize): void;

// --- arenas (Heap, Slab and Vec are library code: ex-heap.ts, ex-slab.ts, ex-vec.ts in 3.5, shipped as @tsl/alloc)
export interface Arena extends Disposable {
  bytes(n: usize): Uint8Array;
  u32s(n: usize): Uint32Array;
  make<T extends object>(cls: new () => T): T;
}
export declare function arenaOver(backing: Uint8Array): Arena;

// --- value results
export type Ok<T> = { readonly ok: true; readonly value: T };
export type Err<E> = { readonly ok: false; readonly error: E };
export type Result<T, E> = Ok<T> | Err<E>;

// --- MMIO descriptors
export type Access = "ro" | "wo" | "rw";
export type RegDesc<A extends Access, T> = { readonly offset: number; readonly access: A; readonly __value?: T };
export declare const reg: {
  ro8(offset: number): RegDesc<"ro", u8>; wo8(offset: number): RegDesc<"wo", u8>; rw8(offset: number): RegDesc<"rw", u8>;
  ro16(offset: number): RegDesc<"ro", u16>; wo16(offset: number): RegDesc<"wo", u16>; rw16(offset: number): RegDesc<"rw", u16>;
  ro32(offset: number): RegDesc<"ro", u32>; wo32(offset: number): RegDesc<"wo", u32>; rw32(offset: number): RegDesc<"rw", u32>;
  ro64(offset: number): RegDesc<"ro", u64>; wo64(offset: number): RegDesc<"wo", u64>; rw64(offset: number): RegDesc<"rw", u64>;
};
export type RegMap = { readonly [name: string]: RegDesc<Access, any> };
export type MmioDesc<R extends RegMap> = { readonly regs: R; readonly size: number };
export type RegHandle<A extends Access, T> = (A extends "wo" ? {} : { read(): T }) & (A extends "ro" ? {} : { write(v: T): void });
export type MmioRef<D> = D extends MmioDesc<infer R>
  ? { readonly [K in keyof R]: R[K] extends RegDesc<infer A, infer T> ? RegHandle<A, T> : never }
  : never;
export declare function mmio<const R extends RegMap>(size: number, regs: R): MmioDesc<R>;

// --- atomics
export type LoadOrder = "relaxed" | "acquire" | "seqcst";
export type StoreOrder = "relaxed" | "release" | "seqcst";
export type RmwOrder = "relaxed" | "acquire" | "release" | "acqrel" | "seqcst";
export declare const atomic: {
  load<R, K extends keyof R>(r: R, field: K, order: LoadOrder): R[K];
  store<R, K extends keyof R>(r: R, field: K, value: R[K], order: StoreOrder): void;
  fetchAdd<R, K extends keyof R>(r: R, field: K, value: R[K], order: RmwOrder): R[K];
  cas<R, K extends keyof R>(r: R, field: K, expected: R[K], desired: R[K], order: RmwOrder): bool;
  fence(order: RmwOrder): void;
};
```

// file: tsl-unsafe.d.ts  -- module "@tsl/unsafe"; importable only from modules listed in tsl.json
import type { ArrayOf, bool, MmioDesc, MmioRef, RegMap, u32, u64, usize } from "@tsl/core";

// Element descriptors are compile-time constants, so a field holding one takes no memory natively.
export type Elem<T> = { readonly size: usize; readonly align: usize; readonly __elem?: T };
export type ElemOf<T> = Elem<T> | ((() => T) & { readonly desc: unknown });
export declare function ref<T>(): Elem<T>;      // a stored reference: 8 bytes
export declare function inlineOf<T>(): Elem<T>; // an object in place: sizeOf(T) bytes, known to tslc
export declare function elemSize<T>(e: ElemOf<T>): usize;
export declare class Ptr<T> {
  readonly addr: u64;
  add(n: usize): Ptr<T>;
  read(): T;
  write(v: T): void;
  cast<U>(e: ElemOf<U>): Ptr<U>;
}
export declare function ptrAt<T>(e: ElemOf<T>, addr: u64): Ptr<T>;
export declare function sliceOf<T>(e: ElemOf<T>, addr: u64, n: usize): ArrayOf<T>;
export declare function copyBytes(dst: u64, src: u64, n: usize): void;
// A slot is [next free slot: u64][generation: u32][owner: u32][object]. These form and inspect generation-carrying references.
export declare function placeObject<T extends object>(slot: u64, gen: number, item: T): T;
/** placeObject for a class with a tail (D69): the moved object's fields, then n zeroed elements. */
export declare function placeTail<T extends object>(slot: u64, gen: number, n: usize, item: T): T;
/** The bytes an object of T with a tail of n elements takes. */
export declare function tailBytes<T>(e: ElemOf<T>, n: usize): usize;
/** The bytes an object takes, its tail's included. */
export declare function objectBytes(item: object): usize;
/** The address of an object's tail's element 0. */
export declare function tailAddr(item: object): u64;
export declare function objectAt<T extends object>(slot: u64): T;
/** Whether tslc's `rc` expansion places every count of T (3.5, D74, R1b): a constant natively, `false` on the host. */
export declare function countedExactly<T>(): boolean;
/** T's group in the type graph of classes (3.5, D41, R1c): a constant natively, 0 if T can't be in a cycle or the collector is off. */
export declare function cycleGroup<T>(): u32;
/** The same, for the host, which can't see T: read by class name from the table in `TSL_CYCLE_GROUPS`. Natively `item` isn't evaluated. */
export declare function cycleGroupOf<T extends object>(item: T): u32;
/** Whether any counted class can be in a cycle (3.5, D41, R1c): with none, `@tsl/gc`'s collector is never reached. */
export declare function cyclesLinked(): boolean;
/** A release function's number in the program's closed set, the functions named at `new Rc<T>(f)`, from 1 (3.5, D70, R1d). */
export declare function releaseIndex<F extends (item: never, at: usize, op: never) => usize>(f: F): u32;
/** Calls release function number i: a comparison with each number and a direct call, trap 18 for none (3.5, D70, R1d). */
export declare function callRelease<O>(i: u32, item: object, at: usize, op: O): usize;
export declare function slotOf(item: object): u64;
/** slotOf for a reference known live, `@tsl/gc`'s where `countedExactly<T>()` (3.5, D74, R1f): natively nothing is checked; on the host, slotOf. */
export declare function slotOfLive(item: object): u64;
export declare function genOf(item: object): number;
export declare function retireObject(item: object): void;
/** `"memory": "manual"` only (TSL5007). On the host it poisons the object; natively a use after it is a bug (3.10, 8). */
export declare function unsafeFree(item: object): void;
/** Takes a top-level function by name (TSL5009): zeroed runs of pages, or 0n when there are none. */
export declare function setPageSource(source: (pages: usize) => u64): void;
// Pages from the registered source, or 0n: @tsl/std's default allocator (3.5, D43).
export declare function sourcePages(pages: usize): u64;
// The per-call region (R6, 3.5, 4.5): where tslc places what no export call of a lowered `leak` or `manual` package
// outlives, given back as the export returns. Whether an object, or an address, is there: never on the host, nor in a
// package tslc placed nothing there. And bytes from it, not zeroed, for memory kept beside an object that is there (JsArray's
// buffer); never on the host.
export declare function inCallRegion(item: object): bool;
export declare function addrInCallRegion(addr: u64): bool;
export declare function callRegionBytes(bytes: usize): u64;
// What a Heap says about a run of whole pages given back: no code at all in a program with no @tsl/std.
export declare function pageRunFreed(addr: u64, pages: usize): void;
export declare function onPageRunFreed(hook: (addr: u64, pages: usize) => void): boolean;
// Traps 5 if x is a reference to something removed, and does nothing otherwise.
export declare function checkLive<T>(x: T): void;
// By the key's type: an integer's value, a class's own hashKey and sameKey, or identity. A float is TSL2003.
export declare function keyHash<K>(k: K): u32;
export declare function keySame<K>(a: K, b: K): bool;

export declare function viewAt<T extends object>(cls: new () => T, addr: u64): T;
export declare function staticView<T extends object>(cls: new () => T, align?: usize): T;
export declare function bytesAt(addr: u64, len: usize): Uint8Array;
export declare function addrOf(s: object): u64;
export declare function mmioAt<R extends RegMap>(d: MmioDesc<R>, base: u64): MmioRef<MmioDesc<R>>;
export declare function fnAddr(f: (...args: never[]) => unknown): u64;
export declare function asmFn<F extends (...args: never[]) => unknown>(body: TemplateStringsArray): F;
export declare function setLogSink(sink: (bytes: Uint8Array) => void): void;

`@tsl/std`'s surface is its five modules in 3.5, with what `index.ts` exports: `Vec`, `Map`, `ExactMap`, `Set`, `Slab`, `Str`, `StrBuilder`, `ref`, `globalAllocator` and `setHashKey`.

**Host simulation runtime.** `new T()` on a layout class is a plain zeroed object, and views (`over`,
`viewAt`) are objects with `T`'s prototype and accessors over a `DataView`, with arrays as real typed arrays,
so methods work on both.
`retireObject` and `unsafeFree` poison objects. `setPageSource` keeps its argument for `sourcePages`, and `leak` and `manual` don't ask, since a JS object needs no pages. `sourcePages` with nothing registered maps simulated regions as they're needed. `Ptr` works over simulated memory with a handle table for objects
(3.5). `@tsl/alloc` is the same source on every engine, so its behaviour can't vary between them. Host
`viewAt` and `bytesAt` read simulated memory regions in `kernel/sim`, `mmioAt` routes to a simulated device
registry by base address and records the access order for tests,
`fnAddr` hands out made-up stable addresses, and `asmFn` returns a stub replaced with `hostStub`. Intrinsics
in host mode record calls and are no-ops unless a test installs a handler. A scratch version of all this was
run; see Appendix B.

Strings, `Map` and `Set` have no import either: they're JavaScript's (4.5, D42). What's linked into a module that reaches them is ordinary lowered code from `compiler/rt`, and what's added to a native caller's surface is normative: `__str_place(len)`, `__str_units(p)`, `__str_length(p)`, `__hash_key_use(a, b)`, and the `make` and `put` exports `DownMeta` names per map type (4.5).

Ordinary TS under `rc` has no library of its own, and no new import: `WeakRef` is JavaScript's, and `.shift()`, `.splice()` and `.length =` are `Array`'s (4.5). What's linked is the counted heap, whose native surface is normative for a native caller (4.5): `__rc_new(size, desc)`, `__vec_new_rc(len, slot, desc)`, `__rc_retain(p)`, `__rc_release(p)`, `__rc_retain_arr(p)`, `__rc_release_arr(p)`, `__rc_collect()`, and `__page_source_use(code)` as for the other modes. The cycle collector (D41) adds nothing to it: `desc` is still what `DownMeta` gives, and `__rc_collect` includes cycles.

Exceptions and classes (D49, D50) add no import either: `Error`, `TypeError`, `RangeError`, `SyntaxError`, `ReferenceError`, `EvalError`, `URIError` and `SuppressedError` are JavaScript's, with `message`, `name`, `cause` and `toString()` as JS has them and `stack` as divergence 13, and what's linked is `compiler/rt/exc.ts`. A native caller's surface gains, in a module that can throw (4.5): `__exc_catch_use(on)`, `__exc_pending()`, `__exc_take()`, `__exc_stack_use(limit)`, and the describing function `DownMeta.exc.describe` names.

## Appendix B: Measured host facts

All on 2026-11-02, on the owner's machine, with throwaway probes in `/tmp`. Moire was only read.

**Machine:** Apple M1 Max, 10 CPUs, 64 GiB, macOS 27.0 (build 26A428). `kern.hv_support` = 1.

**Toolchain:**

| QEMU | `/opt/homebrew/bin/qemu-system-aarch64`, `qemu-img` | 10.1.2 | Accel: hvf, tcg. `virt` = virt-10.1. |
| Node | `/opt/homebrew/bin/node` | 25.8.1 | Strips types; `using` works. A `vite-plus` shim earlier on `PATH` gives 26.13.0, and all TSL tests below passed on both. |

**Stock tsc 5.9.3 tests, using this spec's flags:**

- Flavoured lattice: literals, arithmetic and lossless widening assign. `u32`→`u8`, `i32`→`u32`, `u32`→`i32`
  and `u64`→`u32` are all rejected.
  `getTypeAtLocation` returns `aliasSymbol.name` for annotated declarations, including with widening flavours.
- Negative: write to `ro`, read from `wo` (version 1), and against the Appendix A surface: number to u64
  field, bigint to u32 field, unknown field, unknown `bits` flag, bad `make` value, `make` on a non-scalar,
  bad `offsetOf` name, narrowing, sign changes, wrong slab element, an unset plain-class field: all rejected.
- This spec's code blocks marked `// file:` compile together, using the flags in 9.2, with `@tsl/*` mapped to
  the blocks in Appendix A.
  They were extracted from this file and checked, 2026-11-03. Only type-correctness and host behaviour were
  checked, not tslc's own rules, as tslc doesn't exist yet.

**Language probes, 2026-11-03, with a throwaway host runtime, run on Node 25.8.1 and 26.13.0 through the load
hook, and on Bun 1.3.11:** the extracted examples passed a test of 68 checks with identical results: exact
bytes for `VirtqDesc` and its `bits`, sizes and offsets, typed-array fields, methods on views and on plain
objects, overlay traps, MMIO over a simulated bus, closures, arena exhaustion, `decode`, `enumOf` traps,
`asmFn` stubs, `viewAt`, and `addrOf`. The `@tsl/alloc` code in 3.5 ran as written over simulated pages: heap
block reuse, `Vec` growth to 1,000 elements, references held in a `Vec` across growth through the host handle
table, borrow, use-after-free and double-free traps, slab growth and slot reuse, stale stored references,
generation exhaustion at 16 bits, and out-of-memory as a normal result. None of it has been compiled natively,
so the 48-bit tagged reference, slot prefix and `inlineOf` sizes are design only.

- Node strip mode rejects `enum` and parameter properties in both versions. `--experimental-transform-types`
  works on 25.8.1 and is a bad option on 26.13.0. Bun runs both directly.
- Tuple-form structs: `tsc` computes sizes and offsets at type level and rejects wrong ones, up to 9,992 bytes
  tested, failing with TS2800 at 10,000.
- A base class with plain-typed layout fields (`class T extends Base { len: u32; }`): runs, but only with the
  host parsing source. `new T().len` is `undefined`, since a stripped `len;` runs after the base constructor.
  Also, `extends` here inherits nothing real. Rejected as D25.
- `tsc` accepts assigning a discriminated union to `{ kind: string }` and writing its tag, despite `readonly`,
  and accepts `as` from `JSON.parse`. On Node, both read wrong values (D26).

**QEMU probes under `-M virt,gic-version=3`:**

| Fact | HVF (`-cpu host`) | TCG (`-cpu max`) |
|------|------------------|-----------------|
| Boot EL | EL1 | EL1 |
| Image-header load address | `0x40200000` | `0x40200000` |
| `x0` (Image form, 256 MiB) | `0x48000000`, DTB magic OK | Same |
| `x0` (ELF form) | 0 | Not run |
| Timer frequency | 24 MHz | 1 GHz |
| GICv3 and virtual-timer IRQ | Works, INTID 27 | Works, INTID 27 |
| `PFR0.GIC` field | 0 (misleading) | Non-zero in the raw value |
| `PFR0` raw | `0x1101000010110011` | `0x1301001121110022` |
| `PFR1` raw (BT, SSBS, MTE) | `0x0` | `0x0000001002000121` |
| `ISAR0` raw | `0x0221100110212120` | `0x1221111110212120` |
| `ISAR1` raw | `0x0000011110211202` | `0x0111211110211502` |
| `MMFR0` raw | `0x000010000f100002` (40-bit PA, 8-bit ASID) | `0x2100032310201126` |
| `MMFR1` raw | `0x0000000011212000` | `0x0110112010312122` |
| QEMU start to PSCI off, trivial probe | 72 to 80 ms | 72 to 80 ms |
| **EL0 `svc` + EL1 `eret` round trip, MMU and caches on** | **27.2 to 27.4 ns** (3 runs) | 729 to 750 ns |
| `PMCCNTR` over a 100k-iteration loop | 38,000 to 42,000, round thousands | 127,000 to 133,000, round thousands |

Other:

- macOS sysctl: `FEAT_LSE`, `FEAT_SHA256`, `FEAT_SB`, `FEAT_PAuth`, `FEAT_CSV2`, `FEAT_CSV3`, `FEAT_SSBS`,
  `FEAT_DPB`, `FEAT_DPB2` = 1. `FEAT_BTI`, `FEAT_MTE`, `FEAT_ECV`, `FEAT_PAuth2` = 0.
- virtio-mmio: 32 slots from `0x0a000000`, stride `0x200`, first `-device` at the top slot. Magic
  `0x74726976`. Version 1 by default, 2 with `force-legacy=false`. Device ID 2 for blk, 4 for rng.
- DTB: `pl011@9000000` (SPI 1), `intc@8000000` (`GICD 0x8000000+0x10000`, `GICR 0x80a0000+0xf60000`),
  `its@8080000`, `memory@40000000`, `pcie@10000000`, `pl031@9010000`, `fw-cfg@9020000`, PSCI `method = "hvc"`.
  Timer PPIs: 13, 14, 11, 10. `/chosen` has per-boot random `rng-seed` and `kaslr-seed`: two identical QEMU
  runs produced different DTB hashes.

**Native probes, 2026-11-03:** a TIR image boots, prints and powers off in about 35 ms from QEMU start, on HVF and on TCG, with MMU and caches on.
Against 20,000 random arguments, plain fdlibm `sin` differed from V8's in 325 places and fdlibm with fused multiplies in none. Over 2,000 random
arguments each, V8 and JSC differed on `sin` 87 times, `cos` 112, `log` 136, `exp` 198, `atan2` 201, and `pow` not at all, since both use the host's.

**JPEG decoder baseline, one run on a busy host, so rough:** see M2's table. After 200 warm-up decodes, median
of 101. Cold first decode of `tower-portrait.jpg`: 18.19 ms V8, 20.25 ms JSC. JSC's steady state was around
30% faster than V8's on this decoder, which is why JSC is reported too.

**`typescript@5.9.3` size:** `lib/typescript.js` 200,276 lines, 9,112,572 bytes. `lib/_tsc.js` 133,818 lines.
